Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 24, verse 1:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿A surah which We have sent down and made obligatory, and in which We have sent down clear verses that you may remember.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His saying, exalted is He, ﴿A surah which We have sent down﴾, it means: This surah, which We have sent down. We have said that this is its meaning because the Arabs hardly begin with indefinite nouns before their predicates unless it is in response (to a question), since such nouns are connected the way the relative pronoun (alladhi) is connected, and then a predicate other than the connecting clause is stated about them. Thus it is considered objectionable to begin with them before the predicate when they are not connected, since when they are begun with, their predicate becomes like a connecting clause for them, and the listener becomes like one awaiting their predicate, given that the predicate about them comes after them, like the connecting clause for them. But when the predicate about them is begun before them, doubt does not enter the listener's mind regarding the speaker's intended meaning. We have already explained earlier that "surah" is a description of something elevated by its evidences, so this makes repeating it in this place unnecessary.

As for His saying, ﴿and made obligatory﴾, the reciters differed in its recitation. Some reciters of Hijaz and Basra recited it as "wa faradnaha" (with the letter ra lightened), and they interpret it as: We have explained it, and We have sent down in it various obligations. Mujahid also recited it this way and interpreted it accordingly.

⁕ My paternal uncle Ahmad ibn Yusuf narrated to me, saying: al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Ibn Mahdi narrated to us, from Abd al-Warith ibn Sa'id, from Humayd, from Mujahid, that he used to recite it: "wa farradnaha" (with the letter ra doubled), meaning with the shaddah.

⁕ Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us, and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: "wa farradnaha", he said: The command to what is lawful and the prohibition of what is unlawful.

⁕ al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, the like of it. This (meaning) may be admitted when it is recited with the shaddah, in a sense other than what we have mentioned from Mujahid, namely that its meaning is: We have made it obligatory upon you and upon those who come after you of mankind until the Hour. The majority of reciters of Medina, Kufa and Syria recited ﴿wa faradnaha﴾ with the letter ra lightened, meaning: We have made obligatory upon you the rulings contained in it, required them of you, and clarified that for you.

The correct view on this matter is that both are well-known recitations, and scholars among the reciters have recited each of them, so whichever one the reciter reads is correct. This is because God has explained it, sent down in it various kinds of rulings, commanded and prohibited in it, and imposed upon His servants obligations within it. Thus both meanings are present in it: the making obligatory (tafrid) and the obligation (fard). For this reason we say that whichever of the two recitations the reciter reads, he is correct in what is right.

Mention of those who interpreted it in the sense of obligation and clarification from among the people of interpretation.

⁕ Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿and made obligatory﴾, he said: means: We have made it clear.

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿A surah which We have sent down and made obligatory﴾, he said: We made it obligatory for this one who recites it, of what is obligated in it, and he recited in it: ﴿clear verses that you may remember﴾.

* *

And His saying: ﴿And in it We have sent down clear verses﴾

He, exalted is He, says: And We have sent down in this surah signs and evidences of the truth, clear, meaning evident to whoever contemplates them and reflects upon them with intellect, that they are from God, for they are the manifest truth, and they guide to the straight path.

⁕ al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj: ﴿And in it We have sent down clear verses﴾, he said: the lawful and the unlawful and the prescribed penalties. ﴿that you may remember﴾ means: that you may take heed through these clear verses which We have sent down.

The Interpretation of the Words of God, the Exalted: ﴿The adulterer and the adulteress: flog each one of them with a hundred lashes. Let not compassion for them detain you in the religion of God, if you believe in God and the Last Day. And let a group of the believers witness their punishment.﴾ (2)

God, He is exalted in remembrance, says: Whoever among men commits adultery, or whoever among women does, being free, a virgin, and not muhsan (protected) by a spouse, then flog him or her a hundred lashes as a punishment for what they did and for the disobedience of God they committed. ﴿And let not compassion for them detain you in the religion of God﴾: God, He is exalted in remembrance, says: Do not let compassion for the adulterer and the adulteress, O believers, detain you; ra'fah (compassion) is the softness of mercy. ﴿In the religion of God﴾ means in obedience to God, regarding what He has commanded you concerning carrying out the hadd (prescribed punishment) upon them, as He has obligated you.

The people of ta'wil (interpretation) differed regarding what the believers are forbidden from, namely taking compassion upon them. Some said: it is abandoning the carrying out of God's hadd upon them. As for when the hadd has been carried out upon them, then compassion has not taken hold of you regarding them in the religion of God.

Those who said that:

– Abu Hisham narrated to us, he said: Yahya ibn Abi Za'idah narrated to us, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, from Ibn Abi Mulaykah, from 'Ubayd Allah ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar, who said: Ibn 'Umar flogged a slave-girl of his who had committed an offence; he flogged her legs. Nafi' said: and I think he said: and her back. I said: ﴿And let not compassion for them detain you in the religion of God﴾. He said: Has compassion taken hold of you concerning her? God did not command me to kill her.

– Ya'qub narrated to us, he said: Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: I heard 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Mulaykah say: 'Ubayd Allah ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar told me that 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar punished a slave-girl of his, and he said to the executioner, pointing to her leg and to her lower part: I said: Then where is the words of God: ﴿And let not compassion for them detain you in the religion of God﴾? He said: Shall I kill her?

– Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, he said: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, he said: Sufyan narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿And let not compassion for them detain you in the religion of God﴾, he said: that you carry out the hadd.

– Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, regarding ﴿And let not compassion for them detain you in the religion of God﴾, he said: Do not neglect the hudud of God.

Ibn Jurayj said: Mujahid said: ﴿And let not compassion for them detain you﴾: do not neglect the hudud by refraining from carrying them out. 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah also said this.

– Abu Hisham narrated to us, he said: 'Abd al-Malik and Hajjaj narrated to us, from 'Ata': ﴿And let not compassion for them detain you in the religion of God﴾, he said: The hadd of God is carried out and not suspended, and it is not killing.

– Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Fudayl narrated to me, from Dawud, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: It is the flogging.

– 'Ubayd ibn Isma'il al-Habbari narrated to me, he said: Muhammad ibn Fudayl narrated to us, from al-Mughirah, from Ibrahim, regarding His words: ﴿And let not compassion for them detain you in the religion of God﴾, he said: The striking.

– Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, he said: al-Mu'tamir narrated to us, he said: I heard 'Imran say: I said to Abu Mijlaz: ﴿The adulterer and the adulteress: flog each one of them﴾ ... up to His words: ﴿and the Last Day﴾. We truly have mercy on them, that a man be flogged as a hadd, or that his hand be cut off. He said: That is only because it is not for the ruler, when they are brought to him, to leave them out of mercy for them until he carries out the hadd.

– al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, he said: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, he said: al-Thawri informed us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿And let not compassion for them detain you in the religion of God﴾, he said: The hudud are not to be carried out.

– Yunus narrated to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words: ﴿And let not compassion for them detain you﴾: that you leave them from the hudud of God which He commanded and made obligatory upon them.

He said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Lahi'ah informed us, from Khalid ibn Abi 'Imran, that he asked Sulayman ibn Yasar about the words of God: ﴿And let not compassion for them detain you in the religion of God﴾: is that in the hudud or in the punishment? He said: That applies to both of them together.

– 'Amr ibn 'Abd al-Hamid al-Amili narrated to us, he said: Yahya ibn Zakariyya narrated to us, from 'Abd al-Malik ibn Abi Sulayman, from 'Ata', regarding His words: ﴿And let not compassion for them detain you in the religion of God﴾, he said: That the hadd of God is carried out and not suspended, and it is not killing.

– Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Jarir narrated to us, from 'Ata', from 'Amir, regarding His words: ﴿And let not compassion for them detain you in the religion of God﴾, he said: The severe striking.

Others said: rather, the meaning of it is: ﴿And let not compassion for them detain you﴾, so that you lighten the striking upon them, but strike them painfully.

Those who said that:

– Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, he said: Yahya ibn Abi Bakr narrated to us, he said: Abu Ja'far narrated to us, from Qatadah, from al-Hasan and Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib: ﴿And let not compassion for them detain you in the religion of God﴾, he said: The severe flogging.

– He said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, from Shu'bah, from Hammad, who said: The slanderer and the drinker are punished with their garments on them. As for the adulterer, his garments are removed. He recited this verse: ﴿And let not compassion for them detain you in the religion of God﴾. I said to Hammad: Is this regarding the judgment? He said: Regarding the judgment and the flogging.

– al-Hasan narrated to us, he said: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, he said: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: One exerts oneself in the hadd of the adulterer and the slanderer, and lightens it in the hadd of the drinker. Qatadah said: He lightens it for the drinker and exerts himself for the adulterer.

The more correct of the two opinions regarding this, in the view of truth, is the opinion of the one who said: the meaning of it is: ﴿And let not compassion for them detain you in carrying out God's hadd upon them, which He has obligated you to carry out upon them.﴾

We said that this is the more correct of the two interpretations because of God's words after it: "in the religion of God", meaning in the obedience of God which He commanded you. It is known that the religion of God which He commanded regarding the two adulterers is carrying out the hadd upon them, as commanded, a hundred lashes on each of them, while the severity of striking has no limit that can be fixed, and every strike that causes pain is severe, and there is no limit to what is painful in severity that could be commanded. It is impermissible to describe Him, majestic is His praise, as commanding what the one commanded has no way to know. Since that is so, what the commanded can know the way to is the number of lashes as He commanded, and that is carrying out the hadd as we have said. The Arabs have two forms for ra'fah: ra'fah with the hamzah unvocalized, and ra'afah with its madd, like al-sa'mah and al-sa'amah, and al-ka'bah and al-ka'abah. It is as if ra'fah is the single instance and ra'afah is the verbal noun, as it is said: đu'ul, du'alah, like fa'ul, fa'alah, and qabuha, qabahah.

* *

His words: ﴿If you believe in God and the Last Day﴾

He says: if you affirm God your Lord and the Last Day, and that you will be resurrected in it for the gathering of the Resurrection, and for reward and punishment, then whoever is affirming of that does not oppose God in His command and His prohibition, out of fear of His punishment for His disobediences.

* *

His words: ﴿And let a group of the believers witness their punishment﴾

God, He is exalted in remembrance, says: Let a group of the believers be present at the flogging of the two virgin adulterers and their hadd when it is carried out upon them. The Arabs call one and what exceeds it a ṭā'ifah. ﴿Of the believers﴾ means: of the people of faith in God and His Messenger.

The people of ta'wil differed regarding the minimum number of the ṭā'ifah whose presence at the punishment of the two virgin adulterers God commanded. Some said: its minimum is one.

Those who said that:

– Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, he said: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, he said: Sufyan narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said: The ṭā'ifah: a man.

– 'Ali ibn Sahl ibn Musa ibn Ishaq al-Kinani and Ibn al-Qawwas narrated to us, both said: Yahya ibn 'Isa narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding the words of God: ﴿And let a group of the believers witness their punishment﴾, he said: The ṭā'ifah is a man. 'Ali said: and what is above that; and Ibn al-Qawwas said: and more than that.

– 'Ali narrated to us, he said: Zayd narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said: The ṭā'ifah: a man.

– Ya'qub narrated to us, he said: Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, he said: Ibn Abi Najih said: ﴿And let a group of the believers witness their punishment﴾. Mujahid said: its minimum is a man.

– Ya'qub narrated to me, he said: Hushaym narrated to us, he said: Abu Bishr informed us, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿And let a group of the believers witness their punishment﴾, he said: The ṭā'ifah: from one to a thousand.

– Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, he said: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Abu Bishr, from Mujahid regarding this verse: ﴿And let a group of the believers witness their punishment﴾, he said: The ṭā'ifah is one to a thousand. And: ﴿If two groups of the believers fight, then make peace between them﴾.

– Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, he said: Wahb ibn Jarir narrated to me, he said: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Abu Bishr, from Mujahid, who said: The ṭā'ifah: a single man up to a thousand. He said: ﴿And if two groups of the believers fight, then make peace between them﴾: they were only two men.

– al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: I heard 'Isa ibn Yunus say: al-Nu'man ibn Thabit narrated to us, from Hammad and Ibrahim, who both said: The ṭā'ifah: a man.

– al-Hasan narrated to us, he said: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, he said: al-Thawri informed us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿And let a group of the believers witness their punishment﴾, he said: The ṭā'ifah: one man or more.

Others said: its minimum in this place is two men.

Those who said that:

– Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, he said: Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, he said: Ibn Abi Najih narrated to us, regarding His words: ﴿And let a group of the believers witness their punishment﴾, he said: 'Ata' said: its minimum is two men.

– al-Qasim narrated to me, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: 'Umar ibn 'Ata' informed me, from 'Ikrimah, who said: Let two men or more be present.

Others said: its minimum is three or more.

Those who said that:

– al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: 'Isa ibn Yunus narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Dhi'b, from al-Zuhri, who said: The ṭā'ifah: three or more.

– Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding His words: ﴿And let a group of the believers witness their punishment﴾, he said: A group of the Muslims.

– al-Hasan narrated to us, he said: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, he said: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, the like of it.

– Abu al-Sa'ib narrated to me, he said: Hafs ibn Ghiyath narrated to us, he said: al-Ash'ath narrated to us, from his father, who said: I came to Abu Barzah al-Aslami on some business, and he had brought out a slave-girl to the door of the house, and she had committed adultery. He called a man and said: Strike her fifty! He called a group of people, then recited: ﴿And let a group of the believers witness their punishment﴾.

– Abu Hisham al-Rifa'i narrated to us, he said: Yahya narrated to us, from al-Ash'ath, from his father, that Abu Barzah ordered his son to strike a slave-girl of his who had given birth from fornication, a striking not severe. He said: He threw a garment over her, and people were with him, and he recited: ﴿And let a group of the believers witness their punishment﴾ ... the verse.

Others said: rather, its minimum is four.

Those who said that:

– Yunus narrated to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words: ﴿And let a group of the believers witness their punishment﴾, he said: The ṭā'ifah by which the hadd becomes obligatory is four.

The most correct of the sayings regarding this, in the view of truth, is the saying of the one who said: the least that should attend that from the number of Muslims is one or more; this is because God generalized with His words: ﴿And let a group witness their punishment﴾, and the ṭā'ifah among the Arabs may fall upon one or more.

Since that is so, and God, He is exalted in remembrance, did not establish any indication that His intent from it is a specific number, it is known that the presence at that place of what the lowest name of ṭā'ifah falls upon exempts the one carrying out the hadd from what God commanded him with His words: ﴿And let a group of the believers witness their punishment﴾. However, although the matter is as I have described, I prefer that the number of those present at that place not fall short of four persons, the number of those whose testimony is accepted for adultery; because when that is the case, there is no disagreement among the group that the one carrying out the hadd has discharged what is upon him in that regard, whereas regarding fewer than that they differ.

**Commentary on the words of God Most High: ﴿The fornicator marries none but a fornicatress or an idolatress, and the fornicatress is married by none but a fornicator or an idolater; and that is forbidden to the believers.﴾ (3)**

The exegetes (ahl al-ta'wil) differed in their interpretation of this. Some of them said: This verse was revealed concerning some men who asked the Messenger of God ﷺ for permission to marry women who were known for fornication among the idolaters, who were owners of banners (ashab rayat), who hired out themselves. So God revealed their prohibition to the believers, saying: The fornicator among the believers marries none but a fornicatress or an idolatress, because they are such; and the fornicatress among those prostitutes is married by none but a fornicator from among the believers or the idolaters, or an idolater like her, because they were idolaters.

﴿And that is forbidden to the believers﴾: According to the proponents of this view, God forbade their marriage by this verse.

Mention of those who said this:

Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: al-Mu'tamir narrated to us, from his father, who said: al-Hadrami narrated to me, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr: that a man from among the Muslims asked the Prophet of God for permission regarding a woman called Umm Mahzul, who used to fornicate with a man and stipulate that he should spend on her, and that he asked the Prophet ﷺ for permission regarding her and mentioned her affair to him. He said: The Prophet of God ﷺ recited: ﴿And the fornicatress is married by none but a fornicator or an idolater﴾, or he said: ﴿The fornicatress﴾ was revealed.

Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to me, from al-Taymi, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr, concerning His saying: ﴿The fornicator marries none but a fornicatress or an idolatress, and the fornicatress is married by none but a fornicator or an idolater﴾. He said: They were women known (by name). He said: A man from the poor Muslims would marry one of them so that she would spend on him, and God forbade them from that.

He said: Sulayman al-Taymi informed us, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, who said: They were women who were hired out (mawarid) in Medina.

Ahmad ibn al-Miqdam narrated to us, saying: al-Mu'tamir narrated to us, saying: I heard my father say: Qatada narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib concerning this verse: ﴿And the fornicatress is married by none but a fornicator or an idolater﴾. He said: It was revealed concerning women hired out (mawarid) who were in Medina.

Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: 'Amr ibn 'Asim al-Kilabi narrated to us, saying: Mu'tamir narrated to us, from his father, from Qatada, from Sa'id, similarly.

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Dawud narrated to us, from a man, from 'Amr ibn Sa'id, who said: Mirthad had a female companion in the Jahiliyyah called 'Anaq, and he was a strong man, and he was called Dildil. He used to go to Mecca and carry the weak Muslims to the Messenger of God ﷺ. He met his female companion, and she invited him to herself. He said: Indeed God has forbidden fornication. She said: Then how will you be seen? He feared that she would spread word about him, so he returned to Medina and came to the Messenger of God ﷺ and said: O Messenger of God, I had a female companion in the Jahiliyyah; do you think I may marry her? He said: So God revealed: ﴿The fornicator marries none but a fornicatress or an idolatress, and the fornicatress is married by none but a fornicator or an idolater﴾. He said: They were women known (by name), who were called "al-Qaylaqiyyat".[[This word is thus given in the manuscripts. Its original form is probably "al-Qalaqiyyat", attributed to al-qalaq, which is a type of necklace strung with pearls that they wore, enticing men with it; or attributed to al-qalaq because of their great agitation and movement. (See al-Taj: q-l-q.)]]

Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'ba narrated to us, from Ibrahim ibn Muhajir, who said: I heard Mujahid say concerning this verse: ﴿The fornicator marries none but a fornicatress or an idolatress﴾: They were prostitutes in the Jahiliyyah.

Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, from 'Abd al-Malik, from one who informed him, from Mujahid, nearly similar to the narration of Ibn al-Muthanna, except that he said: One of them was a woman called Umm Mahzul; meaning in His saying: ﴿The fornicator marries none but a fornicatress or an idolatress﴾. He said: They were women known (by name). He said: A man from the poor Muslims would marry one of them so that she would spend on him, and God forbade them from that. This is in the narration of al-Taymi.

Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning the word of God: ﴿The fornicator marries none but a fornicatress﴾. He said: Men who wanted to commit fornication with fornicating women, prostitutes known (for it), who were in the Jahiliyyah; it was said to them: This is forbidden. So they wanted to marry them, and God forbade their marriage to them.

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid, similarly, except that he said: Openly known prostitutes; they were such in the Jahiliyyah.

Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Hisham ibn 'Urwa, from his father, and Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, from al-Sha'bi, and Ibn Abi Dhi'b, from Shu'ba, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: They were prostitutes in the Jahiliyyah; at their doors were banners like the banners of the farriers, by which they were recognised.

Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us, from Qays ibn Sa'd, from 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Prostitutes known (by name); God forbade their marriage: none marries them but a fornicator from among the believers, or an idolater from among the idolaters.

Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His word: ﴿The fornicator marries none but a fornicatress or an idolatress, and the fornicatress is married by none but a fornicator or an idolater, and that is forbidden to the believers﴾. He said: In the Jahiliyyah there were houses called "al-mawakhir", and they used to hire out their young women there. These were houses known for fornication; no one entered them or came to them except a fornicator from among the People of the Qibla or an idolater from among the people of idols. So God forbade that to the believers.

Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayya narrated to us, from Ibn Juraij, from 'Ata', concerning His word: ﴿The fornicator marries none but a fornicatress or an idolatress, and the fornicatress is married by none but a fornicator or an idolater﴾. He said: They were known prostitutes in the Jahiliyyah: the prostitute of the family of so-and-so, and the prostitute of the family of so-and-so. So God revealed: ﴿The fornicator marries none but a fornicatress or an idolatress, and the fornicatress is married by none but a fornicator or an idolater, and that is forbidden to the believers﴾. Thus God judged, from the matter of the Jahiliyyah, by this in Islam. Sulayman ibn Musa said to him: Has this been related to you from Ibn 'Abbas? He said: Yes.

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, who said: I heard 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah say concerning that: They were known prostitutes, the prostitute of the family of so-and-so and the prostitute of the family of so-and-so, and they were idolatrous fornicatresses. He said: ﴿The fornicator marries none but a fornicatress or an idolatress, and the fornicatress is married by none but a fornicator or an idolater, and that is forbidden to the believers﴾. He said: God judged by this from the matter of the Jahiliyyah. It was said to him: Has this been related to you from Ibn 'Abbas? He said: Yes.

Ibn Juraij said: 'Ikrima said: He used to name nine, after the women of the banners, though they were more than that. But these were the owners of banners: Umm Mahzul, slave-girl of al-Sa'ib ibn Abi al-Sa'ib al-Makhzumi; Umm 'Ulayt, slave-girl of Safwan ibn Umayya; Hunna the Copt, slave-girl of al-'Asi ibn Wa'il; Mariyya, slave-girl of Malik ibn 'Umayla ibn al-Sabbaq ibn 'Abd al-Dar; Halala, slave-girl of Suhayl ibn 'Amr; Umm Suwayd, slave-girl of 'Amr ibn 'Uthman al-Makhzumi; Surayfa, slave-girl of Zam'a ibn al-Aswad; Farisa, slave-girl of Hisham ibn Rabi'a ibn Habib ibn Hudhayfa ibn Jabal ibn Malik ibn 'Amir ibn Lu'ayy; and Qurayba, slave-girl of Hilal ibn Anas ibn Jabir ibn Namir ibn Ghalib ibn Fihr.

Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid; and al-Zuhri and Qatada said: In the Jahiliyyah there were prostitutes known for this among them; some people among the Muslims wanted to marry them, so God revealed: ﴿The fornicator marries none but a fornicatress or an idolatress, and the fornicatress is married by none but a fornicator or an idolater﴾ ... the verse.

Al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid; and al-Zuhri and Qatada said: They were prostitutes in the Jahiliyyah; then he mentioned something similar.

Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Ibn Abi Najih, from al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazza: A man would marry a fornicatress in the Jahiliyyah whose fornication was known, taking her as a source of food. Some Muslims wanted to marry them in that manner, so they were forbidden from that.

Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Ibn Abi Najih, who said: al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazza said, and he mentioned something similar.

Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: Sulayman al-Taymi informed us, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, who said: They were women hired out (mawarid) in Medina.

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Idris narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Malik ibn Abi Sulayman informed us, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr: that women in the Jahiliyyah used to hire out themselves, and a man would marry one of them only wanting to obtain some goods from her; so they were forbidden from that, and this was revealed: ﴿The fornicator marries none but a fornicatress or an idolatress, and the fornicatress is married by none but a fornicator or an idolater﴾, and among them was a woman called Umm Mahzul.

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Jabir ibn Nuh narrated to us, from Isma'il, from al-Sha'bi, concerning His word: ﴿The fornicator marries none but a fornicatress or an idolatress, and the fornicatress is married by none but a fornicator or an idolater﴾. He said: They were women who hired out themselves in the Jahiliyyah.

Others said: The meaning of that is: The fornicator fornicates only with a fornicatress or an idolatress, and the fornicatress is fornicated with only by a fornicator or an idolater. They said: The meaning of "marriage" (nikah) in this place is intercourse (jima').

Mention of those who said this:

Hannad narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Ahwas narrated to us, from Husayn, from 'Ikrima, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning the word of God: ﴿The fornicator marries none but a fornicatress or an idolatress﴾. He said: He does not fornicate except with a fornicatress or an idolatress.

Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'ba narrated to us, from Ya'la ibn Muslim, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, that he said concerning this verse: ﴿And the fornicatress is married by none but a fornicator or an idolater﴾. He said: The fornicator does not fornicate except with a fornicatress like himself or an idolatress.

Al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Ibn Shubruma, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr and 'Ikrima, concerning His word: ﴿The fornicator marries none but a fornicatress or an idolatress﴾. The two of them said: It is the copulation (wat').

Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad narrated to us, from Ma'mar, who said: Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Mujahid said: ﴿The fornicator marries none but a fornicatress or an idolatress﴾. The two of them said: It is the copulation.

Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Salama ibn Nubayt, from al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim and Shu'ba, from Ya'la ibn Muslim, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, concerning His word: ﴿The fornicator marries none but a fornicatress or an idolatress, and the fornicatress is married by none but a fornicator or an idolater﴾. The two of them said: The fornicator, when he fornicates, does not fornicate except with a fornicatress like himself or an idolatress, and an idolatress does not fornicate except with her like.

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning God's word: ﴿The fornicator marries none but a fornicatress or an idolatress, and the fornicatress is married by none but a fornicator or an idolater﴾: These were prostitutes who were in the Jahiliyyah. And "marriage" in the Book of God means reaching (al-isaba) her: none reaches her except a fornicator or an idolater; it does not forbid fornication, and she reaches none but her like.

He said: Ibn 'Abbas used to say: They were prostitutes who were in the Jahiliyyah.

Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Qays ibn Sa'd, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: If he has fornicated with her, then he is a fornicator.

'Ali narrated to us, saying: 'Abd Allah narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to us, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His word: ﴿The fornicator marries none but a fornicatress or an idolatress﴾. He said: The fornicator from among the People of the Qibla does not fornicate except with a fornicatress like himself or an idolatress. He said: And the fornicatress from among the People of the Qibla does not fornicate except with a fornicator like her from among the People of the Qibla, or an idolater from outside the People of the Qibla. Then he said: ﴿And that is forbidden to the believers﴾.

Others said: This was God's judgment regarding every fornicator and fornicatress, until He abrogated it by His word: ﴿And marry off the single among you﴾, so He permitted the marriage of every Muslim woman and the marrying-off of every Muslim man.

Mention of those who said this:

Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, from Yahya ibn Sa'id, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, concerning His word: ﴿The fornicator marries none but a fornicatress or an idolatress, and the fornicatress is married by none but a fornicator or an idolater, and that is forbidden to the believers﴾. He said: They considered the verse that follows it to have abrogated it: ﴿And marry off the single among you﴾. He said: So they are from among the single women of the Muslims.

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, who said: Yahya ibn Sa'id informed me, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib: ﴿The fornicator marries none but a fornicatress or an idolatress, and the fornicatress is married by none but a fornicator or an idolater﴾. He said: The following verse abrogated it: ﴿And marry off the single among you﴾, and he said: They are from among the single women of the Muslims.

Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, who said: It was mentioned from Yahya, from Ibn al-Musayyib, who said: It abrogated it: ﴿And marry off the single among you﴾.

Al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Yahya ibn Sa'id, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, who said: His word ﴿And marry off the single﴾ abrogated it.

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Anas ibn 'Iyad informed us, from Yahya, who said: It was mentioned in the presence of Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib: ﴿The fornicator marries none but a fornicatress or an idolatress﴾. He said: I heard him say: Indeed the verse that follows it has abrogated it. Then Sa'id recited it: ﴿The fornicator marries none but a fornicatress or an idolatress﴾, then God says: ﴿And marry off the single among you﴾, so they are from among the single women of the Muslims.

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of the opinions in my view concerning this is the opinion of the one who said: By marriage in this place is meant copulation, and that the verse was revealed concerning the idolatrous prostitutes who owned banners. This is because of the established proof that a Muslim woman who is a fornicatress is forbidden to every idolater, and that a Muslim man who is a fornicator is forbidden to every idolatrous woman who worships idols. Since this is known to be so, it is clear that the verse did not intend that a fornicator among the believers may not contract a marriage contract with a chaste Muslim woman, and may marry only a fornicatress or an idolatress. And since this is so, it becomes clear that the meaning of the verse is: The fornicator fornicates only with a fornicatress who does not regard fornication as lawful, or with an idolatress who regards it as lawful.

* *

As for His word: ﴿And that is forbidden to the believers﴾:

He says: And fornication is forbidden to the believers in God and His Messenger; and that is the marriage of which He, may His praise be great, said: ﴿The fornicator marries none but a fornicatress﴾.

**The interpretation of His words, the Exalted: ﴿And those who accuse chaste women and then do not produce four witnesses, lash them eighty lashes, and do not accept their testimony ever after. Those are the defiantly disobedient﴾ (4)**

He, the Exalted, says: those who slander chaste women among the free believing women and accuse them of fornication, and then do not produce four upright witnesses who testify that they saw those women committing it, then lash those who made the accusation eighty lashes, do not accept their testimony ever, and those are the ones who opposed the command of God and departed from His obedience, thereby becoming corrupt.

It has been mentioned that this verse was revealed concerning those who accused ʿAʾisha, the wife of the Prophet (ﷺ), with the slander they leveled against her.

Those who said this:

- Abu al-Sāʾib and Ibrahim ibn Saʿid narrated to me, saying: Ibn Fudayl related to us, from Khuṣayf, who said: I said to Saʿid ibn Jubayr: Is fornication worse, or the slander of a chaste woman? He said: No, rather fornication. I said: God says, ﴿And those who accuse chaste women﴾. He said: This refers specifically to the incident of ʿAʾisha.
- I was told, from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muʿadh say: ʿUbayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Ḍaḥḥāk say, concerning His words: ﴿And those who accuse chaste women and then do not produce four witnesses﴾ ... the verse, that it refers to the women of the Muslims.
- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His words: ﴿And those are the defiantly disobedient﴾, he said: They are the liars.

* *

**The interpretation of His words, the Exalted: ﴿Except those who repent after that and make amends; indeed God is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ (5)**

The people of interpretation differed regarding what the exception in His words ﴿Except those who repent after that and make amends﴾ refers to. Some of them said: it is an exception from His words ﴿and do not accept their testimony ever, and those are the defiantly disobedient﴾. They said: if the slanderer repents, his testimony is accepted and the name of corruption (fisq) is removed from him, whether or not he received the prescribed punishment.

Those who said this:

- Aḥmad ibn Ḥammād al-Dūlābī narrated to us, saying: Sufyān related to me, from al-Zuhrī, from Saʿid, God willing, that ʿUmar said to Abu Bakra: If you repent, your testimony will be accepted; otherwise I will reject your testimony.
- Ibn Ḥumayd narrated to us, saying: Salama related to us, from Ibn Isḥāq, from al-Zuhrī, from Saʿid ibn al-Musayyab: that ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb struck Abu Bakra, Shibl ibn Maʿbad and Nāfiʿ ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Kalada with the prescribed punishment. He said to them: Whoever retracts his own statement, I will accept his testimony in what follows; whoever does not, I will not accept his testimony. Shibl and Nāfiʿ retracted their statements, but Abu Bakra refused to do so. Al-Zuhrī said: By God, this is a sunna, so preserve it.
- Ibn Abi al-Shawārib narrated to us, saying: Yazid ibn Zurayʿ related to us, saying: Dāwud related to us, from al-Shaʿbī, who said: If he repents, meaning the slanderer, and nothing is known of him except goodness, his testimony is admissible.
- ʿImrān ibn Mūsā narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Wārith related to us, saying: Dāwud related to us, from al-Shaʿbī, who said: It is incumbent upon the ruler to ask the slanderer to repent after the flogging; if he repents and good is ascertained of him, his testimony is admissible; if he does not repent, he is a rogue (khalīʿ) whose testimony is not admissible.
- Ibn al-Muthannā narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Wārith related to us, saying: Dāwud related to us, from ʿĀmir, that he said concerning the slanderer: If he repents and good is known of him, his testimony is admissible; if he does not repent, he is a rogue whose testimony is not admissible, and his repentance is retracting his own statement.
- He said: Ibn Abi ʿAdiyy related to us, from Dāwud, from al-Shaʿbī, something similar.
- Abu Kurayb and Abu al-Sāʾib narrated to us, both saying: Ibn Idrīs related to us, saying: Dāwud ibn Abi Hind informed us, from al-Shaʿbī, who said concerning the slanderer: If he repents and retracts his statement, his testimony is accepted; otherwise he is a rogue with no testimony, because God says: ﴿Why did they not bring four witnesses against it?﴾ ... to the end of the verse.
- Yaʿqūb narrated to me, saying: Hushaym related to us, saying: Dāwud ibn Abi Hind informed us, from al-Shaʿbī, that he used to say concerning the testimony of the slanderer: If he retracts his statement while being flogged, or retracts his statement, his testimony is accepted.
- He said: Hushaym related to us, from Ismāʿīl ibn Abi Khālid, from al-Shaʿbī, that he used to say: God accepts his repentance, and you reject his testimony; and he would accept his testimony if he repented.
  He said: Ismāʿīl informed us, from al-Shaʿbī, that he used to say concerning the slanderer: If he testifies before the prescribed punishment is inflicted, his testimony is accepted.
- He said: Hushaym related to us, saying: ʿUbayda informed us, from Ibrāhīm and Ismāʿīl ibn Sālim, from al-Shaʿbī, that they both said concerning the slanderer: If he testifies before being lashed, his testimony is admissible.
- Yaʿqūb narrated to me, saying: Abu Bishr, meaning Ibn ʿUlayya, said: I heard Ibn Abi Najīḥ say: The slanderer, if he repents, his testimony is admissible. He said: We used to say this. It was asked of him: From whom? He said: ʿAṭāʾ, Ṭāwūs and Mujāhid said it.
- Ibn Bashshār and Ibn al-Muthannā narrated to us, saying: Muḥammad ibn Khālid ibn ʿUthma related to us, saying: Saʿīd ibn Bashīr related to us, from Qatāda, from ʿUmar ibn Ṭalḥa, from ʿAbd Allāh, who said: If the slanderer repents, he is flogged and his testimony is admissible. Abu Mūsā said: This is what Ibn Abi ʿUthma said.
- Ibn Bashshār and Ibn al-Muthannā narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi ʿUthma related to us, saying: Saʿīd ibn Bashīr related to us, from Qatāda, from Sulaymān ibn Yasār and al-Shaʿbī, who both said: If the slanderer repents at the time of the flogging, his testimony is admissible.
- Ibn Bashshār narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Aʿlā related to us, saying: Saʿīd related to us, from Qatāda, that ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abi Ṭalḥa flogged a man for slander, and he said: Retract your statement, so that your testimony may be accepted.
- Ibn Bashshār narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān related to us, saying: Sufyān related to us, from Abu al-Haytham, who said: I heard Ibrāhīm and al-Shaʿbī discussing the testimony of the slanderer. Al-Shaʿbī said to Ibrāhīm: Why do you not accept his testimony? He said: Because I do not know whether he has repented or not.
- He said: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān related to us, saying: ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mubārak related to us, from Mujālid, from al-Shaʿbī, from Masrūq, who said: His testimony is accepted if he repents.
- He said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mubārak related to us, from Yaʿqūb ibn al-Qaʿqāʿ, from Muḥammad ibn Zayd, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, something similar.
- He said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mubārak related to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from ʿImrān ibn Mūsā, who said: I witnessed ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz admit the testimony of a slanderer, along with another man.
- Ibn al-Muthannā narrated to us, saying: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar related to us, saying: Shuʿba related to us, from al-Ḥakam, who said: al-Shaʿbī said: If he repents, his testimony is admissible. Ibn al-Muthannā said: In my view, meaning in the case of slander.
- Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Idrīs related to us, saying: Mismar informed us, from ʿImrān ibn ʿUmayr, that ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUtba used to admit the testimony of a slanderer if he repented.
- Yaʿqūb narrated to me, saying: Hushaym related to me, from Juwaybir, from al-Ḍaḥḥāk, who said: If he repents and makes amends, the testimony of the slanderer is accepted.
- Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr informed us, from Maʿmar, from Qatāda, from Ibn al-Musayyab, who said: The testimony of a slanderer is accepted if he repents.
- al-Ḥasan narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzāq related to us, saying: Maʿmar informed us, from Qatāda, from Ibn al-Musayyab, something similar.
- Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā narrated to us, saying: Muḥammad related to us, from Maʿmar, who said: al-Zuhrī said: When the slanderer receives the prescribed punishment, the ruler should ask him to repent; if he repents, his testimony is accepted, otherwise it is not. He said: This is what ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb did with those who testified against al-Mughīra ibn Shuʿba: they repented, except Abu Bakra, whose testimony was therefore not accepted.

Others said: the exception applies to His words ﴿and those are the defiantly disobedient﴾.

As for His words ﴿and do not accept their testimony ever﴾, it is joined to "ever" and it is not permissible to accept their testimony at any time.

Those who said this:

- Ibn Abi al-Shawārib narrated to us, saying: Yazid ibn Zurayʿ related to us, saying: Ashʿath ibn Sawwār related to us, saying: al-Shaʿbī related to me, who said: Shurayḥ used to admit the testimony of anyone who had committed any offence once he repented, except the slanderer. As for his repentance, it is between him and his Lord, and we do not admit his testimony.
- Ḥumayd ibn Masʿada narrated to us, saying: Yazīd related to us, saying: Ashʿath ibn Sawwār related to us, saying: al-Shaʿbī related to us, from Shurayḥ, with something similar, except that he said: The one subject to any prescribed punishment, if he was just on the day he testified.
- Abu al-Sāʾib narrated to me, saying: Abu Muʿāwiya related to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Ibrāhīm, from Shurayḥ, who said: He would not admit the testimony of a slanderer, and would say: His repentance is between him and his Lord.
- Abu Kurayb and Abu al-Sāʾib narrated to us, both saying: Ibn Idrīs related to us, from Muṭarrif, from Abu ʿUthmān, from Shurayḥ concerning the slanderer: God accepts his repentance, but I do not accept his testimony.
- Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Idrīs related to us, saying: Ashʿath informed us, from al-Shaʿbī, who said: Two litigants came to him, and one of them brought a witness who had lost a hand. The opponent said: Do you not see what is wrong with him? He said: I have seen it. He then asked the people, and they praised him highly. Shurayḥ said: We admit the testimony of everyone subject to a prescribed punishment, if on the day he testifies he is just, except the slanderer, whose repentance is between him and his Lord.
- Abu al-Sāʾib narrated to us, saying: Ibn Idrīs related to us, saying: Ashʿath informed us, from al-Shaʿbī, who said: Two litigants came to Shurayḥ, and one of them brought evidence, bringing a witness who had lost a hand. The opponent said: Do you not see what is wrong with him? Shurayḥ said: We have seen it, and we asked the people and they praised him well. Then he related the rest of the report, similar to the report of Abu Kurayb.
- Yaʿqūb narrated to me, saying: Hushaym related to us, saying: al-Shaybānī informed us, from al-Shaʿbī, from Shurayḥ, that he used to say: His testimony is never accepted; his repentance is between him and his Lord, meaning the slanderer.
- He said: Hushaym related to us, saying: al-Ashʿath informed us, from al-Shaʿbī, that Rabbāb had cut off a man's hand and foot for highway robbery. He said: Then the man repented and made amends, and he testified before Shurayḥ, and he admitted his testimony. The man against whom he testified said: Do you admit his testimony against me when he has lost a limb? He said: Shurayḥ said: Everyone subject to a prescribed punishment, once it is carried out on him and he then repents and makes amends, his testimony is admissible, except the slanderer.
- Ibn al-Muthannā narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Walīd related to us, saying: Shuʿba related to us, saying: al-Mughīra informed me, saying: I heard Ibrāhīm narrate from Shurayḥ, who said: It is a decree from God: his testimony is never accepted; his repentance is between him and his Lord. Abu Mūsā said: meaning the slanderer.
- Yaʿqūb narrated to me, saying: Hushaym related to us, saying: Mughīra informed us, from Ibrāhīm, who said: Shurayḥ said: God does not accept his testimony ever.
- Ibn al-Muthannā narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Walīd related to us, saying: Ḥammād related to us, from Qatāda, from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab, who said: The testimony of a slanderer is not admissible; his repentance is between him and God.
- Ibn Bashshār narrated to us, saying: Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā related to us, saying: Saʿīd related to us, from Qatāda, from al-Ḥasan, that he said: The slanderer's repentance is between him and God, but his testimony is not accepted.
- Ibn al-Muthannā narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Walīd related to us, saying: Ḥammād related to us, from Qatāda, from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab, who said: The testimony of a slanderer is not admissible; his repentance is between him and God.
- Ibn Bashshār narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Aʿlā related to us, saying: Saʿīd related to us, from Qatāda, from al-Ḥasan, that he said: The slanderer's repentance is between him and God, and his testimony is not accepted.
- Ibn al-Muthannā narrated to us, saying: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar related to us, saying: Shuʿba related to us, from al-Ḥakam, from Ibrāhīm, that he said concerning a man who receives the prescribed punishment: His testimony is never admissible.
- Yaʿqūb narrated to me, saying: Hushaym related to us, saying: Mughīra informed us, from Ibrāhīm, that he would never accept his testimony, and his repentance is between him and God, meaning the slanderer.
- Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Muʿtamir ibn Sulaymān related to us, from Ḥajjāj, from ʿAmr ibn Shuʿayb, from his father, from his grandfather, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "The testimony of one who has received a prescribed punishment in Islam is not admissible."
- Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Maʿmar, from al-Ḥasan, concerning ﴿and do not accept their testimony ever﴾: He would say: The testimony of the slanderer is never accepted; his repentance is only between him and God. And Shurayḥ used to say: His testimony is not accepted.
- ʿAlī narrated to me, saying: ʿAbd Allāh related to us, from ʿAlī, from Ibn ʿAbbās, concerning His words ﴿and do not accept their testimony ever﴾, then he said: Whoever repents and makes amends, his testimony is accepted according to the Book of God.

The correct view among us on this matter is that the exception applies to both meanings together: that is, to His words ﴿and do not accept their testimony ever﴾ and to His words ﴿and those are the defiantly disobedient﴾. This is because there is no disagreement among all of them that this is so when the slanderer has not received the prescribed punishment until he repents, either by the matter being brought before the authority with the one slandered pardoning him, or by her dying before the claim for her prescribed punishment was pursued, with no one seeking it on her behalf. Given that this is the case, and a repentance has occurred from him through which his uprightness (ʿadāla) is validly restored, it is agreed by all that this is the case.

Since it is agreed upon by all, and God, the Exalted, did not stipulate in His Book that his testimony must never be accepted after the prescribed punishment for his accusation, but rather forbade accepting his testimony in the state in which He obliged the punishment upon him and called him a corrupt person (fāsiq), it is known from this that imposing the prescribed punishment on him for his accusation does not produce a change in his testimony with repentance for his sin, unless it was already invalid before the punishment was imposed upon him. Rather, his repentance after the punishment has been imposed upon him for his sin makes his testimony with it more admissible than it was before the punishment was imposed upon him; because the prescribed punishment increases the one receiving it in purification from his crime for which the punishment was owed.

If someone says: Could the exception be from His words ﴿then lash them﴾, so that repentance removes the punishment from him, just as his testimony was admissible for you before and after the punishment, and removes the name of corruption from him? It is said: That is not permissible in our view, because the punishment is a right of the one slandered, like retaliation (qiṣāṣ) that is owed to her for a crime that involves retaliation. There is no disagreement among all that his repentance from that does not remove what is owed to her of retaliation from him; similarly, his repentance from slander does not remove what is owed to her of the prescribed punishment, because that is her right: if she wishes, she may pardon it, and if she wishes, she may pursue it. The repentance of a servant from his sin only removes from him the blameworthy names and the ugly attributes; but the rights of human beings, which God obliged for some of them over others in all circumstances, are not removed or nullified by it.

The people of knowledge differed regarding the manner of the slanderer's repentance by which his testimony is admitted. Some of them said: It is his retracting his own statement regarding it. We have already mentioned some of those who said this previously, and we will now mention some of what we have come across that we did not mention before.

- Abu al-Sāʾib narrated to me, saying: Ḥafṣ related to us, from Layth, from Ṭāwūs, who said: The repentance of the slanderer is that he retracts his own statement.
- Yaʿqūb ibn Ibrāhīm narrated to me, saying: Hushaym related to us, saying: Ḥuṣayn informed us, who said: I saw a man receive the prescribed punishment for slander in Medina. When he had finished being struck, he took up his garment and said: I seek God's forgiveness and turn to Him in repentance from slandering chaste women. He said: I met Abu al-Zinād and mentioned that to him. He said: The matter here, with us, is that if he says that when he finishes being struck, and nothing is known of him except goodness, his testimony is accepted.
- I was told, from al-Ḥusayn, who said: I heard Abu Muʿādh say: ʿUbayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Ḍaḥḥāk say concerning His words ﴿and do not accept their testimony ever, and those are the defiantly disobedient. Except those who repent﴾ ... the verse: He said: Whoever openly acknowledges and confesses on his own behalf that he uttered the slander, and repents to God with sincere repentance (tawba naṣūḥ), and sincere means that they do not return to it, and his acknowledgment and confession at the time of the prescribed punishment, when he is seized for the lashing, is repentance.

Others said: His repentance from that is the rectification of his condition, his regret for what he committed of that, his seeking forgiveness for it, and his abandoning of returning to such a sin. This is the view of a group of the Successors (tābiʿūn) and others, and we have mentioned some of its proponents before; and it is the view of Mālik ibn Anas.

This view is more correct than the other of the two views on this matter, because God, may His remembrance be exalted, made the repentance of every person of the believers who has committed a sin to consist of abandoning its return, regretting what has passed of it, and seeking forgiveness from his Lord for it, in respect of a sin between the servant and Him, apart from what concerns the rights of His servants and their wrongs against one another. The slanderer, when the prescribed punishment (hadd) is carried out against him, or he is pardoned, has nothing left upon him except his repentance from his offence between himself and his Lord; so the way of his repentance from it is the way of his repentance from all his other offences. Since the sound position on this matter is what we have described, the meaning of the speech is: "And those are the defiantly disobedient (fasiqun), except those who repent after that and make amends, from their offence which they committed by their slander of chaste women, after their committing it." ﴿Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾. That is, He conceals their sins by His pardon of them, and He is merciful to them after repentance, by not punishing them for them. So accept their testimony, and do not call them defiant transgressors (fasiqah); rather, call them by the names that belong to them in their state of repentance.

**The interpretation of His words, the Exalted: ﴿And those who accuse chaste women and then do not produce four witnesses, lash them eighty lashes, and do not accept their testimony ever after. Those are the defiantly disobedient﴾ (4)**

He, the Exalted, says: those who slander chaste women among the free believing women and accuse them of fornication, and then do not produce four upright witnesses who testify that they saw those women committing it, then lash those who made the accusation eighty lashes, do not accept their testimony ever, and those are the ones who opposed the command of God and departed from His obedience, thereby becoming corrupt.

It has been mentioned that this verse was revealed concerning those who accused ʿAʾisha, the wife of the Prophet (ﷺ), with the slander they leveled against her.

Those who said this:

- Abu al-Sāʾib and Ibrahim ibn Saʿid narrated to me, saying: Ibn Fudayl related to us, from Khuṣayf, who said: I said to Saʿid ibn Jubayr: Is fornication worse, or the slander of a chaste woman? He said: No, rather fornication. I said: God says, ﴿And those who accuse chaste women﴾. He said: This refers specifically to the incident of ʿAʾisha.
- I was told, from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muʿadh say: ʿUbayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Ḍaḥḥāk say, concerning His words: ﴿And those who accuse chaste women and then do not produce four witnesses﴾ ... the verse, that it refers to the women of the Muslims.
- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His words: ﴿And those are the defiantly disobedient﴾, he said: They are the liars.

* *

**The interpretation of His words, the Exalted: ﴿Except those who repent after that and make amends; indeed God is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ (5)**

The people of interpretation differed regarding what the exception in His words ﴿Except those who repent after that and make amends﴾ refers to. Some of them said: it is an exception from His words ﴿and do not accept their testimony ever, and those are the defiantly disobedient﴾. They said: if the slanderer repents, his testimony is accepted and the name of corruption (fisq) is removed from him, whether or not he received the prescribed punishment.

Those who said this:

- Aḥmad ibn Ḥammād al-Dūlābī narrated to us, saying: Sufyān related to me, from al-Zuhrī, from Saʿid, God willing, that ʿUmar said to Abu Bakra: If you repent, your testimony will be accepted; otherwise I will reject your testimony.
- Ibn Ḥumayd narrated to us, saying: Salama related to us, from Ibn Isḥāq, from al-Zuhrī, from Saʿid ibn al-Musayyab: that ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb struck Abu Bakra, Shibl ibn Maʿbad and Nāfiʿ ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Kalada with the prescribed punishment. He said to them: Whoever retracts his own statement, I will accept his testimony in what follows; whoever does not, I will not accept his testimony. Shibl and Nāfiʿ retracted their statements, but Abu Bakra refused to do so. Al-Zuhrī said: By God, this is a sunna, so preserve it.
- Ibn Abi al-Shawārib narrated to us, saying: Yazid ibn Zurayʿ related to us, saying: Dāwud related to us, from al-Shaʿbī, who said: If he repents, meaning the slanderer, and nothing is known of him except goodness, his testimony is admissible.
- ʿImrān ibn Mūsā narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Wārith related to us, saying: Dāwud related to us, from al-Shaʿbī, who said: It is incumbent upon the ruler to ask the slanderer to repent after the flogging; if he repents and good is ascertained of him, his testimony is admissible; if he does not repent, he is a rogue (khalīʿ) whose testimony is not admissible.
- Ibn al-Muthannā narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Wārith related to us, saying: Dāwud related to us, from ʿĀmir, that he said concerning the slanderer: If he repents and good is known of him, his testimony is admissible; if he does not repent, he is a rogue whose testimony is not admissible, and his repentance is retracting his own statement.

- Abu Kurayb and Abu al-Sāʾib narrated to us, both saying: Ibn Idrīs related to us, saying: Dāwud ibn Abi Hind informed us, from al-Shaʿbī, who said concerning the slanderer: If he repents and retracts his statement, his testimony is accepted; otherwise he is a rogue with no testimony, because God says: ﴿Why did they not bring four witnesses against it?﴾ ... to the end of the verse.

- Ibn Bashshār and Ibn al-Muthannā narrated to us, saying: Muḥammad ibn Khālid ibn ʿUthma related to us, saying: Saʿīd ibn Bashīr related to us, from Qatāda, from ʿUmar ibn Ṭalḥa, from ʿAbd Allāh, who said: If the slanderer repents, he is flogged and his testimony is admissible. Abu Mūsā said: This is what Ibn Abi ʿUthma said.
- Ibn Bashshār and Ibn al-Muthannā narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi ʿUthma related to us, saying: Saʿīd ibn Bashīr related to us, from Qatāda, from Sulaymān ibn Yasār and al-Shaʿbī, who both said: If the slanderer repents at the time of the flogging, his testimony is admissible.
- Ibn Bashshār narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Aʿlā related to us, saying: Saʿīd related to us, from Qatāda, that ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abi Ṭalḥa flogged a man for slander, and he said: Retract your statement, so that your testimony may be accepted.
- Ibn Bashshār narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān related to us, saying: Sufyān related to us, from Abu al-Haytham, who said: I heard Ibrāhīm and al-Shaʿbī discussing the testimony of the slanderer. - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Idrīs related to us, saying: Mismar informed us, from ʿImrān ibn ʿUmayr, that ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUtba used to admit the testimony of a slanderer if he repented.

So accept their testimony, and do not call them defiant transgressors (fasiqah); rather, call them by the names that belong to them in their state of repentance.

Traditions have come from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in accordance with what we have said concerning this, and a group of the people of interpretation have held this view.

Mention of the narration concerning this, and mention of the cause for which this verse was revealed:

⁕ Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, he said: Ibn 'Ulayya narrated to us, he said: Ayyub narrated to us, from 'Ikrima, he said: When ﴿And those who accuse chaste women, then do not bring four witnesses, lash them eighty lashes﴾ was revealed, Sa'd ibn 'Ubada said: "By Allah, if I saw a woman [lying] with her thighs open and a man upon her, I would have said what I saw, that on my back [would be] eighty [lashes] unless I bring four witnesses? By the time I bring four, the man will have finished his need." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O assembly of the Ansar, do you not hear what your chief says?" They said: "O Messenger of Allah, do not blame him, and they mentioned his jealousy: he never married a woman except a virgin, and never divorced a woman and anyone of us went back to her." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, Allah refuses except that." He said: "Allah and His Messenger have spoken the truth." He said: "They did not delay until a cousin of his came and accused his wife, which weighed heavily on the Muslims, and he said: 'No, by Allah, He will not place eighty on my back forever. I looked until I was certain, and I listened until I was healed.'" He said: "Then Allah revealed the Qur'an concerning li'an (mutual cursing). It was said to him: 'Swear!' He swore. He said: 'Stop him at the fifth, for it is binding.' He said: 'Allah will not cause him to enter the Fire by this, ever, just as He averted from him eighty lashes. I looked until I was certain, and I listened until I was healed,' and he swore. Then it was said: 'Swear!' She swore. Then he said: 'Stop her at the fifth, for it is binding.' It was said to her: 'It is binding.' She hesitated for a while, then said: 'I will not disgrace my people,' and she swore. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'If she brings forth such and such, it is for her husband, and if she brings forth such and such, it is for the one about whom was said what was said.'" He said: "So she brought forth a boy like a grey camel, who afterwards became a governor in Egypt, whose lineage was not known, or it was not known who his father was."

⁕ Khallad ibn Aslam narrated to us, he said: al-Nadr ibn Shumayl informed us, he said: 'Abbad informed us, he said: I heard 'Ikrima, from Ibn 'Abbas, he said: When this verse was revealed: ﴿And those who accuse chaste women, then do not bring four witnesses, lash them eighty lashes, and do not accept their testimony ever, and they are the defiantly disobedient﴾, Sa'd ibn 'Ubada said: "Is it thus revealed, O Messenger of Allah? They said: "Do not blame him, for he is a jealous man. He never married among us except a virgin, and no man divorced his wife and another of us dared to marry her." Sa'd said: "O Messenger of Allah, may my father and mother be your ransom, by Allah I know that it is from Allah and that it is true, but I marvelled that if I found a woman whose thighs a man had opened, it would not be for me to stir him or move him until I bring four witnesses. By Allah I will not bring four witnesses until he has finished his need." They had not waited long when Hilal ibn Umayya came from his garden and saw with his eyes and heard with his ears, and he held back until morning. When it was morning he went early to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), while he was sitting with his companions, and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I came to my family in the evening and found a man with my family; I saw with my eyes and heard with my ears." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) disliked what he had brought him and it weighed heavily upon him greatly, until that was recognised in his face. Hilal said: "By Allah, O Messenger of Allah, I see the aversion in your face at what I have brought you, and Allah knows that I am truthful and I have said only what is true, and I truly hope that Allah will make a way out." He said: The Ansar gathered and said: "We have been tested with what Sa'd said: Shall Hilal ibn Umayya be flogged and his testimony nullified among the Muslims?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) resolved to strike him, and he was indeed wishing to order his beating, while the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was sitting with his companions, when revelation descended upon him. His companions held back from speaking to him when they recognised that revelation had come down, until it finished. Allah revealed: ﴿And those who accuse their wives, and have no witnesses except themselves﴾ ... to: ﴿that the wrath of Allah be upon her if he is of the truthful﴾. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Rejoice, O Hilal, for Allah has made a way out." He said: "I had been hoping for that from Allah." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Send for her!" She came, and when they both were gathered before the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), she was addressed, and she denied it. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah knows that one of you two is a liar; is there any repentant among you?" Hilal said: "O Messenger of Allah, may my father and mother be your ransom, I have indeed spoken the truth, and I have said only what is true." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Perform li'an between them!" It was said to Hilal: "O Hilal, bear witness," and he bore witness four testimonies by Allah that he is surely of the truthful. At the fifth it was said to him: "O Hilal, fear Allah, for the punishment of Allah is more severe than the punishment of men; this is the binding one that makes the punishment obligatory upon you." Hilal said: "By Allah, Allah will not punish me for it, just as the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not flog me for it," and he bore the fifth testimony: ﴿that the curse of Allah be upon him if he is of the liars﴾. Then it was said to her: "Bear witness," and she bore witness four testimonies by Allah that he is surely of the liars. At the fifth it was said to her: "Fear Allah, for the punishment of Allah is more severe than the punishment of men, and this is the binding one that makes the punishment obligatory upon you." She hesitated for a while, then said: "By Allah, I will not disgrace my people," and she bore the fifth testimony: ﴿that the wrath of Allah be upon her if he is of the truthful﴾. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) separated them, and decided that the child belonged to her, and that he should not be claimed for a father, and her child should not be accused.

⁕ Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Tusi narrated to me, he said: Abu Ahmad al-Husayn ibn Muhammad narrated to us, he said: Jarir ibn Hazim narrated to us, from Ayyub, from 'Ikrima, from Ibn 'Abbas, he said: "When Hilal ibn Umayya accused his wife, it was said to him: 'By Allah, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) will surely flog you eighty lashes.' He said: 'Allah is more just than that, that He would strike me a blow when He knows that I have seen until I was certain, and heard until I was assured. No, by Allah, he will never strike me.' Then the verse of mutual cursing was revealed, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) summoned them both when the verse was revealed, and said: 'Allah knows that one of you is a liar; is there any repentant among you?' Hilal said: 'By Allah, I am truthful.' He said to him: 'Swear by Allah, other than whom there is no god: I am truthful,' saying this four times, 'and if I am a liar, then upon me is the curse of Allah.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Stop him at the fifth, for it is binding.' He swore. Then she said four times: 'By Allah, other than whom there is no god, he is surely of the liars, and if he is truthful, then upon her is the wrath of Allah.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Stop her at the fifth, for it is binding.' She wavered and was about to confess, then said: 'I will not disgrace my people.'"

⁕ Abu Kurayb and Abu Hisham al-Rifa'i narrated to us, both said: 'Abda narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Ibrahim, from 'Alqama, from 'Abdullah, he said: "We were on a Friday night in the mosque, when a man entered and said: 'If a man found with his wife another man and killed him, you would kill him; and if he spoke, you would flog him.' This was mentioned to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and Allah revealed the verse of li'an. Then the man came afterwards and accused his wife, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) performed li'an between them. He said: 'Perhaps she will bring forth a child who is black and curly-haired.' So she brought forth a child who was black and curly-haired."

⁕ Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, he said: Jarir ibn 'Abd al-Hamid narrated to us, from 'Abd al-Malik ibn Abi Sulayman, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, he said: "I asked Ibn 'Umar, and I said: 'O Abu 'Abd al-Rahman, is there separation between the two who perform li'an?' He said: 'Yes, Glory be to Allah! The first to ask about that was so-and-so; he came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and asked him, saying: "Tell me, if one of us saw his wife in immorality, what should he do?" He did not answer him in that matter at all.' He said: 'Then he came to him afterwards and said: "The thing you asked about, I have been tested with it," and Allah revealed this verse in Surat al-Nur.' He called the man, admonished and reminded him, and informed him that the punishment of this world is easier than the punishment of the Hereafter. He said: 'By Him who sent you with the truth, I saw and I did not lie about her.' He called the woman, admonished her, and informed her that the punishment of this world is easier than the punishment of the Hereafter. She said: 'By Him who sent you with the truth, he is surely a liar and he saw nothing.' He said: The man began, and bore witness four testimonies by Allah: that he is surely of the truthful, and the fifth that the curse of Allah be upon him if he is of the liars. Then the woman bore witness four testimonies by Allah that he is surely of the liars, and the fifth that the wrath of Allah be upon her if he is of the truthful; and they were separated."

⁕ Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, he said: Ibn Abi 'Adi narrated to us, from Dawud, from 'Amir, he said: "When this was revealed: ﴿And those who accuse chaste women, then do not bring four witnesses, lash them eighty lashes﴾, 'Asim ibn 'Adi said: 'If I see and speak, I will be flogged eighty; and if I remain silent, I remain silent in rage.' He said: That was difficult upon the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), so this verse was revealed: ﴿And those who accuse their wives, and have no witnesses except themselves﴾. He said: They did not delay except a week, until a man of his people and his wife had an incident, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) performed li'an between them."

⁕ 'Ali narrated to me, he said: 'Abd Allah narrated to us, he said: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, his saying: ﴿And those who accuse their wives, and have no witnesses except themselves﴾ ... the verse; and the fifth: that it be said to him: "Upon you is the curse of Allah if you are of the liars." If the woman confesses to his statement, she is stoned; and if she denies it, she bears witness four testimonies by Allah that he is surely of the liars, and the fifth that it be said to her: "Upon you is the wrath of Allah if he is of the truthful." Thus the punishment is averted from her, and they are separated, and they never come together again, and the child is attributed to its mother.

⁕ al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from 'Ikrima, his saying: ﴿And those who accuse their wives﴾, he said: "Hilal ibn Umayya: the one I accused was Shurayk ibn Sahma', and the one who asked 'Asim ibn 'Adi for a ruling."

He said: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, he said: al-Zuhri informed me concerning li'an and the sunna in it, from the hadith of Sahl ibn Sa'd that a man from the Ansar came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "Tell me, if a man found with his wife another man, would he kill him and you kill him? Or how should he act?" So Allah revealed concerning his matter what was mentioned about the mutual cursers. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah has decided concerning you and your wife," and they performed li'an while I was present, then he separated from her in the presence of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). So the sunna after that became that the mutual cursers be separated; she was pregnant, and he disowned it, so the child was called after his mother, and then the sunna established that her son inherits from her and she inherits what Allah has prescribed for her.

⁕ Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, he said: My father narrated to me, he said: My paternal uncle narrated to me, he said: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, his saying: ﴿And those who accuse their wives﴾ ... to his saying: ﴿if he is of the liars﴾, he said: "When the man bears witness five testimonies, each of them is cleared from the other; and her waiting period, if she is pregnant, is to deliver her burden; neither of them is flogged. If she does not swear, the hadd and stoning are established against her."
