⁕ Abu Kurayb and Abu Hisham al-Rifa'i narrated to us, both said: 'Abda narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Ibrahim, from 'Alqama, from 'Abdullah, he said: "We were on a Friday night in the mosque, when a man entered and said: 'If a man found with his wife another man and killed him, you would kill him; and if he spoke, you would flog him.' This was mentioned to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and Allah revealed the verse of li'an. Then the man came afterwards and accused his wife, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) performed li'an between them. He said: 'Perhaps she will bring forth a child who is black and curly-haired.' So she brought forth a child who was black and curly-haired."

⁕ Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, he said: Jarir ibn 'Abd al-Hamid narrated to us, from 'Abd al-Malik ibn Abi Sulayman, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, he said: "I asked Ibn 'Umar, and I said: 'O Abu 'Abd al-Rahman, is there separation between the two who perform li'an?' He said: 'Yes, Glory be to Allah! The first to ask about that was so-and-so; he came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and asked him, saying: "Tell me, if one of us saw his wife in immorality, what should he do?" He did not answer him in that matter at all.' He said: 'Then he came to him afterwards and said: "The thing you asked about, I have been tested with it," and Allah revealed this verse in Surat al-Nur.' He called the man, admonished and reminded him, and informed him that the punishment of this world is easier than the punishment of the Hereafter. He said: 'By Him who sent you with the truth, I saw and I did not lie about her.' He called the woman, admonished her, and informed her that the punishment of this world is easier than the punishment of the Hereafter. She said: 'By Him who sent you with the truth, he is surely a liar and he saw nothing.' He said: The man began, and bore witness four testimonies by Allah: that he is surely of the truthful, and the fifth that the curse of Allah be upon him if he is of the liars. Then the woman bore witness four testimonies by Allah that he is surely of the liars, and the fifth that the wrath of Allah be upon her if he is of the truthful; and they were separated."

⁕ Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, he said: Ibn Abi 'Adi narrated to us, from Dawud, from 'Amir, he said: "When this was revealed: ﴿And those who accuse chaste women, then do not bring four witnesses, lash them eighty lashes﴾, 'Asim ibn 'Adi said: 'If I see and speak, I will be flogged eighty; and if I remain silent, I remain silent in rage.' He said: That was difficult upon the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), so this verse was revealed: ﴿And those who accuse their wives, and have no witnesses except themselves﴾. He said: They did not delay except a week, until a man of his people and his wife had an incident, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) performed li'an between them."

⁕ 'Ali narrated to me, he said: 'Abd Allah narrated to us, he said: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, his saying: ﴿And those who accuse their wives, and have no witnesses except themselves﴾ ... the verse; and the fifth: that it be said to him: "Upon you is the curse of Allah if you are of the liars." If the woman confesses to his statement, she is stoned; and if she denies it, she bears witness four testimonies by Allah that he is surely of the liars, and the fifth that it be said to her: "Upon you is the wrath of Allah if he is of the truthful." Thus the punishment is averted from her, and they are separated, and they never come together again, and the child is attributed to its mother.

⁕ al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from 'Ikrima, his saying: ﴿And those who accuse their wives﴾, he said: "Hilal ibn Umayya: the one I accused was Shurayk ibn Sahma', and the one who asked 'Asim ibn 'Adi for a ruling."

He said: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, he said: al-Zuhri informed me concerning li'an and the sunna in it, from the hadith of Sahl ibn Sa'd that a man from the Ansar came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "Tell me, if a man found with his wife another man, would he kill him and you kill him? Or how should he act?" So Allah revealed concerning his matter what was mentioned about the mutual cursers. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah has decided concerning you and your wife," and they performed li'an while I was present, then he separated from her in the presence of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). So the sunna after that became that the mutual cursers be separated; she was pregnant, and he disowned it, so the child was called after his mother, and then the sunna established that her son inherits from her and she inherits what Allah has prescribed for her.

⁕ Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, he said: My father narrated to me, he said: My paternal uncle narrated to me, he said: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, his saying: ﴿And those who accuse their wives﴾ ... to his saying: ﴿if he is of the liars﴾, he said: "When the man bears witness five testimonies, each of them is cleared from the other; and her waiting period, if she is pregnant, is to deliver her burden; neither of them is flogged. If she does not swear, the hadd and stoning are established against her."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 24, verses 8–9:

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿And it shall avert from her the punishment that she testify four times by Allah that he is surely one of the liars﴾ (8), ﴿and the fifth [testimony] that the wrath of Allah be upon her if he is of the truthful﴾ (9).

By His saying, may His mention be exalted, ﴿and it shall avert from her the punishment﴾: it means it shall ward off the prescribed punishment (hadd) from her.

The scholars differed concerning the punishment that Allah means in this place, that her four testimonies avert it from her. Some of them said: it is in line with what we have said on this, namely that the prescribed punishment (hadd) is a hundred lashes if she is a virgin, or stoning if she is a previously married woman who has been made chaste (muhsana).

Others said: rather, that is imprisonment. They said: what is obligatory upon her, if she does not give the four testimonies after the husband's four testimonies, is imprisonment, not the prescribed punishment; and li'an (the mutual oath of condemnation) is imprisonment rather than the hadd.

We have only said that what is obligatory upon her, if she refrains from li'an after the husband has performed li'an, is the prescribed punishment described above, by analogy with the consensus of all that when the prescribed punishment is lifted from the husband by the four testimonies, given his truthfulness in what he accused her of, the prescribed punishment becomes obligatory upon her. So Allah made his four oaths, and his li'an in the fifth, a means of exempting him from the prescribed punishment that is due to her by his accusing her, just as He made the four witnesses a means of exempting him from it in that matter, the prescribed punishment being removed from him by them. Likewise, it is necessary that when the prescribed punishment is removed from him by this, her prescribed punishment becomes obligatory upon her, just as when it was removed from him by the witnesses it became obligatory upon her; there is no difference between these. We have fully explained the reasons for this in the chapter on li'an in our book called [Latif al-Qawl fi Sharai' al-Islam], so it suffices to not repeat it in this place.

* *

And His saying: ﴿that she testify four times by Allah﴾

It says: and it shall ward off the punishment from her that she swear by Allah four oaths that her husband, who accused her of the immorality with which he accused her, is surely among the liars concerning the fornication of which he accused her. And His saying: ﴿and the fifth [testimony] that the wrath of Allah be upon her﴾ ... the verse, means: and the fifth testimony is that the wrath of Allah be upon her if her husband is among the truthful in what he accused her of, namely fornication. The word ﴿والخامسة﴾ in both verses is in the nominative case (raf'), because of what follows it (as its predicate-subject structure, with the verb/clause following it supplying the predicate).

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 24, verses 8–9:

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿And it shall avert from her the punishment that she testify four times by Allah that he is surely one of the liars﴾ (8), ﴿and the fifth [testimony] that the wrath of Allah be upon her if he is of the truthful﴾ (9).

By His saying, may His mention be exalted, ﴿and it shall avert from her the punishment﴾: it means it shall ward off the prescribed punishment (hadd) from her.

* *

And His saying: ﴿that she testify four times by Allah﴾

It says: and it shall ward off the punishment from her that she swear by Allah four oaths that her husband, who accused her of the immorality with which he accused her, is surely among the liars concerning the fornication of which he accused her. And His saying: ﴿and the fifth [testimony] that the wrath of Allah be upon her﴾ ... the verse, means: and the fifth testimony is that the wrath of Allah be upon her if her husband is among the truthful in what he accused her of, namely fornication. The word ﴿والخامسة﴾ in both verses is in the nominative case (raf'), because of what follows it (as its predicate-subject structure, with the verb/clause following it supplying the predicate).

The commentary on His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And were it not for the grace of Allah upon you and His mercy, and that Allah is Accepting of repentance, Wise﴾ [24:10]

Says the Exalted, may His remembrance be great: "And were it not for the grace of Allah upon you, O people, and His mercy toward you, and that He is One who returns (to forgiveness) toward His creatures with His kindness and His bounty, Wise in His management of them and His governance of them, He would have hastened to punish you for your disobedience and exposed the people of sin among you for their sins. But He has concealed your sins from you and withheld their exposure upon you for now, out of His mercy toward you and His favour upon you. So thank Him for His blessings, and desist from advancing toward what He has forbidden you from among His acts of disobedience." The answer (to the conditional) is left out in this, relying on the listener's understanding of the intended meaning.

**Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 24, verse 11 (part 1 of 3):**

**On the interpretation of His words, may He be exalted:** ﴿Indeed, those who came with the slander are a band among you. Do not think it bad for you; rather, it is good for you. For every person among them is what he earned of the sin, and he who undertook the greater part of it among them will have a great punishment.﴾

His words, may His remembrance be exalted: "Indeed, those who came with the falsehood and the slander" — ﴿a band among you﴾ means a group among you, O people. ﴿Do not think it bad for you; rather, it is good for you﴾ means: do not suppose that what they brought of the slander is bad for you, with God or with people. Rather, that is good for you with Him and with the believers. This is because God makes it an expiation for the one who was accused, and He manifests his innocence of what he was accused of, and He makes a way out for him from it.

It has been said: those whom God meant by His words, ﴿Indeed, those who came with the slander are a band among you﴾, were a group including Hassan ibn Thabit, Mistah ibn Uthathah, and Hamnah bint Jahsh.

As related:

◆ Abd al-Warith ibn Abd al-Samad narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to us, saying: Aban al-Attar narrated to us, saying: Hisham ibn Urwah narrated to us, from Urwah, that he wrote to Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan: "You wrote to me asking me about those who came with the slander, and they are as God said: ﴿Indeed, those who came with the slander are a band among you﴾. None of them was named except Hassan ibn Thabit, Mistah ibn Uthathah, and Hamnah bint Jahsh, and it is said of others whom I have no knowledge of; only that they are a band, as God said."

◆ Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, regarding His words, ﴿they came with the slander, a band among you﴾: they were the companions of Aishah. Ibn Jurayj said: Ibn Abbas said regarding His words, ﴿they came with the slander, a band among you﴾ ... the verse: those who fabricated against Aishah were Abdullah ibn Ubayy, who undertook its greater part, and Hassan ibn Thabit, Mistah, and Hamnah bint Jahsh.

◆ It was narrated to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd informed us, who said: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words, ﴿those who came with the slander, a band among you﴾: those who said the slander and the falsehood to Aishah.

◆ Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words, ﴿Indeed, those who came with the slander are a band among you. Do not think it bad for you; rather, it is good for you﴾: He said: the evil for you is in the slander they uttered, the speech they spoke; it was evil for them. Among them were some who did not say it but only heard it, so God admonished them, and first said: ﴿Indeed, those who came with the slander are a band among you. Do not think it bad for you; rather, it is good for you﴾. Then He said: ﴿and he who undertook the greater part of it among them will have a great punishment﴾.

* *

And His words: ﴿For every person among them is what he earned of the sin﴾.

He says: for every person among those who came with the slander is the recompense of what he committed of sin by his coming with what he came with. The first of them was Abdullah.

* *

And His words: ﴿and he who undertook the greater part of it among them﴾.

He says: and he who bore the greater part of that sin and slander among them is the one who began to engage in it.

As related:

◆ It was narrated to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd informed us, who said: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words, ﴿and he who undertook the greater part of it among them﴾: He said: the one who began with that.

◆ Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to us, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words, ﴿a band among you﴾: He said: the companions of Aishah were Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul, Mistah, and Hassan.

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: for him is a great punishment from God on the Day of Resurrection.

The reciters have differed concerning the reading of His words, ﴿kibrahu﴾. The majority of the reciters of the principal cities read it ﴿kibrahu﴾ with a kasra on the kaf, except Humayd al-A'raj, who used to read it "kubrahu", meaning: "and he who bears its greatest part". [Qira'at: the recognized canonical readings of the Qur'an.]

The more correct of the two readings is the one upon which the common reciters agree, namely the kasra on the kaf, because of the consensus of the authoritative reciters upon it, and because kibr with a kasra is the verbal noun of "greatness" in matters, whereas kubr with a damma on the kaf is only from patronage and lineage, from their saying: "he is the kubr of his people" (i.e., the chief of his people). The kibr in this place is what we have described of the greater part of the sin and slander. Since this is so, the kasra on its kaf is the eloquent speech rather than its damma, although the damma has an understandable basis.

The people of interpretation have differed regarding who is meant by His words, ﴿and he who undertook the greater part of it among them﴾, the verse. Some of them said: it is Hassan ibn Thabit.

Those who said that:

◆ Al-Hasan ibn Qaza'ah narrated to us, saying: Maslamah ibn Alqamah narrated to us, saying: Dawud narrated to us, from Amir, that Aishah said: I have not heard anything more beautiful than the poetry of Hassan, and whenever I recited it I hoped Paradise for him, his saying to Abu Sufyan:

*You satirized Muhammad, so I answered on his behalf,*
*and with God is the recompense for that.*
*Indeed my father, his father, and my honour*
*are a shield for the honour of Muhammad from you.*
*Do you revile him, while you are not his equal?*
*So your evil is the ransom of your good.*
*My tongue is a sharp blade with no flaw in it,*
*and my sea is not disturbed by buckets.* [[These four verses are by Hassan ibn Thabit al-Ansari, the poet of the Messenger (ﷺ), satirizing Abu Sufyan ibn al-Harith ibn Abd al-Muttalib, the poet of Quraysh before his Islam. They are from his poem whose opening is: "The fingers' traces have worn away at al-Jawa..." The verses are near the end of the poem, and before them: "Let Abu Sufyan know from me, a message delivered, though the concealment has ceased..." (See the poem in Ibn Hisham's Sirah, Halabi edition, vol. 4, pp. 64–66.) The author cited it as evidence that Hassan was among those who engaged in the story of the slander by which the Mother of the Believers, Aishah, the innocent, was accused, may God be pleased with her.]]

It was said: "O Mother of the Believers, is this not idle talk?" She said: "No, idle talk is only what is said among women." It was said: "Does not God say: ﴿and he who undertook the greater part of it among them will have a great punishment﴾?" She said: "Has he not been struck by a great punishment? Has his sight not gone, and was he not struck with the sword?" [Kanaa bi al-sayf: he was struck with the sword until his skin dried out (Lisan al-Arab).]

◆ He said: Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Mu'ammal narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu al-Duha, from Masruq, who said: I was with Aishah when Hassan ibn Thabit entered, and she gave orders, and a cushion was placed for him. When he left, I said to Aishah: "Why do you do this, when God has said what He said?" She said: "God said: ﴿and he who undertook the greater part of it among them will have a great punishment﴾, and his sight has gone. Perhaps God makes that great punishment the loss of his sight."

◆ Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Abi Adi narrated to us, from Shu'bah, from Sulayman, from Abu al-Duha, from Masruq, who said: Hassan ibn Thabit entered upon Aishah and sang some verses of his, saying:

*"And she wakes up hungry from the flesh of the heedless."* [[This is the second half of a verse by Hassan ibn Thabit, from verses of his in praise of the Mother of the Believers Aishah, may God be pleased with her, after her innocence was revealed in Surah al-Nur, from the slander in which some of the Companions engaged, and Hassan was among the most engaged in it. When the truth became clear and the innocence of the Mother of the Believers was manifest, Hassan repented and apologized and said verses praising her. The first half of the verse is: "A chaste woman, dignified, who is not suspected of doubt." Hisan: chaste; razan: sedate and steadfast, one not moved by frivolity. Tazunnu: she casts suspicion and accuses. Rayba: accusation and doubt. Ghar-tha: hungry; he means she does not backbite women. Al-ghawafil: plural of ghafilah, one whose heart is heedless of evil (see Ibn Hisham's Sirah, Halabi edition, vol. 3, pp. 319–320).]]

Aishah said: "As for you, you are not like that." I said: "You allow this man to enter upon you, when God has revealed about him: ﴿and he who undertook the greater part of it﴾, the verse?" She said: "And what punishment is greater than blindness?" And she said: "He used to defend the Messenger of God (ﷺ)."

◆ Muhammad ibn Uthman al-Wasiti narrated to me, saying: Ja'far ibn Awn narrated to us, from al-Mu'alla ibn Irfan, from Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Jahsh, who said: Aishah and Zaynab boasted, and Zaynab said: "I am the one whose marriage was revealed from the heavens." He said: And Aishah said: "I am the one whose innocence was revealed in His Book when Ibn al-Mu'attal carried me on the camel." Zaynab said to her: "O Aishah, what did you say when you mounted it?" She said: "I said: 'God is sufficient for me, and He is the best Disposer of affairs.'" She said: "You said the word of the believers."

Others said: it was Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul.

Those who said that:

◆ Ibn Waki narrated to us, saying: Abu Usamah narrated to us, from Hisham ibn Urwah, from his father, from Aishah, who said: Those who spoke about it were the hypocrite Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul, who used to spread it and gather it, and he is the one who undertook the greater part of it; and Mistah, and Hassan ibn Thabit.

◆ Sufyan narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Bishr narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Hatib narrated to us, from Alqamah ibn Waqqas and others as well, who said: Aishah said: "The one who undertook its greater part was the one who gathered them in his house, Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul."

◆ Ibn Abd al-Ala narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Ibn Shihab, who said: Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, Alqamah ibn Waqqas, and Ubaydullah ibn Abdullah ibn Utbah narrated to me, from Aishah, who said: "The one who undertook its greater part was Abdullah ibn Ubayy."

◆ Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ibn Abbas said: ﴿Indeed those who came﴾, the verse: those who fabricated against Aishah were Abdullah ibn Ubayy, who undertook its greater part, and Hassan, and Mistah, and Hamnah bint Jahsh.

◆ Abd al-Warith ibn Abd al-Samad narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to us, saying: Aban al-Attar narrated to us, saying: Hisham ibn Urwah narrated to us regarding those who came with the slander; they allege that the greatest part of it was from Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul, one of the Banu Awf ibn al-Khazraj, and it was reported to me that he used to narrate it about them, and he would confirm it, listen to it, and spread it.

◆ Yunus narrated to us, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: As for the one who undertook its greater part among them, it is Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul the wicked; he is the one who began this speech, and said: "The wife of your Prophet spent the night with a man until morning, then he came leading her."

◆ Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "And he who undertook the greater part of it is Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul, and he was the one who began it."

The more correct of the two sayings is the saying of the one who said: the one who undertook the greater part of it among the band of the slander was Abdullah ibn Ubayy. This is because there is no disagreement among the people of biography (ahl al-sir) that the one who began mentioning the slander, and who used to gather his people and talk to them, was Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul; and his doing so, as I have described, constituted his undertaking the greater part of that matter.

The cause of the coming of the people of the slander was what Ibn Abd al-Ala narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Muhammad ibn Muslim ibn Ubaydullah ibn Abdullah ibn Shihab: Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, Alqamah ibn Waqqas, and Ubaydullah ibn Abdullah ibn Utbah ibn Mas'ud narrated to me, from the account of Aishah, wife of the Prophet (ﷺ), when the people of the slander said what they said to her, and God cleared her. All of them related to me a portion of her account, and some of them were more retentive of her account than others and more precise in its telling. I have retained from each of them the account they related to me from Aishah, and some of their account confirms some of the rest:

They claim that Aishah, wife of the Prophet (ﷺ), said: "When the Messenger of God (ﷺ) intended a journey, he would draw lots among his wives, and whichever lot came out, he would take her with him. Aishah said: He drew lots between us for a battle he fought, and my lot came out, so I went out with the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and that was after the veil had been revealed, and I was carried in my howdah and dismounted in it. We journeyed until the Messenger of God (ﷺ) finished his campaign and turned back toward Madinah. He announced the departure one night, so I got up when they announced the departure, and I walked until I passed the army. When I had finished my need, I came back to the saddle and touched my chest, and behold, my necklace of Zafar onyx had broken. So I returned and searched for my necklace, and its search detained me. Meanwhile the men who used to saddle for me came, and they lifted my howdah and fastened it on my camel which I used to ride, and they thought I was in it. Aishah said: The women at that time were light, not heavy, and flesh had not covered them; they ate only a small morsel of food. So the people did not notice the lightness of the howdah when they lifted and raised it. I was a young girl, so they drove the camel and set off. I found my necklace after the army had moved on, and I came to their camp, and there was no one there to call or to answer. So I headed to my place where I had been, thinking that the people would miss me and return to me. While I was sitting in my place, my eyes overcame me, and I slept until morning. Safwan ibn al-Mu'attal al-Sulami, then al-Dhakwani, had stayed behind the army; he set out at night and arrived at my place in the morning. He saw the shape of a sleeping person, so he came to me and recognized me when he saw me, for he had seen me before the veil was imposed upon me. I awoke at his reciting of 'Inna lillah' when he recognized me, so I covered my face with my outer garment. By God, I did not speak a word, nor did I hear from him any word except his reciting, until he made his mount kneel, and he stepped on its forelegs, and I mounted it. He set off leading the mount with me, until we reached the army after they had halted in the heat of midday. Whoever was destroyed was destroyed regarding my affair, and the one who undertook its greater part was Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul. We came to Madinah, and I fell ill for a month, while the people were spreading the saying of the people of the slander, and I was not aware of any of that. What troubled me in my illness was that I did not notice from the Messenger of God the gentleness I used to see from him when I was ill. He would only enter, greet, and say: 'How are you?' That troubled me, and I was not aware of the evil until I went out after I had recovered. I went out with Umm Mistah toward al-Manasi, which was our place for relieving ourselves, and we did not go out except at night to night, and that was before we took latrines close to our houses, and our custom was the old custom of the Arabs regarding the open country. [[This is how Imam Muslim narrated it in his Sahih (17:106) with the commentary of al-Nawawi. In the Sahih of al-Bukhari, Halabi edition (5:150): "al-Bariyyah before al-Ghait, in a place: al-tanazzuh."]] We used to be harmed by latrines close to our houses. I went out with Umm Mistah, who was the daughter of Abu Ruhm ibn Abd al-Muttalib ibn Abd Manaf, and her mother was the daughter of Sakhr ibn Amir, the maternal aunt of Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, and her son was Mistah ibn Uthathah ibn Abbad ibn al-Muttalib. I and the daughter of Abu Ruhm came toward my house when we had finished our need. Umm Mistah stumbled in her cloak and said: 'May Mistah perish!' I said to her: 'How evil what you said is! Will you revile a man who witnessed Badr?' She said: 'O you, have you not heard what he said?' I said: 'And what did he say?' So she told me the saying of the people of the slander, and I became more ill upon my illness. When I returned to my house, the Messenger of God (ﷺ) entered upon me and said: 'How are you?' I said: 'Will you permit me to go to my parents?' He said: 'Yes.' She said: I wanted at that time to verify the news from them. [[This is the narration of Muslim. In the Sahih of al-Bukhari (5:150): she said: "I want to be certain of the news from them." She said: "So he permitted me..." etc.]] So the Messenger of God (ﷺ) permitted me, and I went to my parents, and I said to my mother: 'O mother, what are the people talking about?' She said: 'O daughter, ease your mind, for by God, rarely has there been a beautiful woman with a man who loves her who has co-wives, without them making much of it against her.' I said: 'Glory be to God! Have the people really spoken of this, and has it reached the Messenger of God (ﷺ)?' She said: 'Yes.' So I wept that night until morning, my tears would not stop, and I could not close my eyes in sleep. Then in the morning Abu Bakr entered upon me while I was weeping, and he said to my mother: 'What is making her weep?' She said: 'She had not known what was said to her.' So he fell to weeping, and he wept for a while, then said: 'Be quiet, O daughter.' I wept that whole day, my tears would not stop and I could not close my eyes in sleep. Then I wept the following night; my tears would not stop and I could not close my eyes in sleep; then I wept the next night, my tears would not stop and I could not close my eyes in sleep, until my parents thought that weeping would split my liver."

So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ summoned ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib and Usāmah ibn Zayd when the revelation was delayed, consulting them about separating from his wife. She said: As for Usāmah, he advised the Messenger of Allah ﷺ according to what he knew of the innocence of his household and the affection he held for them, and said: "O Messenger of Allah, they are your family, and we know nothing but good." As for ʿAlī, he said: "Allah has not constricted you, and there are many women other than her. But ask the slave-girl and she will tell you the truth," meaning Barīrah. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ summoned Barīrah and said: "Did you see anything from ʿĀʾishah that made you doubt?" Barīrah said to him: "By the One who sent you with the truth, I never saw anything in her that I would find fault with, except that she is young in age; she sleeps and leaves the dough of her family, and then a domestic sheep comes and eats it."

The Prophet ﷺ then stood up to deliver a sermon, praised Allah and extolled Him as He is worthy, and then said: "Who will excuse me from a man whose harm has reached me regarding my family?" meaning ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy ibn Salūl. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ also said, while still on the pulpit: "O assembly of Muslims, who will excuse me from a man whose harm has reached me regarding my family? By Allah, I know nothing about my family but good. They have mentioned a man about whom I know nothing but good, and he never entered my household except with me."

Then Saʿd ibn Muʿādh al-Anṣārī stood up and said: "I will excuse you from him, O Messenger of Allah. If he is from the Aws, we will strike off his neck; and if he is from our brothers, the Khazraj, command us and we will carry out your command." Then Saʿd ibn ʿUbādah stood up, and he was the chief of the Khazraj, a righteous man, but zealous pride moved him. He said: "Be silent, O Saʿd ibn Muʿādh! By the life of Allah, you will not kill him, and you are not able to kill him." Then Usayd ibn Ḥuḍayr, who was the cousin of Saʿd ibn Muʿādh through his paternal aunt, stood up and said to Saʿd ibn ʿUbādah: "You lie! By the life of Allah, we will certainly kill him, for you are a hypocrite who argues on behalf of the hypocrites." The two tribes, the Aws and the Khazraj, rose up until they were about to fight each other, while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was standing on the pulpit. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ kept calming them down until they fell silent.

Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to me while I was in the house of my parents. While the two of them were sitting with me and I was weeping, a woman of the Anṣār asked permission to enter upon me. I permitted her, and she sat down weeping with me. She said: While we were in that state, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ entered upon us, then sat down with me. He had not sat with me since what was said had been said, and he had remained a month without any revelation coming to him concerning my matter.

She said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited the tashahhud when he sat down, then said: "Now then, O ʿĀʾishah, it has reached me that such-and-such was said about you. If you are innocent, Allah will certainly clear you; and if you have committed a sin, then ask Allah for forgiveness and repent to Him, for when a servant confesses his sin and then repents, Allah accepts his repentance."

When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ finished his speech, my tears dried up until I did not feel even a single tear. I said to my father: "Answer the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on my behalf concerning what he said." He said: "By Allah, I do not know what to say to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ." So I said to my mother: "Answer the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on my behalf." She said: "By Allah, I do not know what to say to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ." Then I said, and I was a young girl, not having memorized much of the Qurʾān: "Indeed, by Allah, I know that you have heard this, until it has settled in your souls and you have almost believed it. If I tell you that I am innocent, and Allah knows that I am innocent, you will not believe me. And if I confess to you a matter, and Allah knows that I am innocent of it, you will believe me. By Allah, I find no example for myself and for you except that of the father of Joseph," [[The Mother of the Believers, may Allah be pleased with her, did not mention the name of the Prophet Yaʿqūb, father of Yūsuf, peace be upon them both, because she was a young girl who had not yet memorized much of the Qurʾān]] ﴿So patience is most fitting; and it is Allah whose help is sought against what you describe﴾. Then I turned away and lay down on my bed, and by Allah, I knew that I was innocent and that Allah would clear me by my innocence. But by Allah, I never thought that a revelation would be sent down concerning my matter that would be recited. My affair was too insignificant in my own eyes for Allah to speak about me with a matter that would be recited. But I hoped that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would see a dream in which Allah would clear me.

She said: By Allah, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had not moved from his place, nor had anyone left the house, until Allah sent down revelation to His Prophet. He was seized by what he used to be seized by of the distress at the time of revelation, to the extent that drops like pearls of sweat poured from him even on a cold day, because of the weight of the word that had been revealed to him.

She said: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was relieved and was smiling, the first word he spoke was: "Rejoice, O ʿĀʾishah, for Allah has cleared you!" My mother said to me: "Get up and go to him." I said: "By Allah, I will not get up to him, nor will I praise anyone except Allah, who revealed my innocence."

So Allah revealed: ﴿Indeed, those who came up with the slander are a group among you﴾, ten verses. He revealed these verses as my innocence.

She said: Abū Bakr, who used to spend on Mistaḥ because of kinship and his poverty, said: "By Allah, I will never spend anything on him again after what he said about ʿĀʾishah." So Allah revealed: ﴿And let not those of virtue and wealth among you swear not to give to the near of kin﴾ up to: ﴿Forgiving and Merciful﴾. Abū Bakr said: "Indeed, I love that Allah should forgive me." So he returned to Mistaḥ the spending he used to give him, and said: "I will never withdraw it from him."

ʿĀʾishah said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to ask Zaynab bint Jaḥsh about my matter, and about what she had seen and heard. She said: "O Messenger of Allah, I protect my hearing and my sight; by Allah, I have seen nothing but good." ʿĀʾishah said: She was the one who used to compete with me, but Allah protected her through her piety. Her sister Ḥamnah began to fight on behalf of the slander, and she was destroyed among those who were destroyed.

Al-Zuhrī ibn Shihāb said: This is what has reached us concerning the matter of these people.

⁕ Ibn Ḥumayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Isḥāq, from al-Zuhrī, and from ʿAlqamah ibn Waqqāṣ al-Laythī, from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab, and from ʿUrwah ibn al-Zubayr, and from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿUtbah ibn Masʿūd. Al-Zuhrī said: Each of them has narrated to me part of this report, and some of the people had more retention than others. He said: I have gathered for you all that has been narrated to me.

⁕ Ibn Ḥumayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, saying: Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq also narrated to me, saying: Yaḥyā ibn ʿAbbād ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Zubayr narrated to us, from his father, from ʿĀʾishah, he said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Bakr ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr ibn Ḥazm al-Anṣārī also narrated to me, from ʿAmrah bint ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from ʿĀʾishah, she said: Each of them has combined in his report the story of ʿĀʾishah's account about herself, when the people of the slander said what they said about her. All of it has entered into her narration about all of these people. Some of them narrated what others did not narrate, and each of them was trustworthy regarding her, and each narrated what he heard from her.

ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, said: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ intended to travel, he would draw lots among his wives, and whichever wife's lot came out, he would take her with him. When the expedition of Banū al-Muṣṭaliq came, he drew lots among his wives as he used to do, and my lot came out, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ took me with him. She said: At that time, women used to eat only light food, and meat did not make them heavy. She said: When my camel was saddled, I would sit in my howdah, and then the people who saddled my camel would come and carry me. They would take hold of the bottom of the howdah, lift it, and place it on the back of the camel, and then set off with it.

She said: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ finished that journey, he turned back, and when he was near Medina, he stopped at a place and spent part of the night there, then he gave permission to the people to depart. When the people set out, I went out for some of my needs, and there was a necklace of mine made of Ẓafār onyx around my neck. When I finished, it slipped off my neck without my knowing. When I returned to the howdah, I went to look for it at my neck but did not find it, and the people had begun to depart. She said: I returned to the place where I had gone, searching for it until I found it. Meanwhile, the people who used to saddle my camel had come and carried the howdah, thinking I was in it.

Then he mentioned something similar to the report of Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā, from Ibn Thawr.

⁕ Ibn Wakīʿ narrated to us, saying: Abū Usāmah narrated to us, from Hishām ibn ʿUrwah, from his father, from ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, she said: When what was mentioned about me was mentioned, and what I knew of it, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood up to deliver a sermon. He recited the tashahhud, praised Allah and extolled Him as He is worthy, then said: "Now then, advise me concerning people who have slandered my family. By Allah, I know nothing about my family but evil ever, and they have slandered them with a man about whom, by Allah, I know nothing but evil ever. He never entered my house except that I was present, and I never went away on a journey except that he went with me."

Saʿd ibn Muʿādh stood up and said: "O Messenger of Allah, we think we should strike off their necks." A man from the Khazraj stood up, and the mother of Ḥassān ibn Thābit was from the kin of that man. He said: "You lie! By Allah, if they were from the Aws, you would not have liked us to strike off their necks until there almost arose evil between the Aws and the Khazraj in the mosque." And I did not know of this.

When it was evening that day, I went out for some of my needs, accompanied by the mother of Mistaḥ. She stumbled, and said: "Mistaḥ is ruined." I said: "Why do you curse your son?" She was silent. Then she stumbled a second time and said: "Mistaḥ is ruined." I said: "Why do you curse your son?" She was silent. Then she stumbled a third time and said: "Mistaḥ is ruined." I scolded her and said: "Why do you curse your son?" She said: "By Allah, I curse him only because of you." I said: "Because of what matter concerning me?" So she explained the report to me in detail. I said: "Has this really happened?" She said: "Yes, by Allah." She said: So I returned to my house, and it was as if what I had gone out for, I had not gone out for, and I did not find any of it, little or much. I fell ill, so I said: "O Messenger of Allah, send me to my father's house," and he sent a boy with me. I entered the house and there was my mother, Umm Rūmān. She said: "What brought you, my daughter?" I told her, and she said: "Calm yourself about the matter, for by Allah, there has never been a beautiful woman with a husband who loved her, who had co-wives, but they envied her and spoke about her." I said: "And has my father known of it?" She said: "Yes." I said: "And the Messenger of Allah?" She said: "Yes." So I wept and my tears flowed. Abū Bakr heard my voice while he was above the house reciting, so he came down and said to my mother: "What is the matter with her?" She said: "What was mentioned about her has reached her." His eyes overflowed, and he said: "I adjure you, return to your house."

So I returned. My parents were with me in the morning, and they stayed with me until the Messenger of Allah ﷺ entered upon me after the afternoon prayer, while my parents were on either side of me, on my right and on my left. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited the tashahhud, praised Allah and extolled Him as He is worthy, then said: "Now then, O ʿĀʾishah, if you have committed an evil or have been inclined toward a sin, then repent to Allah, for Allah accepts repentance from His servants." A woman from the Anṣār had come and was sitting, so I said: "Are you not ashamed before this woman to say something?" I said to my father: "Answer him." He said: "What should I say?" I said to my mother: "Answer him." She said: "What should I say?" When they did not answer him, I recited the tashahhud, praised Allah and extolled Him as He is worthy, then said: "Now then, by Allah, if I tell you that I did not do it, and Allah knows that I am truthful, it will not benefit me with you. Indeed, you have spoken of it and it has been imprinted on your hearts. And if I say that I did it, and Allah knows that I did not do it, you will certainly say: 'She has confessed to it against herself.' By Allah, I find no example for myself and for you except that of the father of Joseph, and I do not remember his name": ﴿So patience is most fitting; and it is Allah whose help is sought against what you describe﴾. Then Allah revealed to His Messenger at that very moment, and it was lifted from him, and I could see the joy in his face as he wiped his forehead, saying: "Rejoice, O ʿĀʾishah, for Allah has revealed your innocence." I had been at my most angry, and my parents said to me: "Get up and go to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ." I said: "By Allah, I will not get up to him, nor will I praise him or praise you both. You heard it and did not deny it or change it. But I praise Allah who revealed my innocence."

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to my house and asked the slave-girl about me. She said: "By Allah, I know of no fault in her, except that she used to sleep until a sheep would come in and eat her mat or her dough." One of his companions scolded her and said: "Tell the Messenger of Allah ﷺ the truth." ʿUrwah said: He became angry with the one who had said it, and said: "No, by Allah, I know of nothing in her except what a goldsmith knows of red gold ingot." That man who had been accused heard of it and said: "Glory be to Allah! I never uncovered the veil of any woman," and he was killed as a martyr in the way of Allah.

ʿĀʾishah said: As for Zaynab bint Jaḥsh, Allah protected her through her religion, so she said nothing but good. As for her sister Ḥamnah, she was destroyed among those who were destroyed. Those who spoke about it were: the hypocrite ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy ibn Salūl, who used to spread it and gather it, and he was the one who took the greatest part in it; Mistaḥ; and Ḥassān ibn Thābit. Abū Bakr swore that he would never benefit Mistaḥ with any benefit, so Allah revealed: ﴿And let not those of virtue and wealth among you swear not to give to the near of kin﴾, meaning Abū Bakr, ﴿and the needy﴾, meaning Mistaḥ, ﴿Would you not like Allah to forgive you? And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾. Abū Bakr said: "Yes, by Allah, we indeed love that Allah should forgive us." And Abū Bakr returned to Mistaḥ with what he used to do for him.

⁕ Ibn Wakīʿ narrated to us, saying: Muḥammad ibn Bishr narrated to us, saying: Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to us, saying: Yaḥyā ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ḥāṭib narrated to us, from ʿAlqamah ibn Waqqāṣ and others as well, saying: ʿĀʾishah went out intending to go to the al-madhhab [[al-madhhab: the place for relieving oneself outdoors]], and with her was the mother of Mistaḥ. Mistaḥ ibn Uthāthah was among those who had said what they said. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ had addressed the people before that, saying: "What do you think of the one who harms me regarding my family and gathers in his house the one who harms me?" Saʿd ibn Muʿādh said: "O Messenger of Allah, if he is from us, the men of the Aws, we will beat his head; and if he is from our brothers, the Khazraj, command us and we will obey you." Saʿd ibn ʿUbādah said: "O son of Muʿādh, by Allah, you have no support for the Messenger of Allah in this; rather, there were old grudges in the time of ignorance, and enmities that have not been removed from your hearts toward us." Ibn Muʿādh said: "Allah knows what you intended." Then Usayd ibn Ḥuḍayr stood up and said: "O son of ʿUbādah, Saʿd is not harsh, but you argue on behalf of the hypocrites and defend them." The clamor between the two tribes in the mosque increased, while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was sitting on the pulpit. The Prophet ﷺ kept gesturing with his hand to the people here and there until the noise subsided.

And ʿĀʾishah said: The one who took the greatest part in it, and the one who gathered them in his house, was ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy ibn Salūl. She said: I went out to the al-madhhab with the mother of Mistaḥ, and she stumbled and said: "Mistaḥ is ruined." I said: "May Allah forgive you! Do you say this about your son and about a companion of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ?" She said it twice, and she did not realize what had happened. Then I was told, and what I had gone out for left me, so that I did not find anything of it...

I returned to my parents, Abu Bakr and Umm Ruman, and said: "Did you not fear Allah? Will you not join my kinship?" The Prophet (ﷺ) had said what he said, and people had spoken of what they spoke of, and you did not tell me. So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was informed. She said: "My daughter, by Allah, a man rarely loved his wife without people saying to her things like what they said to you. My daughter, return to your house until we come to you there."

So I returned, and a fever seized me. My parents came in, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came and sat on my bed beside me. They said: "My daughter, if you did what people say, then ask Allah's forgiveness. If you did not do it, then tell the Messenger of Allah of your innocence."

I said: "I can find no one for me or for you except the father of Yusuf": ﴿So patience is most fitting, and Allah is the one sought for help against what you describe.﴾

She said: "I searched for the name of Ya'qub but could not find it, or I could not recall it." Then the eyes of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) fixed on the ceiling. Whenever revelation came down upon him, he would be seized by it. Allah says: ﴿Indeed, We will charge you with a heavy word.﴾ By Him who is most noble, and who sent down the Book upon him, he did not stop smiling until I could see his molars from joy. Then he wiped his face and said: "O Aisha, rejoice, for Allah has revealed your innocence." I said: "Praise be to Allah, not to you, nor to your companions."

Allah said: ﴿Indeed, those who came with the slander are a group among you﴾ ... until He reached ﴿And let not those of virtue and wealth among you swear against giving to the near of kin﴾. Abu Bakr had sworn that he would never benefit Mistah with anything, and there was kinship between them. When this was revealed: ﴿And let not those of virtue among you swear﴾ ... until He reached ﴿And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ Abu Bakr said: "Yes, my Lord, indeed." Then he returned to what he had given to Mistah.

﴿Indeed, those who accuse chaste, unaware, believing women﴾ ... until He reached ﴿Those are cleared of what they say; for them is forgiveness and noble provision.﴾

Aisha said: "By Allah, I did not expect that a revelation would descend concerning me, nor did I aspire to it. But I hoped that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would see a dream by which Allah would remove what was in his heart."

She said: "He questioned the Abyssinian slave girl, and she said: 'By Allah, Aisha is purer than refined gold. The only fault in her is that she sleeps until a sheep comes and eats her dough. If she had done what people say, she would surely have told you of it.'"

She said: "So the people marvelled at her understanding."

The explanation of His words, exalted be He: ﴿Why, when you heard it, did the believing men and believing women not think well of their own kind and say, "This is an obvious lie"?﴾

This is a reproof from God, exalted be His remembrance, to the people of faith concerning what occurred within their own souls of the rumour that the spreaders of rumour spread about the affair of ʿAʾisha. God, exalted be His remembrance, says to them: "Why, O people, when you heard what the people of the slander (ahl al-ifk) said about ʿAʾisha, did the believing men and believing women among you not think well of their own kind?" That is: you should have thought well of those among you who were accused of it, and should not have supposed that they had committed the grave sin. He said "their own kind" (bi-anfusihim) because all the people of Islam are like a single soul, since they are the people of one community (millah).

Something similar to what we have said has been said by the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil).

Those who said that:

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salama narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from his father, from some men of the Banu al-Najjar, that Abu Ayyub Khalid ibn Zayd was told by his wife Umm Ayyub: "Do you not hear what people are saying about ʿAʾisha?" He said: "Yes, and that is a lie. Would you have done such a thing, O Umm Ayyub?" She said: "No, by God, I would never have done it." He said: "Then ʿAʾisha, by God, is better than you." He said: When the Qur'an was revealed, God mentioned those who spoke the slander about the grave sin, as they said: ﴿Indeed, those who brought the slander are a group among you﴾, and that was Hassan and his companions who said what they said. Then He said: ﴿Why, when you heard it, did the believing men...﴾ ... the verse; that is, as Abu Ayyub and his wife had said.

Yunus narrated to us, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His words: ﴿Why, when you heard it, did the believing men and believing women not think well of their own kind﴾: "What is this good thought? The believer thought that a believer would not commit adultery with his mother, and that a mother would not commit adultery with her son. If he wished to commit adultery, he would commit it with someone other than his mother." He said: "ʿAʾisha was indeed a mother, and the believers are her sons, and it is forbidden for her to them." And he recited: ﴿Why did they not bring four witnesses for it?﴾ ... the verse.

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, concerning His words: ﴿the believing men and believing women thought well of their own kind﴾: he said, "well of them." Do you not see that He says: ﴿And do not kill yourselves﴾? He means: some of you kill others. And "greet your own selves": he said, let some of you greet others.

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Hawdha narrated to us, saying: ʿAwf narrated to us, from al-Hasan, concerning His words: ﴿Why, when you heard it, did the believing men and believing women not think well of their own kind﴾: he meant by that the believing men and believing women.

* *

As for His words: ﴿and say, "This is an obvious lie"﴾

That is: the believing men and believing women said: "What we have heard from these people, of the grave sin with which they have charged ʿAʾisha, is a lie and a sin, which is clear to whoever understands and reflects upon it, that it is a lie, a sin and a slander."

As:

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Hawdha narrated to us, saying: ʿAwf informed us, from al-Hasan: ﴿and say, "This is an obvious lie"﴾: they said, "It is not fitting that this be spoken except by one against whom four witnesses have been produced and upon whom the prescribed punishment for fornication has been carried out."

The Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is He: "Why did they not bring four witnesses for it? Since they did not bring the witnesses, it is they who are the liars in the sight of Allah" (24:13)

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: Why did this band who brought the slander, and who accused ʿĀʾishah of the calumny, not bring four witnesses who would testify to their claim about her and to what they accused her of,

and since they did not bring the four witnesses for the truth of what they accused her of, "then it is they who are the liars in the sight of Allah." He says: so the band who accused her of that are, in the sight of Allah, the liars in what they brought of the slander.

* *

The Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is He: "And were it not for the grace of Allah upon you and His mercy in this world and the Hereafter, a great punishment would have touched you for what you plunged into" (24:14)

His words: "And you say with your mouths what you have no knowledge of"

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: and you say with your mouths what you have no knowledge of, concerning the matter which you relate, saying: We heard that ʿĀʾishah did such-and-such, while you do not know the truth or soundness of it. "And you think it trivial": and you suppose that your saying that, your relating it with your tongues, and your receiving it from one another, is trivial and easy, with no sin or blame upon you in it. "And it is, in the sight of Allah, tremendous": he says: your receiving that thus and your saying it with your mouths is, in the sight of Allah, a tremendous matter; because you were by it causing hurt to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his beloved wife.

This is the commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 24, verse 16:

The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And why, when you heard it, did you not say, "It is not for us to speak of this; exalted are You [O Allah], this is a great slander"?﴾

His saying, may His remembrance be exalted: ﴿And why not﴾ — O you who plunge into the slander brought by a faction among you — ﴿when you heard it﴾ from those who brought it — ﴿did you not say﴾ that it is not lawful for us to speak of this, and it is not fitting for us to utter it — ﴿Exalted are You [O Lord]﴾, declaring You far above imperfection and disavowing to You what these people have brought — ﴿this is a great slander﴾. He means: this statement is a great slander.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 24, verse 17–19:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿God admonishes you never to return to the like of it, if you are believers. And God makes the signs clear to you, and God is All-Knowing, All-Wise﴾ (17–18).

His saying, exalted is He, means: God reminds you and forbids you through the verses of His Book, lest you return to the like of your action which you committed in the matter of ʿĀʾisha, namely your receiving of the slander that was spread against her by your tongues and your saying with your mouths what you have no knowledge of, ever. ﴿If you are believers﴾ means: if you are heeding the admonitions of God, obeying His command, and refraining from what He has forbidden you.

Those who have interpreted [the Qur'an] said the same as what we have said about this.

Mention of those who said that:

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying: ﴿And God makes the signs clear to you, and God is All-Knowing, All-Wise﴾: "And what is better for us than this is that God has informed us of this so that we would not fall into it. Had God not informed us of it, we would have perished as the people perished, [in that] a man would say: 'I heard it, and I did not invent it (ukhtariq) [[ikhtaraqa al-kadhib: like ikhtarʿa, iftaʿalahu, and ṣanaʿahu, meaning to fabricate it]] and I did not make it up.' So it was better that God informed us of it, so that we would never enter into the like of it, and it is great in God's sight." His saying: ﴿And God makes the signs clear to you﴾ means: God explains in detail His proofs against you through His command and His prohibition, so that the one among you who obeys Him may be distinguished from the one who disobeys. God is All-Knowing of you and your actions, nothing is hidden from Him, and He is the one who recompenses the good-doer among you for his goodness and the wrongdoer for his wrongdoing. He is All-Wise in the management of His creation, and in what He has imposed upon them of deeds and what He has made obligatory upon them of actions.

* *

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, those who love that indecency should spread among those who believe will have a painful punishment in this world and the Hereafter. And God knows, while you do not know﴾ (19).

His saying, exalted is He, means: Indeed, those who love that adultery should spread among those who have believed in God and His Messenger, and that it should become apparent among them. ﴿For them is a painful punishment﴾ means: for them is a painful punishment in this world, by the prescribed penalty (ḥadd) that God has set for the one who accuses chaste women and chaste men when they accuse them of that, and in the Hereafter the punishment of Hell if he dies persisting in that without repenting.

As [it is narrated]:

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, concerning His saying: ﴿love that indecency should spread﴾: "It appears concerning the matter of ʿĀʾisha."

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who love that indecency should spread among those who believe will have a painful punishment﴾: "The wretch ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul, the hypocrite, who spread about ʿĀʾisha what he spread of the slander against her." ﴿For them is a painful punishment.﴾

Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿĀṣim narrated to us, saying: ʿĪsā narrated to us; and al-Ḥārith narrated to me, saying: al-Ḥasan narrated to us, saying: Warqaʾ narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning His saying: ﴿that indecency should spread﴾: "It appears; it is talked about concerning the matter of ʿĀʾisha."

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And God knows, while you do not know﴾

His saying, exalted is He, means: God knows the falsity of those who brought the slander, and [knows] their truthfulness, while you, O people, do not know that, because you do not know the unseen; only the Knower of the unseen knows that. He means: do not transmit what you have no knowledge of of the slander against the people of faith in God, especially against the wives of the Messenger of God (ﷺ), lest you perish.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 24, verse 17–19:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿God admonishes you never to return to the like of it, if you are believers. And God makes the signs clear to you, and God is All-Knowing, All-Wise﴾ (17–18).

His saying, exalted is He, means: God reminds you and forbids you through the verses of His Book, lest you return to the like of your action which you committed in the matter of ʿĀʾisha, namely your receiving of the slander that was spread against her by your tongues and your saying with your mouths what you have no knowledge of, ever. ﴿If you are believers﴾ means: if you are heeding the admonitions of God, obeying His command, and refraining from what He has forbidden you.

Those who have interpreted [the Qur'an] said the same as what we have said about this.

Mention of those who said that:

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying: ﴿And God makes the signs clear to you, and God is All-Knowing, All-Wise﴾: "And what is better for us than this is that God has informed us of this so that we would not fall into it. So it was better that God informed us of it, so that we would never enter into the like of it, and it is great in God's sight." His saying: ﴿And God makes the signs clear to you﴾ means: God explains in detail His proofs against you through His command and His prohibition, so that the one among you who obeys Him may be distinguished from the one who disobeys. God is All-Knowing of you and your actions, nothing is hidden from Him, and He is the one who recompenses the good-doer among you for his goodness and the wrongdoer for his wrongdoing. He is All-Wise in the management of His creation, and in what He has imposed upon them of deeds and what He has made obligatory upon them of actions.

* *

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, those who love that indecency should spread among those who believe will have a painful punishment in this world and the Hereafter. And God knows, while you do not know﴾ (19).

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, concerning His saying: ﴿love that indecency should spread﴾: "It appears concerning the matter of ʿĀʾisha."

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: "And were it not for the bounty of Allah upon you and His mercy, and that Allah is Kind and Merciful" (24:20).

He, exalted is His mention, says: Were it not that Allah had shown favour to you, O people, and had shown you mercy, and that Allah is possessed of compassion and mercy toward His creatures, you would have been destroyed for what you plunged into, and Allah's punishment would have hastened upon you. The answer (to "were it not") is omitted because the hearer knows the meaning of the speech that follows it, namely His saying: "O you who have believed, do not follow the steps of Satan" (24:21) ... to the end of the verse.

**Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 24, verses 21–22**

*On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿O you who believe, do not follow the steps of Satan. And whoever follows the steps of Satan—indeed, he enjoins immorality and wrongdoing.﴾ (21)*

He, exalted is His remembrance, says to the believers in Him: O you who have affirmed that Allah and His Messenger are true, do not take the path of Satan or his ways, and do not follow his traces by spreading immorality among those who believe, and by your accepting it among them and transmitting that report from whoever brought it. Indeed, Satan enjoins immorality, which is fornication, and wrongdoing in speech.

We have already explained the meaning of "steps" (khutuwat) and "immorality" (fahsha') earlier, with their evidences, which suffices so that it need not be repeated in this place.

* *

*On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And were it not for the grace of Allah upon you and His mercy, none of you would ever have been purified, ever. But Allah purifies whom He wills, and Allah is Hearing and Knowing.﴾ (21)*

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: Were it not for Allah's grace upon you, O people, and His mercy toward you, none of you would have been purified from the filth of his sins and his polytheism, ever. But Allah purifies whom He wills of His creation.

Ahl al-ta'wil (the scholars of Qur'anic interpretation, tafsir) have said the same as what we have said concerning this.

Those who said so:

- Ali related to me, saying: Abdullah narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya related to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿And were it not for the grace of Allah upon you and His mercy, none of you would ever have been purified﴾ He said: None of you among the creatures would have been guided to any good by which he benefits himself, nor would he have guarded against any evil by which he averts it from himself.

- Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words: ﴿And were it not for the grace of Allah upon you and His mercy, none of you would ever have been purified﴾ He said: "Purified" (zaka) means "become Muslim." And he said: Everything in the Qur'an of the form "zaka" or "tazakka" means Islam.

* *

And His words: ﴿And Allah is Hearing and Knowing﴾

He says: Allah hears what you say with your mouths and what you utter with your tongues, and other than that of your speech; He knows all of that and other than it of your affairs, encompasses it, counts it against you, so that He may recompense you for all of it.

* *

*On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And let not those of virtue among you and wealth swear not to give to the near of kin and the needy and the emigrants in the cause of Allah. And let them pardon and overlook. Do you not like that Allah should forgive you? And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ (22)*

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: Let not those of virtue among you swear by Allah, meaning: those of bounty and abundance, that is, those of means.

The reciters differed regarding the recitation of His words ﴿wa-la ya'tali﴾. The majority of the reciters of the major cities read it as "wa-la ya'tali," meaning yaftaʿil, from al-ilya, which is swearing by Allah. Except Abu Ja'far and Zayd ibn Aslam, for it is reported from them that they recited it as "wa-la yata'all," meaning yatafa'al, from al-ilya.

The correct recitation in this regard, in my view, is the recitation of the one who reads "wa-la ya'tali," meaning yaftaʿil from al-ilya, because it is written thus in the consonantal text of the mushaf (codex), while the other recitation contradicts the writing of the mushaf. Following the mushaf together with the recitation of the majority of the reciters and the soundness of what is recited is preferable to opposing all of that.

It was specifically meant by this that Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him) swore by Allah that he would not spend on Mistah. So He, mighty is His praise, said: Let not those among you, O believers in Allah, who possess bounty and abundance of wealth, swear not to give to their kinsfolk, so that they might maintain their ties of kinship, such as Mistah, who was the son of Abu Bakr's maternal aunt. ﴿And the needy﴾ means those in state of need and poverty, and Mistah was among them, for he was poor and in need. ﴿And the emigrants in the cause of Allah﴾ are those who emigrated from their homes and wealth in struggle against the enemies of Allah, and Mistah was among them, for he was among those who emigrated from Mecca to Medina, and he witnessed Badr with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). ﴿And let them pardon﴾ means: let them pardon what was done to them of wrongdoing, such as the wrong Mistah did to Abu Bakr in spreading the slander about his daughter Aisha. ﴿And let them overlook﴾ means: let them abandon punishing them for that by withholding what they used to give them before, but rather return to them to the same kind of bounty they had bestowed upon them. ﴿Do you not like that Allah should forgive you?﴾ means: Do you not like that Allah should conceal your sins for you through your bounty toward them, so that He abandons punishing you for them? ﴿And Allah is Forgiving﴾ to the sins of one who obeys Him and follows His command, ﴿Merciful﴾ toward them, that He would not punish them while they follow His command and obey Him, for whatever slip or lapse they had, from which they have sought His forgiveness and repented to Him for doing it.

Ahl al-ta'wil have said the same as what we have said concerning this.

Those who said so:

- Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Salama narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from al-Zuhri, from Alqama ibn Waqqas al-Laythi, and from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, and from Urwa ibn al-Zubayr, and from Ubayd Allah ibn Abd Allah ibn Utba, from Aisha. He said: And Ibn Ishaq related to me, saying: Yahya ibn Abbad ibn Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr narrated to us, from his father, from Aisha. He said: And Ibn Ishaq related to me, saying: Abd Allah ibn Abi Bakr ibn Muhammad ibn Amr ibn Hazm al-Ansari related to me, from Amra bint Abd al-Rahman, from Aisha, who said: When this was revealed, meaning His words, ﴿Indeed, those who came with the slander are a group among you﴾, concerning Aisha and those who said what they said to her, Abu Bakr—who used to spend on Mistah because of his kinship and need—said: By Allah, I will never spend anything on Mistah, ever, nor benefit him with any benefit, after what he said to Aisha and what he brought upon her. She said: So Allah revealed concerning that: ﴿And let not those of virtue among you and wealth swear﴾ ... to the end of the verse. She said: Then Abu Bakr said: By Allah, I truly love that Allah should forgive me. So he restored to Mistah the spending that he used to give him, and said: By Allah, I will never withdraw it from him, ever.

- Ali related to me, saying: Abdullah narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya related to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿And let not those of virtue among you and wealth swear﴾ He said: Do not swear that you will not benefit anyone.

- Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: My father related to me, saying: My paternal uncle related to me, saying: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿And let not those of virtue among you and wealth swear﴾ ... to the end of the verse. He said: Some people among the companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had accused Aisha of the foul, and spread it and spoke of it. So some of the companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), among them Abu Bakr, swore that they would not give charity to a man who had spoken anything of this, nor would they maintain relations with him. So He said: Let not those of virtue among you and wealth swear that they will not maintain their ties of kinship and give them from their wealth as they used to do before that. So Allah commanded that they be forgiven and pardoned.

- I was told on the authority of al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words: ﴿And let not those of virtue among you and wealth swear﴾: When Allah, mighty is His remembrance, revealed the excuse for Aisha from the heavens, Abu Bakr and others among the Muslims said: By Allah, we will not maintain relations with any man among them who spoke anything about the affair of Aisha, nor will we benefit him. So Allah revealed: ﴿And let not those of virtue among you and wealth swear﴾, meaning: let them not swear.

- Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words: ﴿And let not those of virtue among you and wealth swear to give to the near of kin﴾ He said: Mistah was a relative. ﴿And the needy﴾ He said: He was needy. ﴿And the emigrants in the cause of Allah﴾: He was one of the people of Badr.

- Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿And let not those of virtue among you and wealth swear﴾ He said: Abu Bakr swore that he would not benefit an orphan in his care who had spread that (slander). When this verse was revealed, he said: Yes, I love that Allah should forgive me. So I will certainly be to my orphan the best I have ever been to him.
