He, exalted is His remembrance, says: Return, O believers, to the obedience of Allah regarding what He has commanded and forbidden you concerning lowering the gaze, guarding the private parts, and not entering houses other than your own without seeking permission and greeting, and other of His commands and prohibitions; ﴿that you may succeed﴾, meaning: that you may prosper and attain your aims with Him, if you obey Him in what He has commanded and forbidden you.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 24, verse 32:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿And marry off the single among you, and the righteous among your male servants and your female servants. If they are poor, Allah will enrich them from His bounty. And Allah is All-Encompassing, All-Knowing﴾ [24:32]

His, the Exalted's, remembrance says: Marry off, O believers, those who have no spouse, from your free men and women, and from the people of righteousness among your slaves and bondservants. Al-Ayama (the single ones) is the plural of ayim, and the plural of ayim is ayama, because it is a form (fa'ila) in meaning, so it is pluralized in that way, just as the orphan (yatima) is pluralized as yatama. From this is the verse of Jamil:

"I love the single women, since Buthayna became a widow, and I came to love the courtesans when they became wealthy."[[The verse is by Jamil al-Udhri, the companion of Buthayna, as the author said, and as in (Lisan: ghana). He said: al-ghaniya is the one who has become independent through a husband, and Jamil said: "I love the single women..." the verse. And the woman was enriched (ghaniya) by her husband, ghaniyan, meaning: she became self-sufficient. Al-ayama is the plural of ayim, and it originally refers to the one who has no husband, whether a virgin or a previously married woman, divorced or widowed (Lisan). And in the Mighty Revelation: {And marry off the single among you}: it includes the male and the female, and the virgin and the previously married. The author cited it as evidence that the ayim is the one who has no husband.]]

It would also be correct to pluralize it as aya'im, and ayim is applied to both male and female; it is said: a man is ayim, and a woman is ayim and ayima, if she has no husband. From this is the poet's saying:

"If you marry, I will marry, and if you remain single, I, though more advanced in age than you, will remain single."[[The verse was recited by the author of (Lisan) under ayim, and he said: a man remained single (ta'ayyama) for a time, and a woman remained single when they stayed for days and periods without marrying. Ibn Bari recited: "If you marry, I will marry, and if you remain single, (for the duration of time as long as you do not marry) I remain single." There is a difference in the version of the half-line between what the author recited and what Ibn Bari recited. The evidence in it, according to the author, as we mentioned in the previous evidence, is that the ayim among men or women is the one who has no spouse. Its verb is aama, yay'im, and ta'ayyama, yata'ayyam.]] ﴿If they are poor﴾ means: if these whom you marry off, from your single men and women, your slaves and your bondservants, are people of want and poverty, then Allah will enrich them from His bounty, so their poverty should not prevent you from marrying them off.

Those interpreters who spoke on this matter said things similar to what we have said.

Mention of those who said that:

* Ali narrated to me, saying: Abdullah narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿And marry off the single among you, and the righteous among your male servants and your female servants﴾, he said: Allah, glorified is He, commanded marriage, encouraged them to it, and commanded them to marry off their free persons and their slaves, and promised them wealth in that, so He said: ﴿If they are poor, Allah will enrich them from His bounty﴾.

* Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Hasan Abu al-Hasan narrated to us, and Isma'il ibn Subayh was his client, saying: I heard al-Qasim ibn al-Walid, from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, saying: Seek wealth through marriage; Allah says: ﴿If they are poor, Allah will enrich them from His bounty﴾.

* Yunus narrated to us, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words: ﴿And marry off the single among you﴾, he said: The single women are those who have no husbands.

* * *

As for His words: ﴿And Allah is All-Encompassing, All-Knowing﴾

His, the Majestic's, praise says: And Allah is vast in bounty, generous in His gifts. So marry off your female servants, for Allah is Encompassing; He will widen His bounty upon them, if they are poor. ﴿All-Knowing﴾ means: He has knowledge of the poor among them and the rich, and the state of His creatures in anything and their management is not hidden from Him.

**Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 24, verse 33 (part 1 of 2)**

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And let those who cannot find a marriage be chaste until Allah enriches them from His bounty. And those who seek a writing [of manumission] from among those whom your right hands possess, write it for them if you know good in them, and give them from the wealth of Allah which He has given you.﴾

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: ﴿And let those who cannot find﴾ the means to marry women be chaste, refraining from committing the immoralities that Allah has forbidden them, ﴿until Allah enriches them from His abundant bounty, and widens His provision for them.﴾

* *

And His words: ﴿And those who seek the writing from among those whom your right hands possess﴾

He, whose praise is exalted, says: those among your slaves who seek the mukatabah (contract of manumission) from you, ﴿write it for them if you know good in them.﴾ The scholars differed regarding the nature of a man's contracting (kitabah) with his slave in whom he knows good: is the words ﴿write it for them if you know good in them﴾ meant as an obligation (fard), or as a recommendation (nadb)? Some of them said: it is an obligation upon a man to contract with his slave in whom he knows good, if the slave asks him for that.

Mention of those who said this:

- Al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ibn Jurayj informed us, saying: I said to ʿAtaʾ: "Is it obligatory upon me, if I know wealth (in the slave), that I contract with him?" He said: "I do not see it as anything but obligatory." ʿAmr ibn Dinar also said this. He said: I said to ʿAtaʾ: "Do you transmit this from anyone?" He said: "No."
- Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Bakr narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Anas ibn Malik: that Sirin wished to contract with him, and he hesitated over it, so ʿUmar said to him: "You must contract with him!"
- Muhammad ibn Saʿd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: "It is not befitting for a man, if he has a righteous slave who has wealth, and he wants to contract with him, that he should not contract with him."

Others said: that is not obligatory upon the master; rather the words ﴿write it for them﴾ are a recommendation from Allah to the masters of slaves to contract with those among them in whom good is known, not a command.

Mention of those who said this:

- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Malik ibn Anas said: "The matter with us is that it is not incumbent upon the master of the slave to contract with him if he asks for that. I have not heard of any of the imams compelling anyone to contract with his slave. I have heard some of the scholars, when they were asked about this, and it was said to them: 'Allah, blessed and exalted is He, says in His Book: ﴿write it for them if you know good in them﴾,' reciting these two verses after it: ﴿And when you have come out of the state of ihram, then hunt﴾ and ﴿And when the prayer is concluded, disperse in the land and seek of Allah's bounty﴾." Malik said: "That is only a command by which Allah permitted the people, and it is not an obligation upon people, nor does it bind anyone." Al-Thawri said: "If the slave asks his master to contract with him, and the master wishes to contract with him, he may do so; the master is not compelled to do that."
- Ali narrated to me this, from Zayd, from him (al-Thawri). And Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿write it for them if you know good in them﴾: "It is not obligatory upon him to contract with him; this is only a command by which Allah permitted, and a guidance."

The more correct of the two views in my opinion is the view of the one who says: it is obligatory upon the master of the slave to contract with him if he knows good in him and the slave asks him for the mukatabah. This is because the apparent meaning of His words ﴿write it for them﴾ is an apparent command, and the command of Allah requires compliance, unless there is an indication from the Book or the Sunnah that it is a recommendation. I have already explained the reason for this in my book entitled al-Bayan ʿan Usul al-Ahkam (Clarification of the Foundations of the Rulings).

As for the good which Allah, exalted is His remembrance, commanded His servants to find in their slaves before contracting with them, it is the capacity to earn a living and to gain, so as to pay what they have been contracted to pay.

Mention of those who said this:

- Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Karim al-Jazari, from Nafiʿ, from Ibn ʿUmar, that he disliked contracting with his slave if the slave had no trade. He said: "He would feed me the filth of people."
- Ali narrated to me, saying: ʿAbd Allah narrated to us, saying: Muʿawiyah narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His words ﴿write it for them if you know good in them﴾, he said: "That is, if you know that they have a means (of earning), and do not place their maintenance upon the Muslims."
- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ashhab informed us, saying: Malik ibn Anas was asked about His words ﴿write it for them if you know good in them﴾, and he said: "It is said that the good is the capacity to pay."
- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd narrated to me, from his father, regarding the saying of Allah ﴿write it for them if you know good in them﴾, he said: "The good is the capacity for that."

Others said: rather, the meaning is: if you know in them truthfulness, fidelity, and payment.

Mention of those who said this:

- Yaʿqub narrated to me, saying: Ibn ʿUlayyah narrated to us, saying: Yunus informed us, from al-Hasan, regarding His words ﴿write it for them if you know good in them﴾, he said: "Truthfulness, fidelity, payment, and trustworthiness."
- He said: Ibn ʿUlayyah narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd Allah narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid and Tawus, that both of them said regarding His words ﴿write it for them if you know good in them﴾: "Wealth and trustworthiness."
- Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Jabir ibn Nuh narrated to us, saying: Ismaʿil ibn Abi Khalid narrated to us, from Abu Salih: ﴿write it for them if you know good in them﴾, he said: "Payment and trustworthiness."
- Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, saying: Shuʿbah narrated to us, from al-Mughirah, who said: Ibrahim used to say regarding this verse ﴿write it for them if you know good in them﴾: "Truthfulness and fidelity, or one of them."
- Abu Bakr narrated to us, saying: Ibn Idris narrated to us, saying: I heard ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Abi Sulayman, from ʿAtaʾ, regarding His words ﴿write it for them if you know good in them﴾, he said: "Payment and wealth."
- Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ibn Jurayj informed us, saying: ʿAmr ibn Dinar said: "I think it is all of that: wealth and righteousness."
- Ali ibn Sahl narrated to me, saying: Zayd narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us: ﴿if you know good in them﴾, meaning: truthfulness, fidelity, and trustworthiness.
- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿if you know good in them﴾: "If you know good in him for yourself, that he will pay you and be truthful to you about what he tells you, then contract with him."

Others said: rather, the meaning is: if you know that they have wealth.

- Muhammad ibn Saʿd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His words ﴿write it for them if you know good in them﴾, he says: "If you know that they have wealth."
- Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ibn ʿAbbas said: ﴿if you know good in them﴾: "Wealth."
- Ibn Bashshar and Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, both saying: ʿAbd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Shuʿbah narrated to us, from al-Hakam, from Mujahid: ﴿write it for them if you know good in them﴾, he said: "Wealth."
- Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, saying: Shuʿbah narrated to us, from al-Hakam, from Mujahid, the same.
- Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding the saying of Allah ﴿if you know good in them﴾, he said: "If they have wealth, then contract with them."
- Al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqaʾ narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the same.
- Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid: ﴿write it for them if you know good in them﴾, he said: "If you know that they have wealth, whatever their characters and religions may be."
- Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, saying: Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Mansur, from Zadhan, from ʿAtaʾ ibn Abi Rabah: ﴿write it for them if you know good in them﴾, he said: "Wealth."
- Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: Abu Bishr informed us, from Mujahid, who said: "If you know that they have wealth with them."
- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn ʿAmr al-Yafiʿi informed me, from Ibn Jurayj, that ʿAtaʾ ibn Abi Rabah used to say: "We do not see it as anything but wealth," meaning His words ﴿if you know good in them﴾. Then he recited: ﴿Prescribed for you, when death approaches one of you, if he leaves behind wealth (khayr)﴾.

The most correct of these views in my opinion is the view of the one who says: its meaning is: write it for them if you know in them strength for earning and gaining, and fulfilment of what they have bound themselves to and obligated themselves with, and truthfulness of speech. This is because these meanings are the causes for which the master of the slave needs them when he contracts with his slave, from what would be in the slave himself.

As for wealth, although it is a good, it is not in the slave himself; rather it is with him or belongs to him, not within him. Allah has only obligated us to contract with the slave if we know good in him, not if we know it is with him or belongs to him. Therefore, we have not said that the good in this context means wealth.

* *

And His words: ﴿and give them from the wealth of Allah which He has given you﴾

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: give them from the wealth of Allah which He has given you.

Then the interpreters differed regarding the one commanded to give from the wealth of Allah which He has given him: who is he? And regarding the wealth: which wealth is it? Some of them said: the one whom Allah commanded to give the contracted slave from the wealth of Allah is the master of the contracted slave, and the wealth of Allah from which he is commanded to give is the wealth of the contract (kitabah), and the amount he is commanded to give from it is a quarter.

Others said: rather, it is whatever the master wills of that.

Mention of those who said this:

- ʿAmr ibn ʿAli narrated to me, saying: ʿImran ibn ʿUyaynah narrated to us, saying: ʿAtaʾ ibn al-Sa'ib narrated to us, from Abu ʿAbd al-Rahman al-Sulami, from ʿAli, regarding the saying of Allah ﴿and give them from the wealth of Allah which He has given you﴾, he said: "A quarter of the contract."
- Al-Hasan ibn ʿArafah narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad al-Muharibi narrated to us, from ʿAtaʾ ibn al-Sa'ib, from Abu ʿAbd al-Rahman al-Sulami, from ʿAli, regarding His words ﴿and give them from the wealth of Allah which He has given you﴾, he said: "A quarter of the contract, which he remits from him."
- Yaʿqub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Ibn ʿUlayyah narrated to us, from Layth ibn Abi Sulaym, from Abu ʿAbd al-Rahman, from ʿAli, may Allah be pleased with him, regarding the saying of Allah ﴿and give them from the wealth of Allah which He has given you﴾, he said: "The quarter from its first installments."
- He said: Ibn ʿUlayyah informed us, saying: ʿAtaʾ ibn al-Sa'ib said, from Abu ʿAbd al-Rahman al-Sulami, from ʿAli, regarding His words ﴿and give them from the wealth of Allah which He has given you﴾, he said: "The quarter from his contract."
- Muhammad ibn Ismaʿil al-Ahmasi narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn ʿUbayd narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Abi Sulayman narrated to me, from ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Aʿyan, who said: Abu ʿAbd al-Rahman contracted with a boy for four thousand dirhams, then he remitted a quarter for him, and said: "Had I not seen ʿAli, may Allah's pleasure be upon him, contract with a boy of his and then remit a quarter for him, I would not have remitted anything for you."
- Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, saying: Shuʿbah narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Aʿla, from Abu ʿAbd al-Rahman al-Sulami: that he contracted with a boy of his for twelve hundred, then he left out the quarter and had me as a witness, and he said to me: "Your friend used to do this," meaning ʿAli, may Allah's pleasure be upon him, interpreting ﴿and give them from the wealth of Allah which He has given you﴾.
- Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Malik, who said: Fadalah ibn Abi Umayyah narrated to me, from his father, who said: "ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, contracted with me, and he borrowed for me two hundred dirhams from Hafsah." I said: "Will you not put it toward my contract?" He said: "I do not know whether I will live to see that."
- He said: ʿAbd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us: "It has reached me that he contracted with him for a hundred ounces." He said: Sufyan narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Malik, who said: "I mentioned that to ʿIkrimah, and he said: 'It is the saying of Allah: ﴿and give them from the wealth of Allah which He has given you﴾.'"
- Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Muʿawiyah narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding the saying of Allah ﴿and give them from the wealth of Allah which He has given you﴾, he said: "Remit from them part of their contract."
- Muhammad ibn Saʿd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas: ﴿and give them from the wealth of Allah which He has given you﴾, he said: "Remit from them part of what you agreed with them upon."
- Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Idris narrated to us, saying: I heard ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Abi Sulayman, from ʿAtaʾ, regarding His words ﴿and give them from the wealth of Allah which He has given you﴾, he said: "From what Allah has brought out for you from them."
- Abu al-Sa'ib narrated to me, saying: Ibn Idris narrated to us, from Layth, from Mujahid: ﴿and give them from the wealth of Allah which He has given you﴾, he said: "Give them from what is in your hands."
- Al-Husayn ibn ʿAmr al-ʿAnqazi narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from Asbat, from al-Suddi, from his father, who said: "Zaynab bint Qays ibn Makhramah, from the Banu al-Muttalib ibn ʿAbd Manaf, contracted with me for ten thousand, and I remitted one thousand for her, and Zaynab had prayed with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ facing both qiblahs."
- Mujahid ibn Musa narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Ibn Masʿud al-Jurayri informed us, from Abu Nadrah, from Abu Saʿid, the freedman of Abu Usayd, who said: "Abu Usayd contracted with me for twelve hundred, so I brought it to him, and he took a thousand from it and returned two hundred to me."
- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Harun ibn al-Mughirah narrated to us, from ʿAnbasah, from Salim al-Afťas, from Saʿid ibn Jubayr, who said: "When Ibn ʿUmar contracted with his contracted slave, he did not remit anything from the first installments, out of fear that he might fail, and then his charity would return to him. But when he was in the last part of the contract, he remitted what he wished."
- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Makhramah informed me, from his father, from Nafiʿ, who said: "ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUmar contracted with a boy of his called Sharaf for thirty-five thousand dirhams, and in the last part of his contract he remitted five thousand. Nafiʿ did not mention that he gave him anything other than what he remitted for him."
- He said: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Malik said: "I heard some of the scholars say: that a man contracts with his boy, then remits from the last part of his contract a specified amount." Malik said: "That is the best I have heard, and on that the scholars agree, and that is the practice of the people with us."
- Ali narrated to me, saying: Zayd narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us: "It is more beloved to me that he gives him a quarter, or something less than it, and it is not obligatory, and doing so is good."
- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from ʿAtaʾ, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Habib, Abu ʿAbd al-Rahman al-Sulami, from ʿAli, may Allah be pleased with him, regarding ﴿and give them from the wealth of Allah which He has given you﴾, he said: "It is a quarter of the contract."

Others said: rather, that is an exhortation from Allah to the owners of wealth to give them their share which He has assigned to them from the obligatory alms (sadaqat) upon their wealth, by His words: ﴿Alms are only for the poor and the needy, and those employed to collect them, and those whose hearts are to be reconciled, and for freeing captives (fi al-riqab)﴾. He said: "The captives (al-riqab) in whom one of the eight shares of the alms was placed are the contracted slaves." He said: "It is this that He, whose praise is exalted, meant by His words: ﴿and give them from the wealth of Allah which He has given you﴾, that is, their share of the alms."

Mention of those who said this:

- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Wadih narrated to me, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, from Ibn Zayd, from his father, regarding His words ﴿and give them from the wealth of Allah which He has given you﴾, he said: "Allah urges them to give it."
- Yaʿqub narrated to me, saying: Ibn ʿUlayyah narrated to me, saying: Yunus informed us, from al-Hasan, regarding ﴿and give them from the wealth of Allah which He has given you﴾, he said: "He urged the people to it, his master and others."
- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Mughirah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, regarding His words ﴿and give them from the wealth of Allah which He has given you﴾, he said: "He gives to his contracted slave and to others; he urged the people to it."
- Yaʿqub narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, from Mughirah, from Ibrahim, who said regarding His words ﴿and give them from the wealth of Allah which He has given you﴾: "He commanded his master and the people all together to help him."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 24, verse 33 (part 2 of 2):

⁕ Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Mughirah, from Ibrahim, regarding ﴿And give them of the wealth of God which He has given you﴾: He said: "He commanded the Muslims to give them from what God has given them."

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd narrated to me, from his father, regarding ﴿And give them of the wealth of God which He has given you﴾: He said: "That refers to zakat (obligatory alms) owed to the rulers. They give them from the zakat, as God says, ﴿and for the captives (fi al-riqab)﴾."

Ibn Zayd narrated to me, from his father, regarding ﴿And give them of the wealth of God which He has given you﴾: He said: "[It refers to] the fay' (spoils that come to the Muslims without battle) and the alms." He recited the words of God, ﴿Alms are only for the poor and the needy﴾, and recited until he reached ﴿and for the captives﴾. "So God commanded that they be paid from it. That is not from the contract (kitabah). My father used to say: 'What does it have to do with the contract? It is from the wealth of God, in which He has appointed a share for them.'"

Of the two opinions, the more correct in my view is the second, which is the view of those who said that it means giving them their share of the prescribed alms.

We said that this is the more correct of the two because His words, ﴿And give them of the wealth of God which He has given you﴾, are a command from God, exalted is He, to give the mukatabin (slaves contracted to purchase their freedom) from His wealth which He has given to the owners of wealth. And God's command imposes an obligation on His servants to comply with it, unless He informs them that He intends it as a recommendation. As we have explained in other places in our book, since that is so, and He has not informed us in His Book, nor through the tongue of His Messenger ﷺ, that it is a recommendation, it is a binding obligation. Since that is so, and the proof has been established that no one has a right to the property of another Muslim except what God has made obligatory for the people entitled to the shares of alms among the wealthy, and since the contract that the master of the mukatab requires from his mukatab is a portion of the master's property, it follows that the right which God has made obligatory upon the believers to give them from their wealth is what has been prescribed upon the wealthy in their property as the prescribed alms, since there is no right in their property for anyone other than that.

* *

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And do not compel your slave girls to prostitution, if they desire chastity, in order to seek the transient goods of this worldly life. And whoever compels them, indeed God, after their compulsion, is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ (24:33).

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: Marry off the righteous among your servants and your female slaves, and do not compel your female slaves to prostitution, which is fornication. ﴿If they desire chastity﴾ means: if they desire modesty and abstention from fornication. ﴿In order to seek the transient goods of this worldly life﴾ means: in order that you may seek, by compelling them to fornication, the transient goods of this worldly life, which is what their need for its ornaments, its adornments, and its wealth leads them to. ﴿And whoever compels them﴾ means: whoever compels his slave girls to prostitution, then indeed God, after their being compelled to that, is ﴿Forgiving and Merciful﴾ toward them, and the burden of what was done in that regard falls upon them (the compellers), not upon them (the women).

It has been mentioned that this verse was revealed concerning Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul, when he compelled his slave girl Musaykah to fornication.

Those who said that are:

⁕ Al-Hasan ibn al-Sabbah narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj ibn Muhammad narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Abu al-Zubayr informed me that he heard Jabir ibn Abdullah say: "Musaykah came to one of the Ansar and said: 'My master compels me to fornication.' So this was revealed concerning that: ﴿And do not compel your slave girls to prostitution﴾."

⁕ Yahya ibn Ibrahim al-Mas'udi narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to us, from his father, from his grandfather, from al-A'mash, from Abu Sufyan, from Jabir, who said: "There was a slave girl belonging to Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul, called Musaykah, and he hired her out or compelled her [al-Tabari is in doubt], so she came to the Prophet ﷺ and complained to him about that. So God revealed: ﴿And do not compel your slave girls to prostitution, if they desire chastity, in order to seek the transient goods of this worldly life, and whoever compels them, indeed God, after their compulsion, is Forgiving and Merciful﴾," meaning concerning them.

⁕ Abu Husayn Abdullah ibn Ahmad ibn Yunus narrated to us, saying: Abthar narrated to us, saying: Husayn narrated to us, from al-Sha'bi, regarding His words: ﴿And do not compel your slave girls to prostitution﴾, he said: "A man had a slave girl who committed fornication. When she embraced Islam, this was revealed."

⁕ Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Abu al-Zubayr informed me, from Jabir, who said: "A slave girl of one of the Ansar came and said: 'My master compelled me to prostitution,' so God revealed concerning that: ﴿And do not compel your slave girls to prostitution﴾." Ibn Jurayj said: Amr ibn Dinar informed me, from Ikrimah, who said: "A slave girl of Abdullah ibn Ubayy, he commanded her to fornicate, so she fornicated and came with a cloak, and he said to her: 'Go back and fornicate again.' She said: 'By God, I will not do that. If this is good, I have already had much of it, and if it is evil, it is time for me to abandon it.'" Ibn Jurayj said: Mujahid said something similar, and added: "He said: 'Al-bigha' is fornication.'" ﴿And God is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [means]: toward those women compelled to fornication, and this verse was revealed concerning them.

⁕ Al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, that a man from Quraysh was taken captive on the day of Badr, and Abdullah ibn Ubayy had taken him captive. Abdullah had a slave girl called Mu'adhah, and the Qurayshi captive wanted her for himself. She was a Muslim, so she resisted him because of her Islam, and Ibn Ubayy compelled her to that and beat her, hoping that she would become pregnant by the Qurayshi, so that he would ask for a ransom for his child. So God said: ﴿And do not compel your slave girls to prostitution, if they desire chastity﴾. Al-Zuhri said: ﴿And whoever compels them, indeed God, after their compulsion, is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ means: Forgiving to them for what they were compelled to.

⁕ Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Ash'ath, from Ja'far, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, that he used to recite: "fa-inna Allaha min ba'di ikrahihinna lahunna ghafurun rahim" (with lahunna placed before ghafur).

⁕ Ali narrated to us, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿And do not compel your slave girls to prostitution, if they desire chastity﴾: He said: "Do not compel your female slaves to fornication. If you do, indeed God, exalted is He, is Forgiving and Merciful toward them, and the sin of them is upon the one who compelled them."

⁕ Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿And do not compel your slave girls to prostitution﴾ ... to the end of the verse. He said: "In the pre-Islamic period they used to compel their female slaves to fornication and would take their earnings. So God said: 'Do not compel them to fornication for the sake of the gain of this worldly life.' ﴿And whoever compels them, indeed God, after their compulsion, is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ toward them, meaning if they are compelled."

⁕ Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿And do not compel your slave girls to prostitution﴾, "to fornication": "Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul commanded a slave girl of his to fornicate, so she brought him a dinar or a cloak [Abu Asim is in doubt], and he took it from her, then said: 'Go back and fornicate with another.' She said: 'By God, I will not go back.' So God is Forgiving and Merciful toward the women compelled to fornication, and this verse was revealed concerning that."

⁕ Al-Harith narrated to me, saying: Al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, similarly, except that in his narration he said: "He commanded a slave girl of his to fornicate, so she fornicated and brought him a cloak, and he accepted it," and he did not express doubt.

⁕ It was related to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say, regarding His words: ﴿And do not compel your slave girls to prostitution﴾, "to fornication." ﴿Indeed God, after their compulsion, is Forgiving and Merciful﴾, "Forgiving toward them, toward the women compelled to fornication."

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words: ﴿And whoever compels them, indeed God, after their compulsion, is Forgiving and Merciful﴾: "Forgiving and Merciful toward them when they were compelled and forced into that."

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, who said: "They used to order their young slave girls to engage in prostitution, and they would do so and earn money, and then bring them their earnings. Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul had a slave girl who used to engage in prostitution. She refused and swore she would not do it, so her people compelled her, and she went and engaged in prostitution and brought them a green cloak. So God, blessed and exalted, revealed: ﴿And do not compel your slave girls to prostitution﴾ ... the verse."

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿And We have certainly sent down to you clear verses, and an example from those who passed away before you, and an admonition for the righteous﴾

Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says: And We have sent down to you, O people, proofs and signs that are clear, meaning that they distinguish the truth from falsehood and make it evident.

The reciters differed over the reading of this word. The majority of the reciters of Medina, and some of the Kufans and Basrans, read *mubayyanāt* (مُبَيَّنَاتٍ) with a fatha on the *yā'*, meaning "made distinct," that is, Allah has distinguished them and made them clear to His servants, so they are distinct and clarified. The majority of the reciters of Kufa read *mubayyinātin* (مُبَيِّنَاتٍ) with a kasra on the *yā'*, meaning that the verses are what make the truth and right clear to people and guide them to the truth.

The correct view on this matter, in our opinion, is that both are well-known recitational variants (qira'at), each has been read by scholars of the reciters, and their meanings are close. When Allah distinguished them and made them clear, they became clear in themselves, showing the truth to whoever seeks it from them. And when they make that clear to whoever seeks it from them, Allah makes it clear within them. So whichever of the two readings a reciter uses, he is correct in his recitation.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿and an example from those who passed away before you﴾

From the nations. ﴿And an admonition﴾ for whoever fears Allah, meaning who fears His punishment and dreads His torment.

The Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 24, verse 35 (part 1 of 2):

On the interpretation (ta'wil) of His words, exalted is He: ﴿God is the Light of the heavens and the earth. His light is like a niche wherein is a lamp, the lamp in a glass, the glass as if it were a shining star, kindled from a blessed tree, an olive that is neither of the east nor of the west, whose oil would almost glow even if no fire touched it. Light upon light. God guides to His light whom He wills. And God presents parables for people, and God is Knower of all things.﴾ (35)

He, exalted is His remembrance, means by His words ﴿God is the Light of the heavens and the earth﴾: the Guide of those in the heavens and the earth. By His light they are guided to the truth, and by His guidance they are protected from the bewilderment of error.

The people of ta'wil differed regarding the interpretation of this. Some of them said something similar to what we have said.

Mention of those who said that:

- Ali narrated to me, saying: Abdullah narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words ﴿God is the Light of the heavens and the earth﴾: he said, God, glory be to Him, is the Guide of the people of the heavens and the earth.
- Sulayman ibn Umar ibn Khalda al-Raqqi narrated to me, saying: Wahb ibn Rashid narrated to us, from Farqad, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: Indeed my God says: "My light is My guidance."

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: God is the Manager (mudabbir) of the heavens and the earth.

Mention of those who said that:

- al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, who said: Mujahid and Ibn Abbas said regarding His words ﴿God is the Light of the heavens and the earth﴾: He manages the affair in them, their stars, their sun, and their moon.

Others said: Rather, by light is meant brightness (ḍiyaʾ). They said: the meaning of that is: the brightness of the heavens and the earth.

Mention of those who said that:

- Abd al-A'la ibn Wasil narrated to me, saying: Ubaydullah ibn Musa narrated to us, saying: Abu Ja'far al-Razi narrated to us, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, from Abu al-Aliyah, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, regarding God's words ﴿God is the Light of the heavens and the earth﴾: he said: He began with the light of Himself, mentioning it, and then mentioned the light of the believer.

We only chose the view we have chosen because it comes after His words: ﴿And We have certainly sent down to you verses that are clear, and an example from those who passed away before you, and an admonition for the God-fearing﴾. So it is more fitting that it be a report about a place where His revelation descends upon His creation. And whatever praise begins with the mention of its praise is more appropriate and more fitting, unless something comes from elsewhere indicating the conclusion of the report about it. If that is so, then the interpretation of the speech is: And We have certainly sent down to you, O people, verses that clarify the truth from falsehood, ﴿and an example from those who passed away before you, and an admonition for the God-fearing﴾, so We have guided you by them, and clarified for you the landmarks of your religion by them, because I am the Guide of the people of the heavens and the people of the earth. He omitted connecting the speech with the lam, and began the report about the guidance of His creation as a fresh beginning. Within it is the meaning I mentioned, being sufficient through the indication of the speech upon it without mentioning it. Then He began the report about the likeness of His guidance of His creation through the clear verses that He sent down to them, saying: ﴿His light is like a niche wherein is a lamp﴾, meaning: the likeness of what He illuminated of the truth through this revelation in its clarification is like a niche.

The people of ta'wil have differed regarding what the pronoun in His words ﴿His light﴾ refers to, and from what it refers back to. Some of them said: it refers to the believer. They said: the meaning of the speech is: the likeness of the believer's light, which is in his heart from faith and the Qur'an, is like a niche.

Mention of those who said that:

- Abd al-A'la ibn Wasil narrated to us, saying: Ubaydullah ibn Musa narrated to us, saying: Abu Ja'far al-Razi informed us, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, from Abu al-Aliyah, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, regarding God's words ﴿His light﴾: he said: He mentioned the light of the believer, saying: "His light," meaning the likeness of the light of the believer. He said: Ubayy used to recite it: "Thus is the likeness of the believer." He said: It is the believer in whose breast God has placed faith and the Qur'an.
- al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Abu Ja'far al-Razi, from Abu al-Aliyah, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b: ﴿God is the Light of the heavens and the earth. His light﴾. He said: He began with the light of Himself, mentioning it, then said: ﴿His light﴾, meaning: the likeness of the light of the one who believed in Him. He said: Thus Ubayy used to recite. He said: It is a servant in whose breast God has placed the Qur'an and faith.
- Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, regarding ﴿His light﴾: he said: the likeness of the believer's light.
- Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Azdi narrated to me, saying: Yahya ibn al-Yaman narrated to us, from Abu Sinan, from Thabit, from al-Dahhak, regarding His words ﴿His light﴾: he said: the light of the believer.

Others said: Rather, by the light is meant Muhammad (ﷺ), and they said: the pronoun in His words ﴿His light﴾ refers back to the name of God.

Mention of those who said that:

- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Ya'qub al-Qummi narrated to us, from Hafs, from Shimr, who said: Ibn Abbas came to Ka'b al-Ahbar and said to him: Tell me about the words of God, mighty and majestic: ﴿God is the Light of the heavens and the earth﴾... the verse? Ka'b said: God is the Light of the heavens and the earth. His light is like the likeness of Muhammad (ﷺ) as a niche.
- Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Azdi narrated to me, saying: Yahya ibn al-Yaman narrated to us, from Ash'ath, from Ja'far ibn Abi al-Mughira, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, regarding His words ﴿His light﴾: he said: Muhammad (ﷺ).

Others said: Rather, what is meant by that is the guidance of God and His clarification, which is the Qur'an. They said: the pronoun refers to the mention of God. They said: the meaning of the speech is: God is the Guide of the people of the heavens and the earth through His clear verses, and they are the light by which the heavens and the earth are illuminated. Their likeness, His guidance and His verses by which He guided His creation and admonished them, in the hearts of the believers, is like a niche.

Mention of those who said that:

- Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿His light﴾: its likeness is His guidance in the heart of the believer.
- Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Ibn Ulayyah narrated to us, from Abu Raja', from al-Hasan, regarding His words ﴿His light﴾: he said: the likeness of this Qur'an in the heart is like a niche.
- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿His light﴾: the light of the Qur'an which was sent down to His Messenger and His servants; this is the likeness of the Qur'an ﴿like a niche wherein is a lamp﴾.
- He said: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Abd Allah ibn Ayyash informed me, saying: Zayd ibn Aslam said regarding God's words, blessed and exalted is He: ﴿God is the Light of the heavens and the earth. His light﴾: and His light is what the Qur'an mentioned, and its likeness is what was struck as an example for it.

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: the likeness of God's light. They said: by the light is meant obedience.

Mention of those who said that:

- Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: Bi narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿God is the Light of the heavens and the earth. His light is like a niche wherein is a lamp﴾: That is because the Jews said to Muhammad: How can the light of God come out without the sky? So God struck the likeness of that for His light, saying: ﴿God is the Light of the heavens and the earth. His light is like a niche﴾. He said: It is a likeness God struck for His obedience, so He named His obedience light, and then named it lights of various kinds.

* *

His words: ﴿like a niche﴾

The people of ta'wil differed regarding the meaning of the mishkat (niche) and the misbah (lamp), what is meant by them, and by the zujajah (glass). Some of them said: the mishkat is every window with no opening through it. They said: this is a likeness God struck for the heart of Muhammad (ﷺ).

Mention of those who said that:

- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Ya'qub narrated to us, from Hafs, from Shimr, who said: Ibn Abbas came to Ka'b al-Ahbar and said to him: Tell me about God's words: ﴿His light is like a niche﴾. He said: The mishkat, which is the window (kuwwa), God struck as a likeness for Muhammad (ﷺ). The mishkat ﴿wherein is a lamp﴾: his heart. The lamp ﴿in a glass﴾: his breast. The glass ﴿as if it were a shining star﴾: he likened the breast of the Prophet (ﷺ) to a shining star. Then the lamp returned to his heart, and He said: ﴿kindled from a blessed tree, an olive that is neither of the east nor of the west﴾: it is not touched by the sun of the east nor the sun of the west. ﴿Its oil would almost glow﴾: Muhammad almost makes it clear to people, even if he does not speak, that he is a Prophet, just as that oil almost glows. ﴿Even if no fire touched it. Light upon light.﴾
- Ali narrated to me, saying: Abdullah narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, His words: ﴿like a niche﴾: he said: the place of the wick.
- Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, His words: ﴿God is the Light of the heavens and the earth, like a niche﴾: he said: The mishkat is the window of the house.

Others said: By the mishkat is meant the breast of the believer, by the lamp: the Qur'an and faith, and by the glass: his heart.

Mention of those who said that:

- Abd al-A'la ibn Wasil narrated to me, saying: Ubaydullah ibn Musa narrated to us, saying: Abu Ja'far al-Razi informed us, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, from Abu al-Aliyah, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b: ﴿His light is like a niche wherein is a lamp﴾: he said: the likeness of the believer, in whose breast God has placed faith and the Qur'an, like a niche. He said: The mishkat is his breast. ﴿Wherein is a lamp﴾: he said: the lamp is the Qur'an and faith which were placed in his breast. ﴿The lamp in a glass﴾: he said: the glass is his heart. ﴿The glass as if it were a shining star kindled﴾: he said: so his likeness, in which the Qur'an and faith shine, is as if it were a shining star, meaning: luminous. ﴿Kindled from a blessed tree﴾: the blessed tree is its root, the blessing of sincerity to God alone and worshipping Him, with no partner. ﴿Neither of the east nor of the west﴾: he said: its likeness is like a tree enclosed by trees, so it is green and soft, and the sun does not reach it in any state, neither when it rises nor when it sets. Likewise this believer is protected from anything of the outside reaching him. He has been tested with them, and God has made him firm in them. He is among four qualities: if he is given, he gives thanks; if he is tested, he is patient; if he judges, he is just; if he speaks, he is truthful. He is among the people like a living man walking among the graves of the dead. He said: ﴿Light upon light﴾: he moves within five kinds of light: his speech is light, his deeds are light, his entrance is light, his exit is light, and his destination on the Day of Resurrection is light, in Paradise.
- al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn al-Yaman narrated to me, from Abu Ja'far al-Razi, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, from Abu al-Aliyah, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: The mishkat is the breast of the believer. ﴿Wherein is a lamp﴾: he said: the Qur'an.
- He said: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Abu Ja'far, from al-Rabi', from Abu al-Aliyah, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, similar to the report of Abd al-A'la, from Ubayd Allah.
- Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿His light is like a niche﴾: he said: its likeness is His guidance in the heart of the believer, as the pure oil almost glows before the fire touches it. When the fire touches it, its light increases, light upon light. Likewise is the heart of the believer: he acts by guidance before knowledge comes to him, and when knowledge comes to him, his guidance increases, guidance upon guidance and light upon light. As Abraham, may God's blessings be upon him, said before knowledge reached him: ﴿This is my Lord﴾, when he saw the star without anyone informing him that there was a Lord. When God informed him that He was his Lord, his guidance increased upon guidance.
- Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, His words: ﴿God is the Light of the heavens and the earth. His light is like a niche wherein is a lamp﴾: That is because the Jews said to Muhammad (ﷺ): How can the light of God come out without the sky? So God struck the likeness of that for His light, saying: ﴿God is the Light of the heavens and the earth. His light is like a niche wherein is a lamp﴾. The mishkat: the window of the house, wherein is a lamp, ﴿the lamp in a glass, the glass as if it were a shining star﴾. The misbah: the lamp that is in the glass, and it is a likeness God struck for His obedience, so He named His obedience light and named it kinds of various lights.

* *

His words: ﴿kindled from a blessed tree, an olive, neither of the east﴾

He said: It is a tree upon which no shade of the east or shade of the west falls, exposed to the sun. That is purer for the oil. [[In the original: al-zayt, without a preceding lam, and I suspect it is a distortion of what we have set down.]] ﴿Whose oil would almost glow even if no fire touched it.﴾ Mu'ammar said, and al-Hasan said: It is not from the trees of this world, it is neither eastern nor western.

Others said: It is a likeness for the believer, except that the lamp and what is in it is a likeness for his heart, and the niche is a likeness for his inner body.

Mention of those who said that:

- al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, who said: Mujahid and Ibn Abbas both said: The lamp and what is in it is a likeness of the heart and inner body of the believer. The lamp is like the heart, and the window is like the inner body.
- Ibn Juraij said: ﴿Like a niche﴾: a window that is not through-going. Ibn Juraij said, and Ibn Abbas said: His words ﴿light upon light﴾ mean: the faith of the believer and his deeds.

Others said: Rather, that is a likeness for the Qur'an in the heart of the believer.

Mention of those who said that:

- Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Ibn Ulayyah narrated to us, from Abu Raja', from al-Hasan, regarding His words: ﴿God is the Light of the heavens and the earth. His light is like a niche﴾: he said: like a window ﴿wherein is a lamp, the lamp in a glass, the glass as if it were a shining star﴾.
- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding God's words: ﴿God is the Light of the heavens and the earth. His light﴾: the light of the Qur'an that was sent down to His Messenger and His servants. So this is the likeness of the Qur'an ﴿like a niche wherein is a lamp, the lamp in a glass﴾. He recited until he reached: ﴿blessed﴾. So this is the likeness of the Qur'an, by whose light they are illumined, they know it, and they take hold of it. It is as it is, not diminished. This is a likeness God struck for His light. Regarding His words: ﴿Its oil would almost glow﴾, he said: the glow is the radiance of that oil, and the niche is that in which is the wick in which is the lamp, and the lamps are those lights.
- Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Sa'id ibn Iyad, regarding His words: ﴿like a niche﴾: he said: the window.
- Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abu Amir narrated to us, saying: Qurrah narrated to us, from Ata', regarding His words: ﴿like a niche﴾: he said: Ibn Umar said: the mishkat is the window.

Others said: The mishkat is the lamp stand (qandil).

Mention of those who said that:

- Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding God's words: ﴿like a niche﴾: he said: the lamp stand, then the pillar upon which the lamp stand is.
- al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿like a niche﴾: the brass that is in the hollow of the lamp stand.
- Ishaq ibn Shahin narrated to me, saying: Khalid ibn Abd Allah narrated to us, from Dawud, from a man, from Mujahid, who said: The mishkat is the lamp stand.

Others said: The mishkat is the iron to which the lamp stand is hung.

Mention of those who said that:

- Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: Dawud ibn Abi Hind narrated to us, from Mujahid, who said: The mishkat is the iron rods by which the lamp stand is hung.

The most correct of these opinions, in my view, is the opinion of the one who said: this is a parable God coined for the Qur'an in the heart of the believers in it. He said: the likeness of God's light by which He illuminated for His servants the path of guidance, which He sent down to them, so they believed in it and affirmed what is in it, is in the hearts of the believers like a niche (mishkat), which is the pillar of the lamp in which the wick is, and this is the counterpart of the alcove that is in walls that have no opening. God only made that pillar a niche because it is not penetrating, and it is hollow with an open top, so it is like the alcove in the wall that does not go through. Then He said: ﴿in it is a lamp﴾, which is the lantern, and He made the lantern, which is the lamp, a parable for the Qur'an and the clear signs in the heart of the believer. Then He said: ﴿the lamp is in a glass﴾, meaning: the lantern that is in the niche, in the lamp-holder, which is the glass, and this is a parable for the Qur'an. He says: the Qur'an that is in the heart of the believer, whose heart God has illuminated within his breast. Then He likened the breast, in its purity from unbelief in God and doubt about Him, and its being illuminated by the light of the Qur'an, and its being lit by the clear signs of its Lord and its admonitions, to the shining star, so He said: ﴿the glass﴾, and that is the breast of the believer in which is his heart, ﴿as if it were a glittering star (kawkab durri)﴾.

The readers differed in the recitation of His saying ﴿durri﴾. The common readers of the Hijaz recited it ﴿durriyyun﴾ with a damma on the dal and without the hamza. Some readers of Basra and Kufa recited "dirri'," with a kasra on the dal and a hamza, and some readers of Kufa recited "durri'," with a damma on the dal and a hamza. It seems that those who read it with a damma on its dal and without the hamza directed its meaning to what the people of exegesis said, which we have mentioned from them, that the glass in its clarity and beauty is like a pearl (durr), and that it is attributed to it for that reason, from its description and attributes. Those who read it with a kasra on its dal and a hamza directed it to its being a form of fa'il from durri'a al-kawkab, meaning it was pushed away and a devil was pelted with it, from His saying ﴿and He repels from it the punishment﴾, meaning He repels. The Arabs call the great stars whose names are unknown "al-darari" without hamza. Some scholars of Arabic speech from Basra used to say: they are al-darari' with hamza, from yadra'n. As for those who read it with a damma on its dal and a hamza, if they meant it as durru'un like subbuhun and quddusun from dara'tu, then they disliked the many dammas in it, so they changed some of them to a kasra, saying dirri'," as it was said: ﴿and I have reached extreme old age (utiyyan)﴾, which is fu'ul from 'utawtu 'utuwwan, then some of its dammas were changed to kasra, so it was said 'itiyyan. This is a school of thought. Otherwise, I do not know a valid direction for their reading in this way, because fa'il is not known in Arabic speech, and some Arabic scholars used to say it is a lahn (solecism).

The most correct of the readings in my view is the reading of the one who read ﴿durriyyun﴾ with a damma on its dal and without its hamza, as a nisba to the pearl (durr), because the people of interpretation came with its interpretation, and we have mentioned their opinions on that before, so this suffices without citing other evidence for its soundness. The meaning of the speech is: the glass, which is the breast of the believer, as if it were a star, meaning as if the glass, which is a parable for the breast of the believer, is a star, in its clarity, brightness and beauty. He describes his breast as pure from every doubt and suspicion regarding the grounds of faith in God, and distant from the filth of sins, like the star that resembles a pearl in clarity, brightness and beauty.

They also differed regarding the recitation of His saying: "tuqadu min shajaratin mubarakah." Some Meccan and Medinan readers and some Basran readers recited it "tawaqqadu min shajaratin," with a ta' and a fatha, a shadda on the qaf and a fatha on the dal, and it seems they directed its meaning to the lamp's kindling from a blessed tree. Some common readers of Medina recited ﴿yuqadu﴾ with a ya' and a light qaf and a raised dal, meaning: the lamp is kindled, its kindler from a tree, without naming its subject. The common readers of Kufa recited "tuqadu" with a damma on the ta', a light qaf and a raised dal, meaning: the glass is kindled by its kindler from a blessed tree, since its subject is not named, so it was said: tuqadu. Some people of Mecca recited "tawaqqadu" with a fatha on the ta', a shadda on the qaf and a damma on the dal, meaning: the glass kindles from a tree, then one of the two ta's was dropped, being satisfied with the remaining one of the omitted. These readings are close in meaning though their wording differs, because when the glass is described as kindling, or as being kindled, the meaning is known, since what is meant is that the lamp kindles in it or the lamp is kindled in it, but they directed the report to the description of it with that being closer in speech, and the listeners understand its meaning and its intent. If that is so, then whichever reading the reciter uses is correct, except that the most wondrous of the readings to me is that I recite in it "tawaqqada," with a ta' fatha, a shadda on the qaf and a fatha on the dal, meaning the lamp is described as kindling, because kindling and being lit are undoubtedly attributes of the lamp rather than the glass. The meaning of the speech then is: like a niche in which is a lamp, the lamp from the oil of a blessed tree, an olive tree, neither eastern nor western.

We have mentioned some of what was reported from some of them about the difference in this matter earlier, and we will mention the rest of what has come to us that we did not mention before. Some said: this tree was called neither eastern nor western, meaning it is not eastern alone so that the sun does not reach it when it sets, but it has its share of the sun in the morning as long as it is on the side facing the east, and then it has no share of it when it inclines toward the west, nor is it western alone so that the sun reaches it in the evening when it inclines toward the west and does not reach it in the morning, but it is eastern-western, the sun rises on it in the morning and sets on it, so the heat of the sun reaches it in the morning and evening. They said: if it is like that, its oil is better.

Mention of those who said that:
• Hannad narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Ahwas narrated to us, from Simak, from Ikrimah, regarding His saying: ﴿an olive tree, neither eastern nor western﴾, he said: no mountain or valley screens it from the sun, when it rises and when it sets.
• Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Harmi ibn Imarah narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, saying: Imarah informed me, from Ikrimah, regarding His saying: ﴿neither eastern nor western﴾, he said: the tree is in a place that nothing screens from the sun; the sun rises on it and sets on it.
• al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Juraij, who said: Mujahid and Ibn Abbas said regarding ﴿neither eastern nor western﴾: they said it is that which is on the side of a mountain, which is reached by the sunrise and its setting, when it rises it reaches it, and when it sets it reaches it.

Others said: rather, the meaning of that is: it is neither eastern nor western.

Mention of those who said that:
• Sulayman ibn Abd al-Jabbar related to me, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Salt related to me, saying: Abu Kudaynah narrated to us, from Qabus, from his father, from Ibn Abbas regarding ﴿neither eastern nor western﴾, he said: it is a tree in the middle of the trees, not from the east or from the west.
• Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His saying: ﴿an olive tree, neither eastern nor western﴾: on the right side of Syria, neither eastern nor western.

Others said: this tree is not one of the trees of this world.

Mention of those who said that:
• Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Buzay' narrated to us, saying: Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Awf narrated to us, from al-Hasan, regarding God's saying: ﴿neither eastern nor western﴾, he said: By God, if it were on the earth it would be eastern or western, but it is only a parable God struck for His light.
• Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Uthman, meaning Ibn al-Haytham, narrated to us, saying: Awf narrated to us, from al-Hasan regarding God's saying: ﴿an olive tree, neither eastern nor western﴾, he said: if this olive tree were on the earth it would be eastern or western, but by God it is not on the earth; it is only a parable God struck for His light.
• Ya'qub related to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: Awf informed us, from al-Hasan regarding His saying: ﴿an olive tree, neither eastern nor western﴾, he said: this is a parable God struck; if this tree were in this world it would be either eastern or western.

The most correct of these opinions regarding the interpretation of this is the opinion of the one who said: it is eastern-western, and he said: the meaning of the speech is: it is not eastern, such that the sun reaches it in the evening but not in the morning; rather the sun rises on it and sets on it, so it is eastern-western.

We said that this is more correct as to the meaning of the speech because God only described the oil that is kindled in this lamp with purity and excellence, and when its tree is eastern-western, its oil is undoubtedly better, purer and brighter.

* *

His saying: ﴿its oil nearly would glow﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: the oil of this olive tree nearly glows from its purity and the goodness of its brightness, ﴿even if no fire touched it﴾, meaning: how much more so if fire touched it.

What is meant by His saying: ﴿it is kindled from a blessed tree﴾ is that this Qur'an is from God, and that it is His speech, so He made its likeness and its being from Him like the lamp kindled from the blessed tree, which He described, may His praise be exalted, in this verse. By His saying: ﴿its oil nearly would glow﴾ He means that the proofs of God, may His remembrance be exalted, upon His creatures nearly glow from their explanation and clarity to whoever reflects on them and considers them, or turns away from them and they are for him, ﴿even if no fire touched it﴾, meaning: even if God had not increased them in clarity and explicitness by sending down this Qur'an to them, as an alert to them regarding His unity; how much more so when He alerted them through it and reminded them of His signs, thereby adding to them proof upon His proofs against them before that. So that is a clarification from God and a light upon clarification, and the light which He had placed for them and set up before its descent.

* *

His saying: ﴿light upon light﴾

Meaning: the fire upon this oil which nearly glows even if no fire touched it.

As:
• Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us, and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿light upon light﴾, he said: the fire upon the oil.

Abu Ja'far said: and it is, in my view, as you have mentioned, a parable of the Qur'an. By His saying ﴿light upon light﴾, this Qur'an is a light from God, which He sent down to His creatures to be illuminated by it, ﴿upon light﴾, upon the proofs and clarifications which He had set up for them before the Qur'an came down, which indicate the truth of His oneness. So that is a clarification from God and a light upon the clarification, and the light which He had placed for them and set up before its descent.

It is reported from Zayd ibn Aslam regarding that what:
• Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Abd Allah ibn Ayyash informed me, saying: Zayd ibn Aslam said regarding His saying: ﴿light upon light﴾: some of it illuminates others, meaning the Qur'an.

* *

His saying: ﴿God guides to His light whom He wills﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: God grants success in following His light, which is this Qur'an, to whomever of His servants He wills.

* *

His saying: ﴿And God strikes parables for the people﴾

He says: God coins parables and likenesses for the people, just as He coined for them the likeness of this Qur'an in the heart of the believer by the lamp in the niche, and the rest of the parables in this verse.

﴿And God is Knower of all things﴾, He says: God strikes the parables, and all other things, and He is possessed of knowledge.

The commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 24, verses 36–38:

The explanation of His saying, exalted is His mention: ﴿In houses which Allah has permitted to be raised and in which His name is mentioned. He is glorified therein morning and evening by men﴾ [24:36]. Its meaning, exalted is His mention, by His saying: ﴿Allah is the Light of the heavens and the earth. The likeness of His light is like a niche within which is a lamp...﴾ [24:35], ﴿in houses which Allah has permitted to be raised.﴾

As related:

* Yunus told me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: "The niche (mishkah) in which is the wick in which is the lamp." He said: "The lamps are in houses which Allah has permitted to be raised."

Abu Ja'far said: It is possible that "min" (from) is connected to "tawqadu" (is kindled), so the meaning would be: that lamp is kindled from a blessed tree in houses which Allah has permitted to be raised. By "houses" is meant the mosques.

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) differed on this. Some of them said what we have said.

Mention of those who said that:

* Ibn Humayd and Nasr ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Azdi told us, both saying: Hakkam related to us, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, from Abu Salih, regarding the words of Allah: ﴿in houses which Allah has permitted to be raised﴾: "The mosques."

* Ali told me, saying: Abu Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah related to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿in houses which Allah has permitted to be raised﴾: "They are the mosques, which are to be honoured, and He forbade idle talk in them."

* Muhammad ibn Sa'd told me, saying: My father related to me, saying: My paternal uncle related to me, saying: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿in houses which Allah has permitted to be raised﴾: "That is every mosque in which prayer is performed, congregational or otherwise."

* Muhammad ibn Amr told me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿in houses which Allah has permitted to be raised﴾: "Mosques that are built."

* al-Harith told me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

* al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid, the like of it.

* al-Hasan related to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Hasan, regarding His words: ﴿in houses which Allah has permitted to be raised﴾: "In the mosques."

He said: Ma'mar informed us, from Abu Ishaq, from Amr ibn Maymun, who said: "I met the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and they used to say: 'The mosques are the houses of Allah, and it is a right upon Allah to honour whoever visits them.'"

* Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak related to us, from Salim ibn Umar, regarding (the words) "in houses which Allah has permitted to be raised": "They are the mosques."

* Yunus told me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words: ﴿in houses which Allah has permitted to be raised﴾: "The mosques."

Others said: By this is meant all houses.

Mention of those who said that:

* Ibn Humayd and Nasr ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Azdi related to us, both saying: Hakkam ibn Salm related to us, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, from Ikrimah, regarding ﴿in houses which Allah has permitted to be raised﴾: "They are all houses."

We have only chosen the view we have chosen because of the indication in His words: ﴿He is glorified therein morning and evening by men whom neither commerce nor sale distracts from the remembrance of Allah﴾, which shows that they are houses built for prayer. Therefore we said they are the mosques.

The people of interpretation differed regarding the interpretation of His words: ﴿Allah has permitted to be raised﴾. Some of them said its meaning is: Allah has permitted them to be built.

Mention of those who said that:

* Muhammad ibn Amr told me, saying: Abu Isam related to us, saying: Isa related to us, and al-Harith told me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿Allah has permitted to be raised﴾: "To be built."

* al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid, the like of it.

Others said: its meaning is: Allah has permitted them to be exalted.

Mention of those who said that:

* al-Hasan ibn Yahya related to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Hasan, regarding His words: ﴿Allah has permitted to be raised﴾: he says: "To be exalted for His remembrance."

The view most correct in my judgement among the two views is the view stated by Mujahid, namely that its meaning is: Allah has permitted them to be raised in construction, as He, majestic is His praise, said: ﴿And when Abraham was raising the foundations of the House﴾ [2:127]. That is because it is the more prevalent sense of "raising" applied to houses and buildings.

* *

As for His words: ﴿and in which His name is mentioned﴾

He says: And He permitted His servants to mention His name in them. It has been said that by this is meant that He permitted them to recite the Qur'an in them.

Mention of those who said that:

* Ali told me, saying: Abd Allah related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah related to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "Then He said: ﴿and in which His name is mentioned﴾," meaning: "His Book is recited in them." This view is close in meaning to what we have said, because recitation of the Book of Allah is among the meanings of the remembrance of Allah. However, what we have said is the more apparent of its two meanings, so we have chosen it.

And His words: ﴿He is glorified therein morning and evening by men whom neither commerce nor sale distracts from the remembrance of Allah﴾.

The readers differed over the recitation of His words: ﴿yusabbihu lahu﴾. The majority of the readers of the regions recited ﴿yusabbihu lahu﴾ with a damma on the yaa and a kasra on the baa', meaning: men pray to Him therein, making "yusabbihu" a verb for the men and a predicate about them, with "men" as its subject. Except Asim and Ibn Amir, who recited it "yusabbaḥu lahu" with a damma on the yaa and a fatha on the baa', in the passive form, and then they put "men" in the nominative as a second, implied predicate, as if they intended: "Allah is glorified in the houses which Allah has permitted to be raised, so men glorify Him," so they made "men" nominative by an implied verb. The reading that is more correct in our view is the reading with a kasra on the baa', making it a predicate for the men and a verb for them. The choice would be to make "men" nominative by an implied verb only if the predicate concerned the houses and could not be complete without His words: ﴿He is glorified therein﴾. But since the predicate about them is complete without that, there is no basis for attaching His words "yusabbihu lahu" to anything other than the predicate about the men. By His words: ﴿He is glorified therein morning and evening﴾, is meant: men pray to Him in these houses in the mornings and evenings.

The people of interpretation said likewise.

Mention of those who said that:

* Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Azdi told me, saying: al-Mu'afa ibn Imran related to us, from Sufyan, from Ammar al-Dhuhni [he is Ammar ibn Mu'awiyah al-Dhuhni, with a dotted... of the Kufan, whom Ahmad declared reliable, died 133], from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "Every glorification (tasbih) in the Qur'an is prayer."

* Ali told me, saying: Abd Allah related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah related to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "Then He said: ﴿He is glorified therein morning and evening﴾," meaning: "He prays to Him therein at dawn and in the evening." By "morning" is meant the dawn prayer, and by "evening" the afternoon prayer, and these two are the first prayers that Allah made obligatory, so He wished to mention them and mention His worship through them.

* al-Hasan related to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Hasan, regarding ﴿He is glorified therein morning and evening by men﴾: "Allah permitted them to be built, so they pray in them morning and evening."

* I was told, from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say regarding His words: ﴿He is glorified therein morning and evening﴾: "He means the obligatory prayer."

* *

As for His words: ﴿by men whom neither commerce nor sale distracts from the remembrance of Allah﴾

He, exalted is His mention, says: These men who pray in these mosques, which Allah permitted to be raised, are not preoccupied, by trade or sale, from the remembrance of Allah therein and the establishment of prayer.

As related:

* Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far related to us, saying: Shu'bah related to us, from Sa'id ibn Abi al-Hasan, from a man whose name he forgot, regarding this verse: ﴿in houses which Allah has permitted to be raised and in which His name is mentioned; He is glorified therein morning and evening by men whom neither commerce nor sale distracts from the remembrance of Allah﴾ ... to His words: ﴿and the eyes﴾: "They are people in their trade and their sales; their trade and their sales do not distract them from the remembrance of Allah."

* al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Ja'far ibn Sulayman related to us, from Amr ibn Dinar, from Salim ibn Abd Allah, that he looked at a group from the market who stood up and left their dealings for prayer, and said: "These are the ones whom Allah mentioned in His Book: ﴿whom neither commerce nor sale distracts from the remembrance of Allah﴾ ... the verse."

* He said: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hushaym related to us, from Sayyar, from one who narrated to him, from Ibn Mas'ud, the like of that.

* Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim told me, saying: Hushaym related to us, from Sayyar, who said: I was told from Ibn Mas'ud that he saw some people of the market, when the call to prayer was made, leave their dealings and rise to prayer. Abd Allah said: "These are of those whom Allah mentioned in His Book: ﴿whom neither commerce nor sale distracts from the remembrance of Allah﴾."

Some of them said: The meaning of that: ﴿neither commerce nor sale distracts them﴾ from their obligatory prayer.

Mention of those who said that:
