* Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Azdi told me, saying: al-Mu'afa ibn Imran related to us, from Sufyan, from Ammar al-Dhuhni [he is Ammar ibn Mu'awiyah al-Dhuhni, with a dotted... of the Kufan, whom Ahmad declared reliable, died 133], from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "Every glorification (tasbih) in the Qur'an is prayer."

* Ali told me, saying: Abd Allah related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah related to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "Then He said: ﴿He is glorified therein morning and evening﴾," meaning: "He prays to Him therein at dawn and in the evening." By "morning" is meant the dawn prayer, and by "evening" the afternoon prayer, and these two are the first prayers that Allah made obligatory, so He wished to mention them and mention His worship through them.

* al-Hasan related to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Hasan, regarding ﴿He is glorified therein morning and evening by men﴾: "Allah permitted them to be built, so they pray in them morning and evening."

* I was told, from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say regarding His words: ﴿He is glorified therein morning and evening﴾: "He means the obligatory prayer."

* *

As for His words: ﴿by men whom neither commerce nor sale distracts from the remembrance of Allah﴾

He, exalted is His mention, says: These men who pray in these mosques, which Allah permitted to be raised, are not preoccupied, by trade or sale, from the remembrance of Allah therein and the establishment of prayer.

As related:

* Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far related to us, saying: Shu'bah related to us, from Sa'id ibn Abi al-Hasan, from a man whose name he forgot, regarding this verse: ﴿in houses which Allah has permitted to be raised and in which His name is mentioned; He is glorified therein morning and evening by men whom neither commerce nor sale distracts from the remembrance of Allah﴾ ... to His words: ﴿and the eyes﴾: "They are people in their trade and their sales; their trade and their sales do not distract them from the remembrance of Allah."

* al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Ja'far ibn Sulayman related to us, from Amr ibn Dinar, from Salim ibn Abd Allah, that he looked at a group from the market who stood up and left their dealings for prayer, and said: "These are the ones whom Allah mentioned in His Book: ﴿whom neither commerce nor sale distracts from the remembrance of Allah﴾ ... the verse."

* He said: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hushaym related to us, from Sayyar, from one who narrated to him, from Ibn Mas'ud, the like of that.

* Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim told me, saying: Hushaym related to us, from Sayyar, who said: I was told from Ibn Mas'ud that he saw some people of the market, when the call to prayer was made, leave their dealings and rise to prayer. Abd Allah said: "These are of those whom Allah mentioned in His Book: ﴿whom neither commerce nor sale distracts from the remembrance of Allah﴾."

Some of them said: The meaning of that: ﴿neither commerce nor sale distracts them﴾ from their obligatory prayer.

Mention of those who said that:

* Ali told me, saying: Abd Allah related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah related to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "Then He said: ﴿men whom neither commerce nor sale distracts from the remembrance of Allah﴾," meaning: "from the prescribed prayer."

* *

His words: ﴿and the establishment of prayer﴾

He says: And that does not distract them either from establishing prayer with its limits at its appointed times.

The people of interpretation said likewise.

Mention of those who said that:

* Muhammad ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Muhammad related to us, saying: Awf related to us, from Sa'id ibn Abi al-Hasan, from a man whose name Awf forgot, regarding ﴿and the establishment of prayer﴾: "They stand for prayer at its appointed times."

If someone says: Is not His words ﴿and the establishment of prayer﴾ a verbal noun from "aqamtu" (I established)? It is said: Yes. If he says: Is not its verbal noun "iqamah," just as the verbal noun of "ajartu" is "ijarah"? It is said: Yes. If he says: How then did He say ﴿iqam al-salah﴾, or may we say "aqamtu iqaman"? It is said: But I permit what seems right to me: "iqam al-salah." If it is asked: What is the justification for that? It is said: The rule for "aqamtu," when its verbal noun is formed, is that one says "iqwaman," just as one says "aqadtu fulanan iqadan" and "a'taytuhu i'taa'." But when the Arabs made the waw of "aqamtu" quiescent, it dropped out because it met a quiescent letter, and the mim was also quiescent, they formed the verbal noun on that basis, since the waw came quiescent before the alif of the verbal-noun pattern (if'al), which was also quiescent, so the first of them fell away. Then they replaced it with a ha' at the end of the word, as an augmentation of the word, just as they did in their saying "wa'adtuhu 'idatan" and "wazantuhu zinatan," when the waw was removed from the beginning, they augmented it at the end with a ha'. Then when "iqamah" was put in construct with "al-salah," they dropped the added letter they had added for augmentation, namely the ha' at its end, because the governing word and what is governed are, in their view, like a single letter, so they dispensed with the added letter by means of the word in the genitive. Some of them have said in a similar instance:

"Indeed the associates have hastened the parting and gone off, and they have failed you in the matter they promised."

[The verse is by al-Fadl ibn Abbas ibn Utbah ibn Abi Lahab. Its context is in Lisan al-Arab (w-ʿ-d) ...]

He means: "the promise of the matter." He dropped the ha' from "'idah" when he put it in construct, and likewise in "iqam al-salah."

* *

His words: ﴿and the giving of zakah﴾

It has been said: its meaning is sincere obedience to Allah.

Mention of those who said that:

* Ali told me, saying: Abd Allah related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah related to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿And establish prayer and give zakah﴾ and ﴿and he used to enjoin on his family prayer and zakah﴾ and His words ﴿and He has enjoined on me prayer and zakah﴾ and His words ﴿Had it not been for the bounty of Allah upon you and His mercy, not one of you would ever have been pure﴾ and His words ﴿and affection from Us and purity﴾, and similar in the Qur'an, he said: "By zakah is meant obedience to Allah and sincerity."

His words: ﴿They fear a Day in which hearts and eyes will be turned about﴾ mean: they fear a day in which hearts are turned about from its terror, between hope for salvation and fear of destruction, and the eyes: that is, in which direction they will be seized, whether to the right or to the left, and from where their books will be given to them, from the right hand or from the left. That is the Day of Resurrection.

As related:

* Yunus told me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Abd Allah ibn Ayyash said, Zayd ibn Aslam said, regarding the words of Allah: ﴿in houses which Allah has permitted to be raised﴾ ... to His words: ﴿in which hearts and eyes will be turned about﴾: "The Day of Resurrection."

* *

His words: ﴿so that Allah may reward them with the best of what they did﴾

He says: They did that, meaning that trade and sale did not distract them from the remembrance of Allah, and they established prayer, gave zakah, and obeyed their Lord, out of fear of His punishment on the Day of Resurrection, so that Allah may reward them on the Day of Resurrection with the best of their deeds which they did in this world, and increase for them, beyond His reward for their best deeds in this world, from His bounty, so He bestows upon them from His presence what He loves of His honour for them.

* *

His words: ﴿And Allah gives provision to whom He wills without account﴾

He, exalted is His mention, says: He bestows His favour upon whom He wills and desires, from His bounty and honour, of what he did not deserve by his deeds, and did not attain by his obedience, ﴿without account﴾, that is: without reckoning for what He gives and bestows.

Commentary on the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And those who disbelieved, their deeds are like a mirage in a level plain, which the thirsty one thinks is water, until, when he comes to it, he finds it to be nothing, and finds Allah with him, so He pays him in full his account. And Allah is swift in reckoning﴾ [24:39]

This is a parable which Allah struck for the deeds of the people of disbelief in Him. He said: those who denied the Oneness of their Lord and denied this Qur'an and the one who brought it, the likeness of their deeds which they did is ﴿like a mirage﴾. He says: like a mirage. The mirage (al-sarab) is that which clings to the ground; this occurs at midday, when the heat intensifies, and it is like water between the sky and the earth; this occurs at the beginning of the day, lifting everything in the forenoon.

* *

And His words: ﴿in a level plain (biqi'ah)﴾

It is the plural of qa' (plain), like jirah being the plural of jar (neighbour). The qa' is the land that is flat and wide, and in it the mirage occurs.

* *

And His words: ﴿which the thirsty one thinks is water﴾

He says: the thirsty one among people thinks the mirage is water. ﴿Until, when he comes to it﴾ — the pronoun (ha') refers to the mention of the mirage, and the meaning is: until, when the thirsty one comes to the mirage seeking water, begging it to relieve his thirst, ﴿he finds it to be nothing﴾. He says: he finds the mirage to be nothing. Likewise the disbelievers in Allah, in respect of their deeds which they did in delusion, think that these will save them from Allah's punishment, just as the thirsty one who saw the mirage thought it was water that would quench his thirst. Then, when he perishes and reaches the point of needing his deed, which he thought would benefit him with Allah, he finds that it does not benefit him at all, because his deed was based on disbelief in Allah. ﴿And finds Allah﴾: this disbeliever, at his death, is in wait for Him; so He pays him on the Day of Resurrection the account of his deeds which he did in the world, and recompenses him with them the recompense which he deserves from Him.

If someone says: How is it said, ﴿until, when he comes to it, he finds it to be nothing﴾? If the mirage is nothing, why was the pronoun added in His words ﴿until, when he comes to it﴾? It is said: it is something seen from afar like fog, which appears dense from a distance, and like dust particles; when a person approaches it, it thins out and becomes like air. It may also be that the meaning is: until, when he comes to the place of the mirage, he finds nothing there, so the mention of the mirage was sufficient in place of the mention of its location. ﴿And Allah is swift in reckoning﴾: He says, Allah is swift in His reckoning, because He, may His remembrance be exalted, does not need to count on fingers or to keep it in memory, but He knows all of that before the servant does it and after he has done it.

Those who interpreted the verse said something similar to what we have said regarding its meaning.

Those who said so:

Ubayy ibn Ka'b said: Then He struck another parable and said: ﴿And those who disbelieved, their deeds are like a mirage in a level plain﴾. He said: Likewise the disbeliever will come on the Day of Resurrection thinking that he has good with Allah, but he finds none, and so He causes him to enter the Fire.

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Abu Ja'far al-Razi, from Abu al-'Aliyah, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, similarly.

Ali narrated to me, saying: Abdullah narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿their deeds are like a mirage in a level plain﴾, he said: the flat land.

Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿And those who disbelieved, their deeds are like a mirage in a level plain﴾ ... to His words: ﴿And Allah is swift in reckoning﴾, he said: It is a parable which Allah struck for a man who became thirsty and his thirst intensified; he saw a mirage and thought it was water, so he sought it and thought he had reached it, until he came to it, and when he came to it he found nothing, and at that moment he died. Thus the disbeliever thinks his deed will suffice him or benefit him in some way, and he does not arrive at anything until death comes to him; when death comes to him, he finds that his deed has not sufficed him at all, and it has not benefited him, just as it did not benefit the thirsty one who pursued the mirage.

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding the words of Allah: ﴿like a mirage in a level plain﴾, he said: in a plain of the land; and the mirage is his deed. Al-Harith added in his report from al-Hasan: and the mirage is the deed of the disbeliever. ﴿When he comes to it, he finds it to be nothing﴾: his coming to it is his death and his departure from the world. ﴿And finds Allah﴾ at his departure from the world, ﴿so He pays him his account﴾.

Al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding His words: ﴿like a mirage in a level plain﴾, he said: a plain of the land. ﴿which the thirsty one thinks is water﴾: it is a parable which Allah struck for the deed of the disbeliever; he says: he thinks he is in something, just as this mirage is thought to be water. ﴿Until, when he comes to it, he finds it to be nothing﴾: likewise the disbeliever, when he dies, finds his deed to be nothing. ﴿And finds Allah with him, so He pays him his account﴾.

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words: ﴿And those who disbelieved﴾ ... to His words: ﴿and finds Allah with him﴾, he said: This is a parable which Allah struck for those who disbelieved: ﴿their deeds are like a mirage in a level plain﴾. He has seen the mirage and trusted himself that it is water; when he comes to it he finds nothing. He said: These people thought their deeds were righteous, and that they would return from them to good, but they return from them only as the owner of the mirage returned. This is a parable which Allah, exalted is His praise and sanctified are His names, has struck.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 24, verse 40:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Or [they are] like darkness in a vast, deep sea, covered by a wave, above which is another wave, above which is a cloud — darknesses, one above another. If he extends his hand, he can hardly see it. And whoever Allah does not give light — for him there is no light.﴾ (24:40)

This is another example that Allah coined for the deeds of the disbelievers. He, exalted is His remembrance, says: The likeness of the deeds of these disbelievers, in that they were done in error, corruption, misguidance and bewilderment on the part of their doers, and without guidance, is like darknesses in a vast sea. He attributed the sea to the deep (lujjah) as a description of it, that it is deep and has much water; and the lujjah of the sea is its main body. ﴿Covered by a wave﴾ means: the sea is covered by a wave. ﴿Above which is another wave﴾ means: above the wave there is another wave covering it. ﴿Above which is a cloud﴾ means: above the second wave, which covers the first wave, there is a cloud. Thus He made the darknesses a likeness of their deeds, and the deep sea a likeness of the heart of the disbeliever. He means: a deed proceeding from a heart that has been overwhelmed by ignorance and covered by error and bewilderment, just as this deep sea is covered by a wave, above which is another wave, above which is a cloud. Likewise the heart of this disbeliever, whose deed is like these darknesses, is covered by ignorance of Allah, in that Allah has sealed it, so it does not understand from Allah; and upon his hearing, so he does not hear the admonitions of Allah; and He placed a veil upon his sight, so he does not see with it the proofs of Allah. Thus [they are] darknesses, one above another. [[Al-Shawkani said in Fath al-Qadir (4: 38): Among the strange interpretations: He, glorified and exalted, intended by the darknesses the deeds of the disbeliever, by the deep sea his heart, and by the waves what covers his heart of ignorance, doubt and bewilderment; and by the cloud the rust, the sealing and the stamping upon his heart. This is an interpretation that is very far from the language of the Arabs. End quote.]]

Similar to what we have said, the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said.

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to us, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿Or [they are] like darkness in a vast, deep sea, covered by a wave, above which is another wave, above which is a cloud﴾ ... to His saying: ﴿no light﴾. He said: By the darknesses he means the deeds, and by the deep sea: the heart of the human being. He said: covered by a wave, above which is another wave, above which is a cloud. He said: darknesses, one above another. He means by that the veil upon the heart, the hearing and the sight, and it is like His saying: ﴿Allah has sealed upon their hearts﴾ ... the verse, and like His saying: ﴿Have you seen one who has taken his desire as his god?﴾ ... to His saying: ﴿Will you not then remember?﴾.

Al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah regarding His saying: ﴿Or [they are] like darknesses in a vast deep sea﴾: deep. It is a likeness Allah coined for the disbeliever who acts in misguidance and bewilderment. He said: ﴿darknesses, one above another﴾.

It is narrated from Ubayy ibn Ka'b:

Abd al-A'la ibn Wasil narrated to me, saying: Ubayd Allah ibn Musa narrated to us, saying: Abu Ja'far al-Razi informed us, from al-Rabi', from Abu al-Aliyah, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, regarding His saying: ﴿Or [they are] like darkness in a vast, deep sea, covered by a wave﴾ ... the verse. He said: He coined another likeness for the disbeliever, saying: ﴿Or [they are] like darknesses in a vast, deep sea﴾ ... the verse. He said: he turns about in five kinds of darkness: his speech is darkness, his deed is darkness, his entrance is darkness, his exit is darkness, and his destination on the Day of Resurrection is toward darknesses, to the Fire.

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Abu Ja'far al-Razi, from Abu al-Rabi', from Abu al-Aliyah, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, similarly.

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His saying: ﴿Or [they are] like darknesses in a vast, deep sea, covered by a wave, above which is another wave﴾ ... to His saying: ﴿darknesses, one above another﴾: evil, one above another.

* *

And His saying: ﴿If he extends his hand, he can hardly see it﴾

It means: if the one looking extends his hand within these darknesses, he can hardly see it.

If someone says to us: How is it said, ﴿he can hardly see it﴾, given the intensity of this darkness that is described, and you know that the saying of the speaker, "I could hardly see so-and-so," is only his affirmation of his own seeing after effort and difficulty; and beneath the darknesses described in this verse there is [darkness] in which the looker does not see his hand when he extends it, so how [is it said] within them? It is said in answer to that: there are sayings, which we mention, and then we inform of the correct view on that. The first: that the meaning of the statement is: if he extends his hand, seeing it, he can hardly see it, i.e., he does not know from where he sees it; so it is of the advanced (muqaddam) whose meaning is delayed (mu'akhkhar), and the interpretation of the statement on this is: if he extends his hand, he is not near to seeing it. The second: that its meaning is: if he extends his hand, he does not see it [[In Fath al-Qadir of al-Shawkani (Halabi edition, 4: 38): al-Zajjaj and Abu Ubaydah said: he did not see it and was not near to. al-Farra' said: kad is extra (za'idah). And the verifier al-Radi in his commentary on Ibn al-Hajib's Kafiyah (2: 306) said: negating nearness to the act is more emphatic in negating that act than negating the act itself; for "I was near to striking" is more emphatic in negating striking than "I struck." End quote.]], and His saying ﴿he can hardly (lam yakad)﴾ in its entry into the statement is like the entry of conjecture (zann) into what is certain within speech, as in His saying: ﴿and they thought that they had no escape﴾ and the like. The third: that he has seen it after slowness and effort, as the speaker says to another: "I could hardly see you in the darkness," while he has seen him, but after despair and hardship. This third view is the most apparent of the meanings of the word from the standpoint of how the Arabs use "akad" in their speech; and the other saying which we mentioned, that it is taken to mean "he did not see it," is a view clearer from the standpoint of the exegesis, though its meaning is the most hidden. This phrasing is fitting in this place, namely saying "he can hardly see it" together with the intensity of the darkness mentioned, because that is a likeness, not a report of something that occurred.

﴿And whoever Allah does not give light — for him there is no light﴾: it means, whoever Allah does not grant faith and guidance from misguidance, and knowledge of His Book — ﴿for him there is no light﴾: it means, for him there is no faith, guidance, or knowledge of His Book.

The commentary on His words, the Exalted: "Do you not see that to Allah glorify whoever is in the heavens and the earth, and the birds in flight? Each has known its prayer and its glorification, and Allah is Knowing of what they do. (41) And to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and to Allah is the destination." (42)

Says the Exalted, addressing His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): Have you not looked, O Muhammad, with the eye of your heart, and so known that whoever is in the heavens and the earth, of angels, humans and jinn, prays to Allah? "And the birds in flight" also glorify Him in the air. "Each has known its prayer and its glorification" [[It appears that there is a omission in the statement. Its meaning: If it is asked: what is the benefit of coordinating "and its glorification" with "its prayer"... etc. This is evidenced by his saying: "It was said... etc.", and it is an answer to a question.]] And glorification, in your view, is prayer. It is said: the prayer is for the children of Adam, and the glorification is for the other creatures; for this reason He distinguished between them.

Commentators of interpretation have said things similar to what we have said.

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to me; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words: "To Allah glorify whoever is in the heavens and the earth, and the birds in flight; each has known its prayer and its glorification." He said: The prayer is for humans, and the glorification is for what is other than that of the creation.

al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid regarding His words: "Do you not see that to Allah glorify whoever is in the heavens and the earth, and the birds in flight; each has known its prayer and its glorification." He said: His prayer is for people, and His glorification is general for every thing.

The words "each has known its prayer and its glorification" may be understood in several ways. First, the pronoun in "its prayer and its glorification" refers back to "each", so the meaning is: every one of them that prays and glorifies, Allah has known its prayer and its glorification, and "each" is then the subject by the returning pronoun in His words "each has known its prayer", which is the pronoun in "its prayer".

The second way: the pronoun in "its prayer and its glorification" also refers to "each", and "each" is the subject by the returning pronoun in "has known", so "has known" is the verb of "each". The meaning then is: every one of them that prays and glorifies has known the prayer of its own self and its glorification, which it was charged with and obliged to.

The third way: the pronoun in "its prayer and its glorification" refers to Allah, and the knowing belongs to "each", so the meaning is: every one of them that glorifies and prays has known the prayer of Allah which He assigned to it, and its glorification.

Of these three meanings, the most apparent in this statement is the first, namely that the meaning is: every one of them that prays and glorifies, Allah has known its prayer and its glorification.

* *

As for His words: "And Allah is Knowing of what they do."

Says the Exalted: Allah has knowledge of what every one of them that prays and glorifies does. Nothing of their actions is hidden from Him, whether obedience or disobedience; He encompasses all of that, and He will recompense them for all of it.

* *

As for His words: "And to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth."

Says His Majesty: To Allah belongs the authority and sovereignty of the heavens and the earth, and their possession, apart from every authority and sovereignty below Him. So fear Him alone, O people, and desire Him alone, not other than Him, for in His hand are the treasuries of the heavens and the earth, and by giving you from them He does not fear poverty. "And to Allah is the destination" means: you will return to Him after your death, your final place and return, and He will pay you the rewards of your deeds that you did in the world. So worship Him well, strive in His obedience, and send forward for yourselves righteous deeds.

The commentary on His words, the Exalted: "Do you not see that to Allah glorify whoever is in the heavens and the earth, and the birds in flight? Each has known its prayer and its glorification, and Allah is Knowing of what they do. (41) And to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and to Allah is the destination." (42)

Says the Exalted, addressing His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): Have you not looked, O Muhammad, with the eye of your heart, and so known that whoever is in the heavens and the earth, of angels, humans and jinn, prays to Allah? "And the birds in flight" also glorify Him in the air. "Each has known its prayer and its glorification" [[It appears that there is a omission in the statement. Its meaning: If it is asked: what is the benefit of coordinating "and its glorification" with "its prayer"... etc. This is evidenced by his saying: "It was said... etc.", and it is an answer to a question.]] And glorification, in your view, is prayer. It is said: the prayer is for the children of Adam, and the glorification is for the other creatures; for this reason He distinguished between them.

Commentators of interpretation have said things similar to what we have said.

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to me; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words: "To Allah glorify whoever is in the heavens and the earth, and the birds in flight; each has known its prayer and its glorification." He said: The prayer is for humans, and the glorification is for what is other than that of the creation.

al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid regarding His words: "Do you not see that to Allah glorify whoever is in the heavens and the earth, and the birds in flight; each has known its prayer and its glorification." He said: His prayer is for people, and His glorification is general for every thing.

The second way: the pronoun in "its prayer and its glorification" also refers to "each", and "each" is the subject by the returning pronoun in "has known", so "has known" is the verb of "each". The meaning then is: every one of them that prays and glorifies has known the prayer of its own self and its glorification, which it was charged with and obliged to.

The third way: the pronoun in "its prayer and its glorification" refers to Allah, and the knowing belongs to "each", so the meaning is: every one of them that glorifies and prays has known the prayer of Allah which He assigned to it, and its glorification.

Of these three meanings, the most apparent in this statement is the first, namely that the meaning is: every one of them that prays and glorifies, Allah has known its prayer and its glorification.

* *

As for His words: "And Allah is Knowing of what they do."

Says the Exalted: Allah has knowledge of what every one of them that prays and glorifies does. Nothing of their actions is hidden from Him, whether obedience or disobedience; He encompasses all of that, and He will recompense them for all of it.

* *

As for His words: "And to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth."

Says His Majesty: To Allah belongs the authority and sovereignty of the heavens and the earth, and their possession, apart from every authority and sovereignty below Him. So fear Him alone, O people, and desire Him alone, not other than Him, for in His hand are the treasuries of the heavens and the earth, and by giving you from them He does not fear poverty. "And to Allah is the destination" means: you will return to Him after your death, your final place and return, and He will pay you the rewards of your deeds that you did in the world. So worship Him well, strive in His obedience, and send forward for yourselves righteous deeds.

The Interpretation of His words, the Exalted: "Have you not seen that Allah drives the clouds gently, then joins them together, then makes them into a heap, so that you see the rain coming out from within them; and He sends down from the sky mountains [of hail] wherein is hail, so He strikes with it whom He wills and averts it from whom He wills. The flash of its lightning nearly takes away the sight. Allah alternates the night and the day. Indeed in that is a lesson for those who have vision."

Allah, the Exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): "Have you not seen" O Muhammad, "that Allah drives" meaning: drives along, "clouds" wherever He wills? "Then joins them together" means: then He joins the clouds together. He attached "between" (bayn) to the clouds, and it was not mentioned with anything else. Bayn is only attached to a group or two, because "clouds" (sahab) carries the sense of a plural, its singular being sahabah, just as the collective "palm trees" (nakhl) has the singular nakhlah, and "dates" (tamr) has the singular tamrah. So this is like the saying of someone: "So-and-so sat between the palm trees." The joining of the clouds by Allah is His gathering of their scattered parts together.

* *

And His words: "Then makes it into a heap"

He says: then He makes the clouds that He drives, and joins some of them to others, into a heap, meaning: piled up, some of them upon others.

⁕ Abd al-Hamid ibn Bayan related to us, saying: Khalid informed us, saying: Matar related to us, from Habib ibn Abi Thabit, from Ubayd ibn Umayr al-Laythi, who said: The winds are four. Allah sends the first wind and it sweeps the earth clean; then He sends the second and it produces clouds; then He sends the third and it joins them together and makes them into a heap; then He sends the fourth and it causes them to rain.

* *

And His words: "So you see the rain coming out from within it"

He says: you see the rain coming out from between the clouds. It is the *waduq* (rain), as the poet said:

"Neither a cloud has poured its rain, nor a land has made its herbage grow..."

[The verse is by Amir ibn Juwayn al-Ta'i (Lisan: wdq). He said: al-waduq is rain in its entirety, both its heavy and its light forms; the verb is waduqa yadiqu waduqan, meaning it dripped. Amir ibn Juwayn al-Ta'i said: "Neither a cloud..." The verse; and al-muzna is a cloud. The author cited the verse as evidence that the meaning of waduq is rain.]

The pronoun in His words "from within it" (min khilalih) refers to the clouds. Khilal is the plural of khilal (gap). It is related from Ibn Abbas and a group that they used to recite it as "min khalalih."

⁕ Ibn al-Muthanna related to us, saying: Harmi ibn Umara related to us, saying: Shu'ba related to us, saying: Qatada related to us, from al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim, that he recited this word: "So you see the rain coming out from within it" as "min khalalih."

⁕ He said: Shu'ba related to us, saying: Umara informed me, from a man, from Ibn Abbas, that he recited this word: "min khalalih" (with fatha on the kha').

⁕ Ahmad ibn Yusuf related to us, saying: al-Qasim related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to us, from Harun, who said: Umara ibn Abi Hafsa informed me, from a man, from Ibn Abbas, that he recited it: "min khalalih" with a fatha on the kha', without an alif.

Harun said: I mentioned that to Abu Amr, and he said: It is indeed good, but khilalih is more comprehensive.

As for the readers of the major cities, they follow the other reading, "min khilalihi," and it is the one we choose, because the readers of authority have reached consensus upon it.

⁕ Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words: "So you see the rain coming out from within it," he said: al-waduq is the rainfall, and al-khilal is the clouds.

* *

And His words: "And He sends down from the sky mountains [of hail] wherein is hail"

Two opinions have been stated on this. One: its meaning is that Allah sends down from the sky mountains which are in the sky, of hail, created there by His creation; so on this view the mountains are of hail, just as one says "mountains of clay." The other opinion: Allah sends down from the sky the amount of mountains, and the likenesses of mountains, of hail to the earth, just as one says: "I have two houses of straw," meaning the amount of two houses of straw, though the two houses are not made of straw.

* *

And His words: "So He strikes with it whom He wills and averts it from whom He wills"

He says: by that which He sends down from the sky of mountains wherein is hail, He punishes whom He wills, destroying him, or destroying by it his crops and property. "And averts it from whom He wills" among His creation, meaning: from their crops and their wealth.

* *

And His words: "The flash of its lightning nearly takes away the sight"

He says: the intensity of the light of the lightning of this cloud nearly takes away the sight of whoever it meets with his gaze. Al-sana is with a short vowel, and it is the light of lightning.

As:

⁕ al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Ata al-Khurasani, from Ibn Abbas regarding His words: "The flash of its lightning" he said: its light.

⁕ al-Hasan related to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada, regarding His words: "The flash of its lightning," he said: the glare of lightning takes away the sight.

⁕ Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words: "The flash of its lightning nearly takes away the sight," he said: its sana is a light that takes away sight.

The readers of the major cities recited "yadhhabu" with fatha on the ya' (yadhhabu bil-absar), except Abu Ja'far the reciter, who recited it with damma on the ya' ("yudhhibu bil-absar").

The reading I do not choose other than is the fatha, because the readers of authority have reached consensus upon it, and because the Arabs, when they introduce the ba' into the object of dhahaba, do not say "illa dhahabat bihi" instead of "adhhabat bihi," and when they introduce the alif into "adhhabat," they hardly introduce the ba' into its object, saying "adhhabtuhu" and "dhahabtu bihi."

* *

And His words: "Allah alternates the night and the day"

He says: Allah causes the night and the day to succeed each other and turns them: when this departs, that comes, and when that departs, this comes. "Indeed in that is a lesson for those who have vision" means: indeed in the creation by Allah of the clouds, His sending down from them the rain, and from the sky the hail, and in His alternating of the night and the day, there is a lesson for whoever takes lesson from it, and an admonition for whoever is admonished by it, among those who have understanding and intellect; for that indicates and proves that He has a Manager, a Disposer, and an Alternator, to whom nothing is like.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 24, verse 45:

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿And Allah created every creature from water. Among them are those who walk on their bellies, and among them are those who walk on two legs, and among them are those who walk on four. Allah creates what He wills. Indeed, Allah is capable of all things.﴾ (45)

The reciters differed over the reading of His saying: ﴿وَاللَّهُ خَلَقَ كُلَّ دَابَّةٍ مِنْ مَاءٍ﴾ (wa-Llahu khalaqa kulla dabbatin min ma'). The majority of the reciters of Kufa, other than ʿAsim, read: "وَاللهُ خَالِقُ كُلِّ دَابَّةٍ" (wa-Llahu khaliqu kulli dabbatin, "And Allah is the Creator of every creature"). The majority of the reciters of Medina and Basra, and ʿAsim, read: ﴿وَاللَّهُ خَلَقَ كُلَّ دَابَّةٍ﴾ with kulla in the accusative, and khalaqa in the form of fa'ala (the past tense). These are two well-known readings that are close in meaning, since the construction with the genitive in the reading of the one who reads "khaliq" indicates that the meaning is past; so whichever of the two the reciter reads, he is correct.

* *

And His saying: ﴿خَلَقَ كُلَّ دَابَّةٍ مِنْ مَاءٍ﴾ (khalaqa kulla dabbatin min ma', "created every creature from water").

He means: from a drop of semen (nutfah). ﴿فَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ يَمْشِي عَلَى بَطْنِهِ﴾ ("Among them are those who walk on their bellies"), like snakes and what resembles them. It has been said: why is it said, ﴿Among them are those who walk on their bellies﴾, when walking does not occur on the belly? The answer: walking properly belongs to what has legs, by way of analogy; and when what has no legs mingles with what has legs, it is permissible. Similarly He said: ﴿وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ يَمْشِي عَلَى رِجْلَيْنِ﴾ ("And among them are those who walk on two legs"), like birds, ﴿وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ يَمْشِي عَلَى أَرْبَعٍ﴾ ("And among them are those who walk on four"), like cattle.

If someone says: how is it said, ﴿فَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ يَمْشِي﴾ (Among them are those who walk), when "man" (min) is used for people, and most of these kinds, or most of them, are other than people? It is said: this is a division of what is included in His saying, ﴿وَاللَّهُ خَلَقَ كُلَّ دَابَّةٍ﴾, and that included people and others; then He said, ﴿فمنهم﴾ ("among them"), because people, cattle and others are mingled together in that, so He referred to all of them with the pronoun used for the children of Adam, then specified them with "min", since He had referred to them with the pronoun used specifically for the children of Adam. ﴿يَخْلُقُ اللَّهُ مَا يَشَاءُ﴾ ("Allah creates what He wills") means: Allah brings into being whatever creation He wills. ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ﴾ ("Indeed, Allah is capable of all things") means: Allah is able to bring about that and create it, and to create other things He wills; He possesses a power that nothing He wishes is beyond.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 24, verse 46–48:

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿Indeed, We have sent down verses making things clear, and Allah guides whom He wills to a straight path﴾ [24:46].

He, the Exalted, says: Indeed We have sent down, O people, clear signs indicating the path of truth and the way of right guidance. ﴿And Allah guides whom He wills to a straight path﴾ means: And Allah guides whom He wills of His creatures by His success, so He guides him to the religion of Islam, which is the straight path, the direct way with no crookedness in it.

* *

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿And they say, "We believe in Allah and in the Messenger and we obey," then a faction of them turns away after that. And those are not believers﴾ [24:47], ﴿And when they are called to Allah and His Messenger to judge between them, at once a faction of them are turning away﴾ [24:48].

He, the Exalted, says: And the hypocrites say, "We affirm belief in Allah and in the Messenger, and we obey Allah and we obey the Messenger." ﴿Then a faction of them turns away﴾ means: Then every group of them turns its back on the Messenger of Allah ﴾ﷺ﴿ after they have said this statement, and calls for litigation before someone other than him, their opponent. ﴿And those are not believers﴾ means: And the speakers of this statement, meaning His saying, ﴿We believe in Allah and in the Messenger and we obey﴾, are not believers, because of their abandoning the judgment of the Messenger of Allah ﴾ﷺ﴿ and their turning away from him when they are called to him.

* *

And His saying: ﴿And when they are called to Allah and His Messenger﴾

It means: And when these hypocrites are called to the Book of Allah and to His Messenger ﴿to judge between them﴾ concerning what they dispute, by the judgment of Allah, ﴿at once a faction of them are turning away﴾ from accepting the truth and being content with the judgment of the Messenger of Allah ﴾ﷺ﴿.

* *

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿But if the right is theirs, they come to him in submission﴾ [24:49], ﴿Is there in their hearts a disease, or have they doubted, or do they fear that Allah and His Messenger will be unjust to them? Rather, it is they who are the wrongdoers﴾ [24:50].

He, the Exalted, says: And if the right were theirs, those who are called to Allah and His Messenger to judge between them, and they refuse and turn away from responding to that, against those who call them to Allah and His Messenger, they would come to the Messenger of Allah in submission. It means: submissive, compliant with his judgment, acknowledging it, obedient, not compelled. It is said of this: "So-and-so has submitted with respect to his right" when he acknowledges it willingly, not under compulsion, and yields to it and accepts it.

Mujahid, as is reported from him, said concerning this:

⁕ Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿they come to him in submission﴾: "Swiftly."

* *

And His saying: ﴿Is there in their hearts a disease﴾

He, the Exalted, says: Is there in the hearts of these who turn away when they are called to Allah and His Messenger to judge between them, doubt about the Messenger of Allah ﴾ﷺ﴿, that he is a messenger of Allah, so that they refuse to accept his judgment and to be content with it? ﴿Or do they fear that Allah and His Messenger will be unjust to them﴾ if they resort to the judgment of the Book of Allah and the judgment of His Messenger. He said: ﴿that Allah and His Messenger will be unjust to them﴾, and the meaning is: that the Messenger of Allah would be unjust to them. He began with Allah, the Exalted, out of glorification of Allah, as one says: "What Allah wills, then you will," meaning "what you will." Among what indicates that this is the meaning is His saying: ﴿And when they are called to Allah and His Messenger to judge between them﴾, where He singled out the Messenger for judgment and did not say "to judge between them both" (la-yahkuma).

* *

And His saying: ﴿Rather, it is they who are the wrongdoers﴾

It means: These who turn away from the judgment of Allah and the judgment of His Messenger did not fear, when they turned away from responding to what they were called to, that the Messenger of Allah would be unjust to them and rule unjustly against them. Rather, they are a people who wrong themselves by opposing the command of their Lord and by disobeying Allah in what He commanded them, namely being content with the judgment of the Messenger of Allah ﴾ﷺ﴿ in what they like and dislike, and submitting to it.

* *

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿And they say, "We believe in Allah and in the Messenger and we obey," then a faction of them turns away after that. And those are not believers﴾ [24:47], ﴿And when they are called to Allah and His Messenger to judge between them, at once a faction of them are turning away﴾ [24:48].

He, the Exalted, says: And the hypocrites say, "We affirm belief in Allah and in the Messenger, and we obey Allah and we obey the Messenger." ﴿Then a faction of them turns away﴾ means: Then every group of them turns its back on the Messenger of Allah ﴾ﷺ﴿ after they have said this statement, and calls for litigation before someone other than him, their opponent. ﴿And those are not believers﴾ means: And the speakers of this statement, meaning His saying, ﴿We believe in Allah and in the Messenger and we obey﴾, are not believers, because of their abandoning the judgment of the Messenger of Allah ﴾ﷺ﴿ and their turning away from him when they are called to him.

* *

And His saying: ﴿And when they are called to Allah and His Messenger﴾

It means: And when these hypocrites are called to the Book of Allah and to His Messenger ﴿to judge between them﴾ concerning what they dispute, by the judgment of Allah, ﴿at once a faction of them are turning away﴾ from accepting the truth and being content with the judgment of the Messenger of Allah ﴾ﷺ﴿.

* *

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿But if the right is theirs, they come to him in submission﴾ [24:49], ﴿Is there in their hearts a disease, or have they doubted, or do they fear that Allah and His Messenger will be unjust to them? Rather, it is they who are the wrongdoers﴾ [24:50].

He, the Exalted, says: And if the right were theirs, those who are called to Allah and His Messenger to judge between them, and they refuse and turn away from responding to that, against those who call them to Allah and His Messenger, they would come to the Messenger of Allah in submission. It means: submissive, compliant with his judgment, acknowledging it, obedient, not compelled. It is said of this: "So-and-so has submitted with respect to his right" when he acknowledges it willingly, not under compulsion, and yields to it and accepts it.

Mujahid, as is reported from him, said concerning this:

⁕ Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿they come to him in submission﴾: "Swiftly."

* *

And His saying: ﴿Is there in their hearts a disease﴾

He, the Exalted, says: Is there in the hearts of these who turn away when they are called to Allah and His Messenger to judge between them, doubt about the Messenger of Allah ﴾ﷺ﴿, that he is a messenger of Allah, so that they refuse to accept his judgment and to be content with it? ﴿Or do they fear that Allah and His Messenger will be unjust to them﴾ if they resort to the judgment of the Book of Allah and the judgment of His Messenger. He said: ﴿that Allah and His Messenger will be unjust to them﴾, and the meaning is: that the Messenger of Allah would be unjust to them. He began with Allah, the Exalted, out of glorification of Allah, as one says: "What Allah wills, then you will," meaning "what you will." Among what indicates that this is the meaning is His saying: ﴿And when they are called to Allah and His Messenger to judge between them﴾, where He singled out the Messenger for judgment and did not say "to judge between them both" (la-yahkuma).

* *

And His saying: ﴿Rather, it is they who are the wrongdoers﴾

It means: These who turn away from the judgment of Allah and the judgment of His Messenger did not fear, when they turned away from responding to what they were called to, that the Messenger of Allah would be unjust to them and rule unjustly against them. Rather, they are a people who wrong themselves by opposing the command of their Lord and by disobeying Allah in what He commanded them, namely being content with the judgment of the Messenger of Allah ﴾ﷺ﴿ in what they like and dislike, and submitting to it.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 24, verse 49–51:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿Only the saying of the believers, when they are called to Allah and His Messenger that He may judge between them, is that they say, "We hear and we obey." And those are the successful.﴾

Allah, the One mentioned, says: It is only befitting that the saying of the believers, when they are called to the judgment of Allah and the judgment of His Messenger, ﴿that He may judge between them﴾ and between their opponents, ﴿is that they say, "We hear"﴾ what has been said to us, ﴿"and we obey"﴾ the one who called us to that. The word ﴿kāna﴾ (was) in this place is not used to report a matter that has already occurred and been decided, but it is a rebuke from Allah, on account of whom this verse was revealed, and a disciplining by Him of others besides them.

* *

And His saying: ﴿And those are the successful﴾

Allah, the One mentioned, says: And those who, when they are called to Allah and His Messenger that He may judge between them and their opponents, ﴿"say, 'We hear and we obey'"﴾. The successful (al-mufliḥūn) means: they are the ones who attain their aims and achieve their needs by doing that, the ones who abide forever in the gardens of Allah.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 24, verse 52–53:

The interpretation of the words of the Exalted: ﴿And whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger, and fears Allah and keeps his duty to Him — those are the attainers [of success].﴾

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: ﴿And whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger﴾ in what He commands and forbids, and submits to their judgment in his favour or against him, and fears the consequence of disobeying Allah and is wary of it, and guards himself against the punishment of Allah by obeying Him in His commands and prohibitions. ﴿Then those﴾ — meaning: those who do that — ﴿they are the attainers﴾ of the pleasure of Allah with them on the Day of Resurrection, and of their safety from His punishment.

* *

The interpretation of the words of the Exalted: ﴿And they swore by Allah their most emphatic oaths that if you commanded them, they would surely go forth. Say, "Do not swear; [your] obedience is [already] known. Indeed, Allah is Acquainted with what you do."﴾

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: And these men who turn away from the judgment of Allah and the judgment of His Messenger, when they were called to it, swore by Allah ﴿their most emphatic oaths﴾ — meaning: their most vehement and strongest oaths — ﴿if you commanded them﴾, O Muhammad, to go forth to fight your enemy and the enemy of the believers, ﴿they would surely go forth. Say: "Do not swear"﴾ — do not take oaths — for this is ﴿[your] obedience [which is] known﴾ from you, in which there is lying.

As for what was said:

Al-Qasim narrated to us, who said: al-Husayn narrated to us, who said: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿Say, "Do not swear; [your] obedience is [already] known"﴾, he said: "Your obedience to me is known: that you are liars." ﴿Indeed, Allah is Acquainted with what you do﴾ — meaning: Allah is All-Knowing of what you do of your obedience to Allah and His Messenger, or your opposition to their command, or other of your affairs; nothing of that is hidden from Him, and He will recompense you for all of it.

As for what was said:

Al-Qasim narrated to us, who said: al-Husayn narrated to us, who said: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿Say, "Do not swear; [your] obedience is [already] known"﴾, he said: "Your obedience to me is known: that you are liars." ﴿Indeed, Allah is Acquainted with what you do﴾ — meaning: Allah is All-Knowing of what you do of your obedience to Allah and His Messenger, or your opposition to their command, or other of your affairs; nothing of that is hidden from Him, and He will recompense you for all of it.

The exegesis of His words, exalted is He: ﴿Say: Obey God and obey the Messenger. But if you turn away, then upon him is what he has been charged with, and upon you is what you have been charged with. And if you obey him, you will be guided. And upon the Messenger is only the clear conveyance.﴾ (24:54)

Says God, may His remembrance be exalted: ﴿Say﴾, O Muhammad, to these who swore by God with their most earnest oaths, ﴿"If you commanded them, they would surely go forth"﴾, and to others of your community: ﴿Obey God﴾, O people, in what He has commanded you and forbidden you, ﴿and obey the Messenger﴾, for his obedience is obedience to God. ﴿But if you turn away﴾, meaning: if you turn away and withdraw from what the Messenger of God ﷺ has commanded you or forbidden you, and refuse to submit to his judgment, for or against you, ﴿then upon him is what he has been charged with﴾, meaning: then upon him is only to do what he was commanded to do, which is to convey the message of God to you as he was charged to convey it. ﴿And upon you is what you have been charged with﴾, meaning: and upon you, O people, is to do what He has obligated and required of you, namely to follow His Messenger ﷺ and to submit to his obedience in what he commands and forbids you.

We have said that His words ﴿But if you turn away [tawallaw]﴾ mean "if you [plural] turn away [tatawallaw]", and it is in the jussive position, because it is addressed to those whom the Messenger of God was ordered to tell, ﴿Obey God and obey the Messenger﴾. What indicates that this is so is His words ﴿and upon you is what you have been charged with﴾. Had His words ﴿tawallaw﴾ been a past-tense verb in the form of a report about an absent party, it would have been in the position of His words ﴿upon him is what he has been charged with and upon you is what you have been charged with﴾.

* *

As for His words: ﴿And if you obey him, you will be guided﴾

Says God, may His remembrance be exalted: And if you obey the Messenger of God, O people, in what he commands you and forbids you, you will be guided, and you will hit upon the truth in your affairs. ﴿And upon the Messenger is only the clear conveyance﴾, meaning: it is not obligatory upon one whom God has sent to a people with a message, except that he convey his message to them in a clear conveyance that makes clear to them what God intends by it.

That is to say: upon Muhammad, O people, is only the performance of God's message to you, and upon you is obedience. If you obey him, it is for the benefit of your own souls that you will attain success [[as if it is the fa' in the response of the condition, meaning: then for your own benefit...]], and if you disobey him, it is to your own detriment that you will perish [[it would have been better to say: "if you disobey him, then to your own detriment you will perish"]].

The commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 24, verse 55:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Allah has promised those among you who believe and do righteous deeds that He will surely grant them succession upon the earth, just as He granted succession to those before them, and that He will surely establish for them their religion which He has approved for them, and that He will surely replace their fear with security, [so that] they worship Me, not associating anything with Me. And whoever disbelieves after that — then those are the defiantly disobedient.﴾ (24:55)

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: ﴿Allah has promised those among you who believe﴾ — O people — ﴿in Allah and His Messenger﴾ ﴿and do righteous deeds﴾ — that is, they obey Allah and His Messenger in what He has commanded them and forbidden them — ﴿He will surely grant them succession upon the earth﴾ — that is, Allah will surely make them inherit the lands of the polytheists among the Arabs and non-Arabs, making them its kings and rulers — ﴿just as He granted succession to those before them﴾ — that is, just as He did this for those before them, the Children of Israel, when He destroyed the tyrants in al-Sham and made them its kings and inhabitants — ﴿and He will surely establish for them their religion which He has approved for them﴾ — that is, He will surely firmly establish for them their religion, meaning their community (millah) which He has approved for them and commanded them with. It was also said: Allah promised those who believe, then He followed that with the answer to the oath in His saying ﴿He will surely grant them succession﴾, because "promise" is a statement in which "an" (that) may be used, and the answer to the oath is like the saying: "I promised you that I would honour you," and "I promised you, I will surely honour you."

The readers differed over the recitation of His saying ﴿kama istakhlafa﴾. The majority of readers recited it ﴿kama istakhlafa﴾ with a fatha on the ta' and the lam, meaning: as Allah made succeed those before them among the nations. ʿĀṣim recited it ﴿kamā ustukhlifa﴾ with a damma on the ta' and a kasra on the lam, according to the passive form where the agent is not named.

They also differed over the recitation of His saying ﴿wa-la-yubaddilannahum﴾. The majority of the readers of the regions, except ʿĀṣim, recited it ﴿wa-la-yubaddilannahum﴾ with a shaddah on the dal, meaning: and He will surely change their state from what it was, from fear to security. The Arabs say: "So-and-so has baddala" when his state has been changed, without anything else being put in its place, and likewise every thing changed from its state is, according to them, mubaddal with the shaddah. It may sometimes be said with the light form, but that is not the eloquent usage. As for when the thing replaced is substituted by something else, then it is with the light form: "abdaltuhu, fa-huwa mubdal." This is like their saying: "abdal hadha al-thawb" — that is, another garment was put in its place. It may also be said with the shaddah, but the eloquent speech is what I have described. ʿĀṣim used to recite it ﴿wa-la-yubdilannahum﴾ with the light form of the dal.

The correct recitation in this matter is the shaddah, with the meaning I described earlier, because of the consensus of the authoritative readers of the regions upon it, and because that is a change of the state of fear into security. I think ʿĀṣim went in the direction that security, since it is the opposite of fear, directed the meaning to mean that He removed the state of fear and brought the state of security, so he used the light form.

As evidence for what we have said, that the light form is only used when one thing is put in place of another, is the verse of Abu al-Najm:

"The removal of the amir for the amir who is replaced [mubdal]"

[The line is from the rajaz meter, by Abu al-Najm al-ʿIjli the rajaz poet (Lisan: b-d-l). Abu al-ʿAbbas (meaning Thaʿlab) said: its reality is that tabdil is changing a form into another form while the substance remains the same; and ibdal is removing one substance and establishing another substance. From it is the saying of Abu al-Najm: "the removal of the amir for the amir who is replaced." Do you not see that he removed one body and put in its place a different body?]

His saying ﴿yaʿbudūnanī﴾ means: they submit to Me in obedience and humble themselves to My command and prohibition. ﴿They do not associate anything with Me﴾ means: they do not associate in their worship of Me idols and images, nor anything other than them; rather they devote worship to Me, singling it out for Me above everything else worshipped besides Me. It is mentioned that this verse was revealed to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on account of some of his companions complaining to him at certain times when they were in great fear from the enemy, with the terror and fear they were in, and the harm and hardship they suffered because of that.

Mention of the narration concerning that:

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Abu Jaʿfar, from al-Rabiʿ, from Abu al-ʿAliyah, regarding His saying ﴿Allah has promised those among you who believe and do righteous deeds﴾ ... the verse, he said: The Prophet ﷺ remained for ten years in fear, calling to Allah secretly and openly. He said: Then he was commanded to emigrate to Medina. He said: He and his companions remained there in fear, rising in arms and retiring in arms. A man said: "Will there not come a day upon us when we are secure and lay down our arms?" The Prophet ﷺ said: "You will not wait except a little while until one of you sits in the great assembly, reclining in it, with no iron upon him." [In Fath al-Qadir of al-Shawkani (4:47): "no iron weapon among them" — perhaps another narration.] So Allah revealed this verse: ﴿Allah has promised those among you who believe﴾ ... to His saying ﴿and whoever disbelieves after that﴾. He said: He says: whoever disbelieves in this blessing ﴿then those are the defiantly disobedient﴾ — and it does not mean disbelief in Allah. He said: Allah made them victorious over the Arabian Peninsula, so they believed; then they became arrogant, so Allah changed what was among them, and they disbelieved in this blessing, so Allah brought upon them the fear that He had removed from them. Al-Qasim said: Abu ʿAli said: by their killing of ʿUthman ibn ʿAffan, may Allah be pleased with him.

The people of interpretation differed concerning the meaning of the disbelief mentioned by Allah in His saying ﴿whoever disbelieves after that﴾. Abu al-ʿAliyah said what we have mentioned from him: that it is disbelief in the blessing, not disbelief in Allah.

It is related from Hudhayfah concerning that:

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Habib ibn Abi Thabit, who said: I was sitting with Hudhayfah and ʿAbd Allah ibn Masʿud. Hudhayfah said: Hypocrisy has gone; hypocrisy was only during the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and what remains is only disbelief after faith. He said: ʿAbd Allah laughed and said: Why do you say that? He said: I know that. He said: ﴿Allah has promised those among you who believe and do righteous deeds, that He will surely grant them succession upon the earth﴾ ... until its end.

Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi ʿAdi narrated to us, saying: Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Abu al-Shaʿthaʾ, who said: I sat with Ibn Masʿud and Hudhayfah. Hudhayfah said: Hypocrisy has gone, so there is no hypocrisy; what remains is only disbelief after faith. ʿAbd Allah said: Do you know what you are saying? He said: Then he recited this verse: ﴿The statement of the believers was only﴾ ... until: ﴿then those are the defiantly disobedient.﴾ He said: ʿAbd Allah laughed. He said: I met Abu al-Shaʿthaʾ some days later and said: What did ʿAbd Allah laugh at? He said: I do not know; a man may laugh at something that pleases him, and may laugh at something that does not please him, so what did he laugh at? I do not know.

What Abu al-ʿAliyah said of the interpretation is more fitting to the meaning of the verse, because Allah promised to bestow favour upon this community with what He informed of in this verse, that He bestows it upon them; then He said after that: whoever disbelieves this blessing after that, ﴿then those are the defiantly disobedient.﴾

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿they worship Me, not associating anything with Me﴾: He said: That is the community of Muhammad ﷺ.

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Layth, from Mujahid, ﴿security, [so that] they worship Me, not associating anything with Me﴾: He said: they do not fear anyone other than Me.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 24, verses 56–57:

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿And establish prayer and give zakah and obey the Messenger that you may receive mercy (56). Do not think that those who disbelieve will cause failure [to Allah] within the earth, and their refuge is the Fire; and wretched is the destination (57)﴾

His saying, may He be remembered, means: ﴿And establish, O people, the prayer﴾ with its limits, so do not neglect it, ﴿and give zakah﴾ which Allah has enjoined upon you, to its recipients, and obey the Messenger of your Lord in what he commands you and forbids you, ﴿that you may receive mercy﴾, meaning: so that your Lord may have mercy on you and save you from His punishment. As for His saying, ﴿Do not think that those who disbelieve will cause failure [to Allah] within the earth﴾, He, may He be remembered, means: Do not think, O Muhammad, that those who disbelieve in Allah can escape Him within the earth when He wills to destroy them, ﴿and their refuge﴾ after their destruction ﴿is the Fire; and wretched is the destination﴾ to which they will return, that refuge.

Some of them used to recite "لا يَحْسَبَنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا" with the letter yāʾ (i.e., "lā yaḥsabanna" with the verb in the third person masculine), but this is a weak view according to the scholars of Arabic grammar (ahl al-ʿarabiyya); this is because "taḥsab" (to think/consider) requires two objects (manṣūbān). When it is read as "yaḥsabanna," it governs only one object. However, I think that the one who recited it with yāʾ thought that it governs "muʿjizīn" and that its second object is "fī al-arḍ," and this has no meaning, if that was what he intended.
