Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 24, verse 58:

The interpretation of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿O you who have believed, let those whom your right hands possess and those who have not yet reached puberty among you ask permission of you three times: before the dawn prayer, and when you put off your clothing at midday, and after the night prayer. Three times of privacy for you. There is no sin upon you or upon them beyond these, as they go about [attending] you, some of you to others. Thus does Allah make clear to you the verses, and Allah is Knowing and Wise.﴾ (24:58)

The scholars of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) differed concerning who is meant by His saying: ﴿those whom your right hands possess﴾. Some of them said: it refers to the men only, not the women, and they were forbidden to enter upon them at these three times without permission, these being the ones named in this verse.

Mention of those who said that:

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, who said: Hakkam narrated to us, from 'Anbasa, from Layth, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, regarding His saying: ﴿those whom your right hands possess﴾, he said: it applies to the males, not the females.

And others said: rather, it refers to both men and women.

Mention of those who said that:

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, who said: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, who said: Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu Husayn, from Abu 'Abd al-Rahman, regarding His saying: ﴿O you who have believed, let those whom your right hands possess ask permission of you﴾, he said: it applies to men and women; they should ask permission at all times, by night and by day.

The more correct of the two opinions in this matter, in my view, is the opinion of the one who said: it refers to both males and females; because Allah, by His saying ﴿those whom your right hands possess﴾, encompassed all of the possessions of our right hands, and did not single out any male or female, so it is general in application by the apparent sense of the revelation.

So the meaning of the statement is: O you who have believed in Allah and His Messenger, let your male and female slaves ask permission of you to enter upon you, so they should not enter upon you except with permission from you to them.

﴿and those of you who have not reached puberty﴾ means: and those among your free children who have not yet reached puberty (ihtilam) ﴿three times﴾, meaning: three times at three periods, from the hours of your night and day.

As:

Al-Qasim narrated to us, who said: al-Husayn narrated to us, who said: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿O you who have believed, let those whom your right hands possess ask permission of you﴾, he said: your owned slaves; ﴿and those of you who have not reached puberty﴾, he said: those among your free children who have not reached puberty.

Ibn Juraij said: 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah said to me: so this applies to every young boy and young girl, that they must ask permission, as He said: ﴿three times: before the dawn prayer, and when you put off your clothing at midday, and after the night prayer﴾. They said: it is the 'atama (night prayer). I said: So when they have put off their clothing after the 'atama, must they ask permission to enter upon them until morning? He said: Yes. I said to 'Ata': Is their asking permission only at the time when people put off their clothing? He said: No.

Al-Qasim narrated to us, who said: al-Husayn narrated to us, who said: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Salih ibn Kaysan, Ya'qub ibn 'Utba and Isma'il ibn Muhammad, who said: there is no requirement to ask permission for a man's servants to enter upon him except at the three times of privacy (al-'awrat al-thalath).

Ali narrated to me, who said: Abu Salih narrated to us, who said: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿those whom your right hands possess ask permission of you﴾, he said: when a man is alone with his family after the night prayer, no servant or child may enter upon him except with permission until he prays the morning prayer; and when he is alone with his family at the time of the noon prayer, it is likewise.

Yunus ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to me, who said: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: Qurra ibn 'Abd al-Rahman informed me, from Ibn Shihab, from Tha'laba, from Abu Malik al-Qurazi: that he asked 'Abd Allah ibn Suwayd al-Harithi, who was one of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), about permission at the three times of privacy. He said: when I have put off my clothing at midday, no servant who has reached puberty may enter upon me, nor any free child who has not reached puberty, except with permission.

Ya'qub narrated to me, who said: Ibn 'Ulayya narrated to us, from Ibn Juraij, who said: I heard 'Ata' say: Ibn 'Abbas said: three verses people have denied: the permission altogether; and He said: ﴿Indeed, the most noble of you in the sight of Allah is the most righteous of you﴾; and people said: the most noble of you is the one with the greatest house. And I have forgotten the third.

Ibn Abi al-Shawarib narrated to me, who said: Yazid ibn Zurayi' narrated to us, who said: Yunus narrated to us, from al-Hasan, regarding this verse ﴿those whom your right hands possess ask permission of you﴾, he said: al-Hasan used to say: if a man has his servant spend the night with him, that is his permission; and if he does not spend the night with him, the servant must ask permission at these times.

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, who said: Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us, who said: Sufyan narrated to us, who said: Musa ibn Abi 'A'isha narrated to me, from al-Sha'bi, regarding His saying: ﴿those whom your right hands possess ask permission of you﴾, he said: it has not been abrogated (lam tunsakh). I said: People do not act upon it. He said: Allah is the one sought for help!

He (the narrator) said: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, who said: Sufyan narrated to us, from Musa ibn Abi 'A'isha, from al-Sha'bi, and I asked him about this verse: ﴿those whom your right hands possess ask permission of you﴾. I said: Is it abrogated? He said: No, by Allah, it has not been abrogated. I said: People do not act upon it. He said: Allah is the one sought for help!

He said: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, who said: Abu 'Awana narrated to us, from Abu Bishr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: Some people say it was abrogated, but it is among the things people are negligent about.

He said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, who said: Shu'ba narrated to us, from Abu Bishr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr regarding this verse ﴿O you who have believed, let those whom your right hands possess ask permission of you﴾ ... to the end of the verse, he said: it is not acted upon today.

Yunus narrated to me, who said: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: Handhala narrated to us, that he heard al-Qasim ibn Muhammad being asked about permission, and he said: one asks permission at every time of privacy; then he is one who goes about [attending], meaning a man with his mother.

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, who said: 'Uthman ibn 'Umar narrated to us, who said: 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Abi Rawwad informed us, who said: a man of the people of al-Ta'if informed me, from Ghaylan ibn Shurahbil, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Let not the Bedouins overcome you regarding the name of your prayer." Allah said: ﴿and after the night prayer, three times of privacy for you﴾; and the 'atama is only the 'atama of the camels.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿three times of privacy for you﴾

The readers differed in reciting this. The majority of the readers of Medina and Basra recited it: ﴿thalathu 'awrat lakum﴾ with the word "thalath" in the nominative (raf'), as an informative statement about these periods that were mentioned, as though it were said: these three periods which We commanded you that none of those mentioned should enter upon you in them except with permission, are three times of privacy for you, because in them you put off your clothing and are alone with your families. And the majority of the readers of Kufa recited it: ﴿thalatha 'awrat﴾ with "thalath" in the accusative (nasb), as a reply to the first three. And the meaning of the statement according to them is: let those whom your right hands possess and those among you who have not reached puberty ask permission of you three times, three times of privacy for you.

The correct view on this matter is that they are two readings close in meaning, and scholars among the readers have recited each of them, so whichever reading the reciter uses, he is correct.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿There is no sin upon you or upon them beyond these, as they go about [attending] you﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: ﴿There is no sin upon you﴾, O company of householders and dwellers, ﴿nor upon them﴾, meaning: nor upon those whom your right hands possess, of men and women, and those among your young children who have not reached puberty, is there any blame or sin ﴿beyond these﴾, meaning beyond the three times of privacy. The ha' and nun in His saying ﴿beyond these (bacdahunna)﴾ refer back to "thalath" in His saying ﴿three times of privacy for you﴾. What is meant is that there is no blame or sin upon people if their adult slaves and their small children enter upon them without permission outside these three periods that He mentioned in His saying: ﴿before the dawn prayer, and when you put off your clothing at midday, and after the night prayer﴾.

The people of interpretation have said what is similar to what we have said.

Mention of those who said that:

Ali narrated to me, who said: Abu Salih narrated to us, who said: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Then He granted them leniency to enter without permission in the periods between them, meaning between the dawn prayer and noon, and after noon until the night prayer, that He permitted a man's servant and child to enter his house without permission. He said: this is His saying: ﴿There is no sin upon you or upon them beyond these﴾. As for one who has reached puberty, he may not enter upon a man and his family except with permission at all times.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿as they go about [attending] you﴾

The word "tawwafun" is raised (rafa') by an implied pronoun, which is "hum" (they). He says: these slaves and small children are those who go about [attending] you, O people, and by "those who go about" is meant that they enter and leave upon their masters and relatives in their homes morning and evening without permission, going about upon them, some of you to others, outside the three times in which He commanded that they not enter upon their masters and relatives except with permission. ﴿Thus does Allah make clear to you the verses﴾: He, may His praise be exalted, says: just as I have made clear to you, O people, the rulings of seeking permission in this verse, so Allah makes clear to you all His signs, proofs, and laws of His religion. ﴿And Allah is Knowing and Wise﴾: He says: Allah possesses knowledge of what benefits His servants, and is Wise in His management of them and in His other affairs.

The Interpretation of His words, the Exalted: ﴿And when the children among you reach puberty, let them ask permission as those before them asked permission. Thus does Allah make clear to you His verses, and Allah is Knowing and Wise.﴾ (24:59)

Says the Exalted: "When the young ones among your children and your relatives reach [the age of] puberty." By His words ﴿among you﴾ He means among your free ones. ﴿Puberty﴾ means ihtilam (wet dreams/sexual maturity), and they have reached ihtilam. ﴿Let them ask permission﴾ means: they must not enter upon you at any time except with permission, not during the three times of nakedness (awrat) nor at any other time.

* *

As for His words, ﴿as those before them asked permission﴾:

That is, as the adults among a man's children and his free relatives ask permission. Allah, the Exalted, singled out the children for mention in this verse, and informed His servants of the ruling on asking permission for them, without mentioning "those whom your right hands possess." The previous verse had already informed them of the ruling on free children and slaves, because the ruling regarding "those whom your right hands possess" in this matter is one ruling: their adults and their children are alike in that permission must be sought from them during the three times that Allah mentioned in the preceding verse.

Scholars of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said similarly to what we have said.

Those who said so:

Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, who said: As for one who has reached puberty, he must not enter upon a man and his family, meaning among the free boys, except with permission in every circumstance. This is His words: ﴿And when the children among you reach puberty, let them ask permission as those before them asked permission.﴾

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ata said regarding ﴿And when the children among you reach puberty, let them ask permission﴾: It is obligatory upon all people that they ask permission when they have had wet dreams, upon whoever is among the people.

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Yunus informed me, from Ibn Shihab, from Ibn al-Musayyab, who said: Should a man ask permission to enter upon his mother? He said: Indeed, ﴿And when the children among you reach puberty﴾ was revealed concerning that. ﴿Thus does Allah make clear to you His verses﴾ means: thus does Allah make clear to you His verses, His rulings and the laws of His religion, just as He has made clear to you the matter of these children regarding seeking permission after puberty. ﴿And Allah is Knowing and Wise﴾ means: Allah is Knowing of what sets right His creation and other things, Wise in His management of His creation.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 24, verse 60:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And as for women past child-bearing who have no hope of marriage, there is no blame upon them for putting aside their outer garments without displaying adornment; but to refrain is better for them. And Allah is Hearing and Knowing.﴾ (60)

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: And those women who have ceased to bear children due to old age, so they neither menstruate nor give birth, and the singular of them is qā'id (one who has ceased), ﴿who have no hope of marriage﴾ means: who have despaired of husbands and no longer desire marriage. ﴿there is no blame upon them for putting aside their outer garments﴾ means: there is no sin or fault upon them in putting aside their garments, meaning their jalabib (outer cloaks), which is the veil that is worn over the khimar (headscarf), and the wrap worn over the clothes. There is no fault upon them in putting these off in the presence of their unmarriageable male relatives (mahram) and non-mahram strangers, ﴿without displaying adornment﴾.

Ahl al-ta'wil (the scholars of interpretation) said the same as what we have said about this.

Mention of those who said that:

- Ali related to me, saying: Abu Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiya related to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿And as for women past child-bearing who have no hope of marriage﴾, that is the woman for whom there is no blame in sitting in her house in a shift and headscarf, and putting aside the jilbab, so long as she does not display herself in what Allah dislikes, and that is His saying: ﴿there is no blame upon them for putting aside their outer garments without displaying adornment﴾, then He said: ﴿but to refrain is better for them﴾.

- It was related to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd related to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say, regarding His saying: ﴿putting aside their outer garments﴾, meaning the jilbab, which is the veil, and this is for the elderly woman who has ceased to bear children, so it does not harm her not to wear a jilbab over the khimar. As for every free Muslim woman, when she reaches puberty, it is obligatory for her to draw the jilbab over the khimar. And Allah said in Surat al-Ahzab: ﴿They should draw their outer garments close around them. That is more suitable that they will be known and not be abused﴾. There were men among the hypocrites in Medina who, when a woman of poor appearance and dress passed by them, the hypocrites assumed she was a prostitute and one of their targets, so they would abuse believing women with lewd words, not distinguishing the free woman from the slave. So Allah revealed concerning that: ﴿O Prophet, tell your wives and your daughters and the women of the believers to draw their outer garments close around them. That is more suitable that they will be known and not be abused﴾, meaning: if their dress is good, the hypocrites will not desire them.

- al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, saying: Ibn Jurayj said, regarding His saying: ﴿And as for women past child-bearing﴾: those who have ceased to bear children and grown old. Ibn Jurayj said: Mujahid said: ﴿who have no hope of marriage﴾: they do not desire it. ﴿there is no blame upon them for putting aside their outer garments﴾: their jalabib.

- Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: (And as for women past child-bearing who have no hope of marriage, there is no blame upon them for putting aside their outer garments without displaying adornment): he said: the putting aside of the khimar. He said: the one who has no hope of marriage is one who has reached the state in which she has no need of men and men have no need of her. When they reach that state, they put aside the khimar, without displaying adornment. Then He said: ﴿but to refrain is better for them﴾. My father used to say all of this.

- Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Yahya and Abd al-Rahman related to us, both saying: Sufyan related to us, from Alqama ibn Martad, from Dharr, from Abu Wa'il, from Abdullah, regarding His saying: ﴿there is no blame upon them for putting aside their outer garments﴾: he said: the jilbab or the rida', Sufyan was uncertain.

- He said: Abd al-Rahman related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from al-A'mash, from Malik ibn al-Harith, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Yazid, from Abdullah: ﴿there is no blame upon them for putting aside their outer garments﴾: he said: the rida'.

- Yahya ibn Ibrahim al-Mas'udi related to me, saying: My father related to us, from his father, from his grandfather, from al-A'mash, from Malik ibn al-Harith, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Yazid, who said: Abdullah said concerning this verse ﴿there is no blame upon them for putting aside their outer garments﴾: he said: it is the mulhafa (wrap).

- Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far related to us, saying: Shu'ba related to us, from al-Hakam, who said: I heard Abu Wa'il say: I heard Abdullah say concerning this verse ﴿there is no blame upon them for putting aside their outer garments﴾: he said: the jilbab.

- Yahya ibn Sa'id related to us, from Shu'ba, who said: al-Hakam informed me, from Abu Wa'il, from Abdullah, the like of it.

- al-Hasan ibn Yahya related to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, from al-Thawri, from al-A'mash, from Malik ibn al-Harith, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Yazid, from Ibn Mas'ud, regarding His saying: ﴿that they put aside their outer garments without displaying adornment﴾: he said: it is the rida'.

al-Hasan said: Abd al-Razzaq said: al-Thawri said: Abu Husayn and Salim al-Aftas informed me, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: it is the rida'.

- Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Jarir related to us, from Mughira, from al-Sha'bi, ﴿that they put aside their outer garments without displaying adornment﴾: he said: the jilbab is put aside by a woman who has become incapable (of child-bearing) and has not been married. Al-Sha'bi said: Ubayy ibn Ka'b used to recite "an yada'na min thiyabihinna" (that they put aside some of their garments).

- Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim related to me, saying: Ibn Ulayya related to us, saying: I said to Ibn Abi Najih, regarding His saying: ﴿there is no blame upon them for putting aside their outer garments without displaying adornment﴾: he said: the jilbab. Ya'qub said: Abu Yunus said: I said to him: from Mujahid? He said: Yes, in the house and the chamber.

- Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿there is no blame upon them for putting aside their outer garments﴾: he said: their jalabib.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿without displaying adornment﴾

It means: there is no blame upon them in putting aside their outer garments, provided they do not intend by putting these aside to reveal to men the adornment they have. Tabarruj (displaying oneself) is for a woman to show from her beauty what she should conceal.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿but to refrain is better for them﴾

It means: if they refrain from putting aside their jalabib and outer garments, then wearing them is better for them than putting them aside.

Ahl al-ta'wil said the same as what we have said about this.

Mention of those who said that:

- Muhammad ibn Amr related to us, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿but to refrain is better for them﴾: he said: that they wear their jalabib.

- Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Jarir related to us, from Mughira, from al-Sha'bi, regarding His saying: ﴿but to refrain is better for them﴾: he said: abandoning that, meaning: abandoning the putting aside of garments.

- Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿but to refrain is better for them﴾: al-isti'faf is wearing the khimar on her head. My father used to say all of this. ﴿And Allah is Hearing﴾ of what you utter with your tongues, ﴿Knowing﴾ of what your breasts conceal. So fear Him, that you do not utter with your tongues what He has forbidden you to utter, or conceal in your breasts what He has disliked for you, for you would thereby deserve punishment from Him.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 24, verse 61 (part 1 of 2):

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿There is no blame upon the blind, nor is there blame upon the lame, nor is there blame upon the sick, nor upon yourselves, that you eat from your own houses or the houses of your fathers or the houses of your mothers or the houses of your brothers or the houses of your sisters or the houses of your paternal uncles or the houses of your paternal aunts or the houses of your maternal uncles or the houses of your maternal aunts, or that of which you hold the keys, or [the house of] your friend. There is no blame upon you for eating together or separately. But when you enter houses, greet one another with a greeting from Allah, blessed and good. Thus does Allah make clear to you the verses, that you might understand.﴾ (24:61)

Abu Ja'far said: The people of interpretation differed concerning the circumstance in which this verse was revealed. Some of them said: this verse was revealed as a concession to the Muslims to eat with the blind, the lame, the sick and those afflicted with disabilities from their food, because they had refrained from eating with them from their food, out of fear that they might have brought with their eating with them from their food something of what Allah had forbidden them by His saying: ﴿O you who have believed, do not consume one another's wealth unjustly, except in the case of trade by mutual consent among you﴾.

Mention of those who said that:

◆ ʿAlī narrated to me, saying: ʿAbd Allah narrated to me, saying: Muʿawiyah narrated to me, from ʿAlī, from Ibn ʿAbbas: ﴿There is no blame upon you that you eat﴾ from your houses... up to His saying: ﴿or in groups﴾. That was when Allah revealed ﴿O you who have believed, do not consume one another's wealth unjustly﴾. The Muslims said: Allah has forbidden us to consume one another's wealth unjustly, and food is among the best of wealth, so it is not lawful for any of us to eat at the house of another. So the people refrained from that. Then Allah revealed after that ﴿There is no blame upon the blind﴾... up to His saying: ﴿or that of which you hold the keys﴾.

◆ It was related to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muʿadh say: ʿUbayd informed us, who said: I heard al-Ḍaḥḥāk say concerning His saying: ﴿There is no blame upon the blind﴾... the verse: The people of Medina, before the Prophet (ﷺ) was sent, would not mix with the blind or the sick in their food. Some of them said: it was only aversion and disgust that was in them. Others said: The sick person does not get his fill of food, as the healthy person does, and the lame who is hindered cannot compete for food, and the blind cannot see good food. So Allah revealed ﴿There is no blame upon you﴾ — blame in eating with the sick, the blind and the lame. The meaning of the speech according to the interpretation of these people is: there is no blame upon you, O people, regarding the blind, that you eat from him and with him, nor regarding the lame, nor regarding the sick, nor upon yourselves that you eat from your houses. So they directed the meaning of "ʿalā" (upon) in this place to the meaning of "fī" (in).

Others said: Rather, this verse was revealed as a concession to the people of disability to eat from the houses of those whom Allah named in this verse, because some men from among the companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), when there was not in their houses anything to feed them, would take them to the houses of their fathers and mothers, or some of those whom Allah named in this verse. The people of disability would fear to eat that food, because he had fed them from what was not his property.

Mention of those who said that:

◆ Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿĀṣim narrated to us, saying: ʿĪsā narrated to us; and al-Ḥārith narrated to me, saying: al-Ḥasan narrated to us, saying: Warqāʾ narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najīḥ, from Mujāhid: ﴿nor upon yourselves that you eat from your houses or the houses of your fathers﴾, he said: There were men who were disabled. Ibn ʿAmr said in his narration: blind and lame. Al-Ḥārith said: blind, lame, people of need, whom men would bring along to their houses. If they did not find food, they would take them to the houses of their fathers, and whoever else they named of houses. The ones who brought them disliked that, so Allah revealed in that regard ﴿There is no blame upon you﴾ and made the food lawful for them wherever they found it.

◆ al-Ḥasan narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Ibn Abi Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, who said: A man would take the blind, the sick and the lame to the house of his father, or to the house of his brother, or his paternal uncle, or his maternal uncle, or his maternal aunt. The disabled would feel uneasy about that, saying: They take us to the houses of others. So this verse was revealed as a concession for them.

◆ al-Qāsim narrated to us, saying: al-Ḥusayn narrated to us, saying: Ḥajjāj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujāhid, similar to the report of Ibn ʿAmr, from Abu ʿĀṣim.

Others said: Rather, it was revealed as a concession to the people of disability whom Allah described in this verse, to eat from the houses of those whom he left in charge of their houses among the warriors.

Mention of those who said that:

◆ al-Ḥasan ibn Yaḥyā narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, who said: I said to al-Zuhrī, concerning His saying: ﴿There is no blame upon the blind﴾: What is the matter with the blind being mentioned here, and the lame and the sick? He said: ʿUbayd Allah ibn ʿAbd Allah informed me that the Muslims, when they went out to fight, would leave their disabled behind, and they would hand over to them the keys of their doors, saying: We have made it lawful for you to eat of what is in our houses. They would feel uneasy about that, saying: We do not enter them while they are absent. So this verse was revealed as a concession for them.

Others said: Rather, by His saying: ﴿There is no blame upon the blind, nor is there blame upon the lame, nor is there blame upon the sick﴾ He meant staying behind from jihad in the way of Allah. They said: His saying: ﴿nor upon yourselves that you eat from your houses﴾ is a statement separate from what precedes it.

Mention of those who said that:

◆ Yūnus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying: ﴿There is no blame upon the blind, nor is there blame upon the lame, nor is there blame upon the sick﴾, he said: This is about jihad in the way of Allah. And concerning His saying: ﴿nor upon yourselves that you eat from your houses﴾ ... up to His saying: ﴿or your friend﴾, he said: This is something that has ended. It was in the beginning, when they had no doors, and the curtains were hanging down, so a man might enter a house with no one in it, and might find food while he was hungry, so Allah permitted him to eat it. He said: That has passed today; houses today have their people in them, and when they go out they lock them, so that has gone.

Others said: Rather, this verse was revealed as a concession to the Muslims who used to avoid eating with the people of disability when they wished to eat.

Mention of those who said that:

◆ Ibn Bashshār narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, saying: Sufyān narrated to us, from Qays ibn Muslim, from Miqsam, concerning His saying: ﴿There is no blame upon the blind﴾, he said: They used to avoid eating with the blind and the lame, so this was revealed: ﴿There is no blame upon you for eating together or separately﴾.

They also differed concerning the meaning of His saying: ﴿or that of which you hold the keys﴾. Some of them said: By this is meant a man's agent and steward, that there is no harm upon him to eat from the produce of his estate, and the like.

Mention of those who said that:

◆ ʿAlī narrated to me, saying: Abu Ṣāliḥ narrated to us, saying: Muʿawiyah narrated to us, from ʿAlī, from Ibn ʿAbbas, concerning His saying: ﴿or that of which you hold the keys﴾, he said: This is the man who appoints a man over his estate, so Allah permitted him to eat of that food and the dates and to drink the milk.

Others said: Rather, by this is meant a man's own dwelling, that there is no harm upon him to eat.

Mention of those who said that:

◆ It was related to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muʿadh say: ʿUbayd informed us, who said: I heard al-Ḍaḥḥāk say concerning His saying: ﴿or that of which you hold the keys﴾, he means: the house of one of them, for he owns it, and the slaves among them are of what they own.

◆ al-Ḥasan narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Qatādah, concerning His saying: ﴿or that of which you hold the keys﴾: of what you love, O son of Adam.

◆ al-Qāsim narrated to us, saying: al-Ḥusayn narrated to us, saying: Ḥajjāj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujāhid, who said: ﴿or that of which you hold the keys﴾: treasuries for themselves, not for others.

The most likely of the sayings we have mentioned concerning the interpretation of His saying: ﴿There is no blame upon the blind, nor is there blame upon the lame﴾ ... up to His saying: ﴿or your friend﴾ is the saying we have mentioned from al-Zuhrī, from ʿUbayd Allah ibn ʿAbd Allah. That is because the most evident meaning of His saying: ﴿There is no blame upon the blind, nor is there blame upon the lame﴾ is that there is no blame upon those named in this verse for eating from the houses of those whom Allah mentioned in it, according to what He permitted them to eat from them. Since that is the most evident of its meanings, directing its meaning to the more common and well-known of its meanings is more fitting than directing it to the more unusual ones. Since that is so, the interpretation that contradicts it, the saying of one who said its meaning is: there is no blame on the blind and the lame, is more correct. Likewise, the most common interpretation of His saying: ﴿nor upon yourselves that you eat from your houses﴾ is that it means: nor upon you, O people, then He gathered these and the disabled he mentioned before in the address, saying: that you eat from the houses of yourselves. Thus the Arabs do when they combine a report about an absent party with the addressed party: they give precedence to the addressed, saying: "You and your brother stood up," and "You and Zayd sat down," and they do not say: "You and your brother sat." Likewise His saying: ﴿nor upon yourselves﴾, and the report about the blind, the lame and the sick gave precedence to the addressed, so He said: "that you eat," and did not say: "that they eat."

If someone says: This eating from their houses we already know; it was lawful for them since it was their property, or it was also lawful for them to eat from the property of others. It is said to him: The matter is not as you suppose. Rather, it is as we have mentioned from ʿUbayd Allah ibn ʿAbd Allah: that when they were absent on their campaigns and the disabled among them stayed behind, the warrior would hand over the key of his dwelling to the one of them who had stayed behind, and he was permitted to eat from the food left in his house. The ones who stayed behind would fear eating from it while its owner was absent, so Allah informed them that there is no blame upon him in eating from it, and permitted them to eat it. Since that is so, it becomes clear that there is no meaning in the saying of one who said: this verse was revealed only because the one who brought the guest disliked eating the food of someone other than the one who brought him, for if that were as the one who said it claimed, it would be said: "There is no blame upon you that you eat from the food of someone other than the one who hosted you, or from the food of the fathers of the one who invited you," and it would not say: "that you eat from your houses or the houses of your fathers." Likewise there is no basis for the saying of one who said: the meaning is: there is no blame on the blind in staying behind from jihad in the way of Allah, because His saying: ﴿that you eat﴾ is the predicate of "laysa" (there is not), and "that" is in the accusative position as its predicate, so it is connected to "laysa." Thus it is known from this that the meaning of the speech is: there is no blame upon the blind that he eat from his house, not what those we have mentioned said, that there is no blame upon him for staying behind from jihad. Since the matter is as we have described, it becomes clear that the meaning of the speech is: there is no constraint upon the blind, nor upon the lame, nor upon the sick, nor upon you, O people, that you eat from your own houses, or from the houses of your fathers, or the houses of your mothers, or the houses of your brothers, or the houses of your sisters, or the houses of your paternal uncles, or the houses of your paternal aunts, or the houses of your maternal uncles, or the houses of your maternal aunts, or from the houses whose keys you hold, or from the house of your friend, when they permit you to do so, in their absence or their presence. The word "al-mafātīḥ" (the keys) means: treasuries. Its singular is "miftaḥ" when it is meant as the verbal noun; and when it refers to the keys with which something is opened, it is "miftaḥ" and "mafātīḥ," and here, according to the interpretation we have chosen, it is the plural of "miftaḥ," the instrument by which one opens.

Qatādah used to interpret His saying: ﴿or [the house of] your friend﴾ as follows:

◆ al-Ḥasan ibn Yaḥyā narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, from Maʿmar, from Qatādah, concerning ﴿or [the house of] your friend﴾: if you eat from the house of your friend without his command, there is no harm in that. Maʿmar said: I said to Qatādah: "Or may I not drink from this jar?" He said: "You are a friend to me."

As for His saying: ﴿There is no blame upon you for eating together or separately﴾, the people of interpretation differed in its interpretation. Some of them said: a wealthy man among the people would fear to eat with a poor man, so they were granted permission to eat with them.

Mention of those who said that:

◆ al-Qāsim narrated to us, saying: al-Ḥusayn narrated to us, saying: Ḥajjāj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from ʿAṭāʾ al-Khurasānī, from Ibn ʿAbbas, concerning His saying: ﴿that you eat together or separately﴾, he said: A wealthy man would enter upon a poor man from among his relatives and friends, and invite him to his food to eat with him, and he would say: "By Allah, I am reluctant to eat with you, and the 'junh' (reluctance) is the blame, while I am wealthy and you are poor." So they were commanded to eat together or separately.

Others said: Rather, by this is meant a tribe of the tribes of the Arabs, who would not eat alone, and would only eat with others, so Allah permitted them that whoever wished among them could eat alone, and whoever wished among them could eat with others.

Mention of those who said that:

◆ ʿAlī narrated to me, saying: Abu Ṣāliḥ narrated to us, saying: Muʿawiyah narrated to me, from ʿAlī, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: They would be too proud and reluctant to eat alone, until someone else was with them, so Allah permitted them, saying: ﴿There is no blame upon you for eating together or separately﴾.

◆ al-Qāsim narrated to us, saying: al-Ḥusayn narrated to us, saying: Ḥajjāj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: The Banū Kinānah, a man among them would be too shy to eat alone, until this verse was revealed.

◆ It was related to me from al-Ḥusayn, who said: I heard Abu Muʿadh say: ʿUbayd informed us, who said: I heard al-Ḍaḥḥāk say: They would not eat except together, and would not eat dispersed, and this was a religious custom among them. So Allah revealed: There is no blame upon you in eating with the sick and the blind, and there is no blame upon you that you eat together or separately.

◆ Yūnus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said concerning His saying: ﴿There is no blame upon you for eating together or separately﴾: Among the Arabs there were those who never ate together, and among them were those who would only eat together. So Allah said that.

◆ al-Ḥasan narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, saying: Maʿmar informed us, from Qatādah, who said: This verse was revealed concerning a tribe of the Arabs, where a man would not eat his food alone; he would carry it for part of a day until he found someone to eat with him. He said: I think he mentioned that they were from Kinānah.

Others said: Rather, by this is meant a people who would not eat when a guest came to them except with their guest, so they were granted permission to eat as they wished.

Mention of those who said that:

◆ Abu al-Sāʾib narrated to me, saying: Ḥafṣ narrated to us, from ʿImrān ibn Sulaymān, from Abu Ṣāliḥ and ʿIkrimah, who both said: The Anṣār, when a guest came to them, would not eat until the guest ate with them, so they were granted permission. Allah said: ﴿There is no blame upon you for eating together or separately﴾.

The most correct of these sayings, in our view, is that it should be said: Allah removed the constraint from the Muslims, that they may eat all together if they wish, or separately, dispersed, if they desire. It is possible that this was revealed because of those who feared that the wealthy would eat with the poor, and it is possible that it was revealed because of the people who are mentioned as not eating except in groups, and because of other things. There is no report about any of these that settles the matter, and there is no indication in the apparent sense of the revelation about the reality of any of it. The correct course is to accept what the apparent sense of the revelation indicates, and to withhold judgment on what has no proof of its authenticity.

* *

And His saying: ﴿But when you enter houses, greet one another with a greeting from Allah﴾

The people of interpretation differed concerning this. Some of them said: its meaning is: When you enter, O people, your own houses, greet your family and dependents.

Mention of those who said that:

◆ al-Ḥasan narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, saying: Maʿmar informed us, from al-Zuhrī and Qatādah, concerning His saying: ﴿greet one another﴾, they both said: [it means] your house; when you enter it, say: "Peace be upon you."

⁕ Al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, regarding ﴿When you enter houses, greet one another﴾: "Greet your family." Ibn Jurayj said: Ata' ibn Abi Rabah was asked: "Is it obligatory for a man, when he enters upon his family, to greet them?" He said: "Yes." Amr ibn Dinar also said this, and they recited: ﴿When you enter houses, greet one another with a greeting from God, blessed and good﴾. Ata' ibn Abi Rabah said: "That was more than once."

Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Abu al-Zubayr informed me that he heard Jabir ibn Abd Allah say: "When you enter upon your family, greet them, ﴿a greeting from God, blessed and good﴾." He said: "I have never seen him [Jabir] regard it as anything other than obligatory."

Ibn Jurayj said: Ziyad informed me, from Ibn Tawus, that he used to say: "When one of you enters his house, let him greet [those in it]."

Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: I said to Ata': "When I leave, is it obligatory for me to greet them? Or [is it only that] God said: ﴿When you enter houses, greet [one another]﴾?" He said: "I do not know it to be obligatory, nor has anyone's obligation been transmitted from anyone. But it is more beloved to me, and I do not abandon it except when I forget."

Ibn Jurayj said: Amr ibn Dinar said, "No." [Ibn Jurayj continued:] I said to Ata': "What if there is no one in the house?" He said: "Greet: say, 'Peace be upon the Prophet and the mercy of God and His blessings; peace be upon us and upon the righteous servants of God; peace be upon the people of the house and the mercy of God.'" I said to him: "Your saying this, when you enter a house in which there is no one, is it from someone whose transmission you cite?" He said: "I heard it, and it was not transmitted to me from anyone."

Ibn Jurayj said: Ata' al-Khurasani informed me, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "Peace be upon us from our Lord." Amr ibn Dinar said: "Peace be upon us and upon the righteous servants of God."

⁕ Ahmad ibn Abd al-Rahim related to us, saying: Amr ibn Abi Salamah related to us, saying: Sadaqah related to us, from Zuhayr, from Ibn Jurayj, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir ibn Abd Allah, who said: "When you enter upon your family, greet them, a greeting from God, blessed and good." He said: "I have never seen him [Jabir] regard it as anything other than obligatory."

⁕ Muhammad ibn Abbad al-Razi related to us, saying: Hajjaj ibn Muhammad al-A'war related to us, saying: Ibn Jurayj said to me: Abu al-Zubayr informed me that he heard Jabir ibn Abd Allah say, and [the narrator] mentioned something similar.

⁕ I was told, from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding the words of God: ﴿When you enter houses, greet one another﴾: "He means: greet your families when you enter your houses, and greet others, so greet them when you enter their houses."

Others said: Rather, its meaning is: when you enter mosques, greet their people.

Mention of those who said that:

⁕ Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman related to us, saying: Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak related to us, from Ma'mar, from Amr ibn Dinar, from Ibn Abbas, regarding ﴿When you enter houses, greet one another﴾: "They are the mosques. [One] says: 'Peace be upon us and upon the righteous servants of God.'"

⁕ [Ibn Bashshar] said: Abd al-Rahman related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from al-A'mash, from Ibrahim, regarding His words: ﴿When you enter houses, greet one another﴾: "When you enter the mosque, say: 'Peace be upon the Messenger of God.' When you enter a house in which there is no one, say: 'Peace be upon us and upon the righteous servants of God.' And when you enter your own house, say: 'Peace be upon you.'"

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: when you enter houses of the Muslims in which there are people from among you, then let some of you greet others.

Mention of those who said that:

⁕ Al-Hasan related to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Hasan, regarding His words: ﴿greet one another﴾, meaning: let some of you greet others, like His words: ﴿and do not kill yourselves﴾.

⁕ Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words: ﴿When you enter houses, greet one another﴾: "When the one who greets enters, he is greeted, like His words: ﴿and do not kill yourselves﴾. It means only: do not kill your Muslim brother."

* *

And His words: ﴿Then you are these who kill yourselves﴾.

He said: "One of you kills another. [This refers to] Qurayzah and al-Nadir."

Others said: its meaning is: when you enter houses in which there is no one, then greet yourselves.

Mention of those who said that:

⁕ Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim related to me, saying: Hushaym related to us, saying: Husayn informed us, from Abu Malik, who said: "When you enter a house in which there is no one, say: 'Peace be upon us and upon the righteous servants of God.' And when you enter a house in which there are people from among the Muslims and others, say the same."

⁕ Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from Abu Sinan, from Mahan, who said: "When you enter houses, greet yourselves": "Say: 'Peace be upon us from our Lord.'"

⁕ Ibn al-Muthanna related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far related to us, saying: Shu'bah informed us, from Mansur. Shu'bah said: "I asked him about this verse: ﴿When you enter houses, greet yourselves with a greeting from God﴾," and he said: "Ibrahim said: 'When you enter a house in which there is no one, say: "Peace be upon us and upon the righteous servants of God."'"

⁕ Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Amr ibn al-Harith informed me, from Bukayr ibn al-Ashajj, from Nafi', that Abd Allah, when he entered a house in which there was no one, would say: "Peace be upon us and upon the righteous servants of God."

⁕ Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Jarir related to us, saying: Mansur related to us, from Ibrahim, regarding ﴿When you enter houses, greet yourselves﴾: "When you enter a house in which there are Jews, say: 'Peace be upon you.' And if there is no one in it, say: 'Peace be upon us and upon the righteous servants of God.'"

The most correct of these opinions, in my view, is the opinion of the one who said that its meaning is: when you enter houses of the Muslims, then some of you should greet others.

We said this is more correct because God, may His praise be exalted, said: ﴿When you enter houses﴾, and He did not specify one house over another. And He said: ﴿greet yourselves﴾, meaning: some of you upon others. So it is known, since He did not specify some houses over others, that it refers to all of them, both mosques and non-mosques. The meaning of His words: ﴿greet yourselves﴾ is similar to His words: ﴿and do not kill yourselves﴾.

* *

And His words: ﴿a greeting from God﴾.

The accusative of "greeting" [tahiyyah] is in the sense of: "greet your selves with a greeting from God, the greeting [being] peace." It is as if He said: "let some of you greet others with a greeting from God." Some of the Arabic grammarians said that it is in the accusative in the sense of: "He has commanded you to do it, [as] a greeting from Him." God, may His praise be exalted, described this blessed, good greeting by the great reward and mighty recompense that it contains.

* *

And His words: ﴿Thus God makes clear to you the signs﴾.

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Thus God makes clear to you the features of your religion and explains them to you, just as He has made clear to you in this verse what is permitted to you in it, and taught you the way of entering upon those whom you enter upon. ﴿So that you may understand﴾: that is, that you may comprehend from God His command, His prohibition, and His discipline.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 24, verse 62:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Only the believers are those who have believed in Allah and His Messenger, and when they are with him on a matter of common concern, they do not leave until they have asked his permission. Indeed, those who ask your permission are the ones who believe in Allah and His Messenger. So when they ask your permission for some of their affairs, give permission to whom you will of them and ask forgiveness for them from Allah. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾

Says God, may His remembrance be exalted: The believers in the true sense of faith are only those who truly affirm Allah and His Messenger. ﴿And when they are with him﴾ means: when they are with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), ﴿on a matter of common concern﴾ means: on a matter that gathers all of them together, such as a war that has arrived, or a prayer for which they have assembled, or a consultation about a matter that has arisen. ﴿They do not leave﴾ means: they do not depart from what they have gathered for, ﴿until they have asked his permission﴾ of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said what we have said on this matter.

Those who said that:

• Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, who said: my father narrated to me, who said: my paternal uncle narrated to me, who said: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿Only the believers are those who have believed in Allah and His Messenger, and when they are with him on a matter of common concern, they do not leave until they have asked his permission﴾, he said: this is when the matter is an act of obedience to Allah.

• al-Qasim narrated to us, who said: al-Husayn narrated to us, who said: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ibn 'Abbas said regarding His saying: ﴿and when they are with him on a matter of common concern﴾: it is a general matter of the obedience of Allah.

• Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, who said: Muhammad ibn Bakr narrated to us, who said: Ibn Jurayj informed us, who said: a man asked Makhul al-Shami while I was listening, and Makhul was sitting with 'Ata', about the saying of Allah in this verse: ﴿and when they are with him on a matter of common concern, they do not leave until they have asked his permission﴾. Makhul said: it is on the day of Friday, in a battle line, and in every matter of common concern. He has commanded that no one leave on the day of Friday until he has asked the imam's permission, and likewise in every gathering. Do you not see that He says: ﴿and when they are with him on a matter of common concern﴾?

• Ya'qub narrated to me, who said: Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to me, who said: Hisham ibn Hassan informed us, from al-Hasan, who said: when a man had a need while the imam was delivering the khutbah, he would stand and pinch his nose, and the imam would signal to him to leave. A man wished to return to his family, so he stood up to Harim ibn Hayyan while he was giving the khutbah, and pinched his nose, and Harim signaled to him to go. He left for his family and stayed with them, then came back. Harim said to him: Where were you? He said: With my family. He said: Did you leave with permission? He said: Yes, I stood up to you while you were delivering the khutbah and pinched my nose, and you signaled to me to go, so I went. He said: Have you taken this as a pretext? Or words to that effect, then he said: O Allah, delay the men of evil until the time of evil.

• al-Hasan narrated to me, who said: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, who said: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, regarding His saying: ﴿and when they are with him on a matter of common concern﴾, he said: it is Friday, when they are with him, they do not leave until they have asked his permission.

• Yunus narrated to me, who said: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿Only the believers are those who have believed in Allah and His Messenger, and when they are with him on a matter of common concern, they do not leave until they have asked his permission﴾, he said: the common matter is when they are with him in a body for war or on Friday. He said: Friday is among the common matters; no one should leave when the imam has sat on the pulpit on Friday except with the permission of the ruler, if he is where he can be seen or reached. He does not leave without permission. If he is where he cannot be seen, cannot be reached, and cannot be contacted, then Allah is more deserving of excuse.

* *

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who ask your permission are the ones who believe in Allah and His Messenger﴾

Says God, may His remembrance be exalted: Indeed, those who do not depart from you, O Muhammad, when they are with you on a common matter, except with your permission to them, out of obedience to Allah and to you, and affirmation of what I have brought them from Me, those are the ones who truly affirm Allah and His Messenger, not those who oppose the command of Allah and the command of His Messenger, who leaves you without permission from you, after you have made it clear to him that he must not leave you except with your permission.

* *

And His saying: ﴿So when they ask your permission for some of their affairs, give permission to whom you will of them﴾

Says God, may His remembrance be exalted: So when those who do not leave you except with your permission in these situations ask you, O Muhammad, for some of their affairs, meaning some of their needs that arise for them, then grant permission to whomever you will of them to depart from you to attend to them. ﴿And ask forgiveness for them﴾ means: and pray to Allah for them, that He graciously pardon them for the consequences of what lies between Him and them. ﴿Indeed, Allah is Forgiving﴾ of the sins of His repentant servants, ﴿Merciful﴾ toward them, not punishing them for them after they have repented of them.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 24, verse 63:

The explanation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Do not make the summoning of the Messenger among yourselves like your summoning of one another. Allah already knows those among you who slip away, sheltering behind others. So let those who oppose his command beware lest a trial afflict them or a painful punishment strike them.﴾

Allah, the Exalted, says to the companions of His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): ﴿Do not make, O believers, the summoning of the Messenger among yourselves like your summoning of one another.﴾

The people of ta'wil (interpretation) differed regarding the meaning of this. Some of them said: Through this verse Allah forbade the believers to bring upon themselves the Prophet's supplication against them. He said to them: Beware of his supplication against you by doing what displeases him, so that he calls down [a curse] upon you and you are destroyed. So do not make his supplication like the supplication of other people, for his supplication is binding.

Those who said this:

⁕ Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, he said: my father related to me, he said: my paternal uncle related to me, he said: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿Do not make the summoning of the Messenger among yourselves like your summoning of one another﴾: The Messenger's summoning against you is binding, so beware of it.

Others said: Rather, that is a prohibition from Allah against calling upon the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) with harshness and rudeness, and a command to them to call upon him with gentleness and humility.

Those who said this:

⁕ Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, he said: Abu 'Asim related to us, he said: 'Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, he said: al-Hasan related to us, he said: Warqa' related to us; all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿like your summoning of one another﴾, he said: He commanded them to call: "O Messenger of Allah," in gentleness and humility, and not to say: "O Muhammad," in brusqueness.

⁕ al-Qasim related to us, he said: al-Husayn related to us, he said: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, the like of it: ﴿Do not make the summoning of the Messenger among yourselves like your summoning of one another﴾, he said: He commanded them to call him: "O Messenger of Allah," in gentleness and humility.

⁕ al-Hasan related to us, he said: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, he said: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿Do not make the summoning of the Messenger among yourselves like your summoning of one another﴾, he said: He commanded them to magnify and honour him.

The more correct of the two interpretations in my view is the one stated by Ibn 'Abbas. This is because what precedes His saying: ﴿Do not make the summoning of the Messenger among yourselves like your summoning of one another﴾ is a prohibition from Allah to the believers against turning away from him in a matter that gathers them all, which He dislikes; and what follows it is a threat to those who depart from him without his permission. Thus, what lies between them, that it be a warning to them lest His displeasure compel him to supplicate against them, is more fitting than that it be a command to them regarding something not previously mentioned, namely honouring and revering him by word and supplication.

* *

His saying: ﴿Allah already knows those among you who slip away, sheltering behind others﴾

The Exalted says: Indeed you, O those who depart from your Prophet without his permission, seeking concealment and secrecy from him, even if the matter of those among you who do this is hidden from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), Allah knows it and it is not hidden from Him. So let those among you who do this beware, those who oppose the command of Allah concerning departing from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) without his permission, lest a trial from Allah afflict them, or a painful punishment strike them, so that a seal is set upon their hearts and they disbelieve in Allah.

The people of ta'wil have said the like of what we have said.

Those who said this:

⁕ Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: al-Hakam ibn Bashir related to us, he said: 'Amr ibn Qays related to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, regarding the saying of Allah: ﴿Allah already knows those among you who slip away, sheltering behind others﴾, he said: They used to hide behind one another and then get up [and leave]. So He said: ﴿So let those who oppose his command beware lest a trial afflict them﴾, he said: a seal is set upon his heart, so he cannot be certain he will not openly declare disbelief with his tongue and then have his neck struck.

⁕ Ibn al-Qasim related to us, he said: al-Husayn related to us, he said: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿Allah already knows those among you who slip away, sheltering behind others﴾, he said: Opposing.

⁕ Yunus related to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿Allah already knows those among you who slip away, sheltering behind others﴾: These are the hypocrites who return without the permission of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). He said: al-liwadh (sheltering): one who turns aside from him, evades and goes off without the permission of the Prophet (ﷺ). ﴿So let those who oppose his command beware﴾: those who do this, lest a trial afflict them, or a painful punishment strike them. The trial here is disbelief. And al-liwad is a verbal noun: "I sheltered behind so-and-so" (lawadtu bi-fulan mulawadhatan wa liwadhan), which is why the waw appears; had it been a verbal noun of "laadhtu," it would have been said liyadh, just as one says qumtu qiyaman, and when one says qawamtuka, one says qiwaman tawilan. Al-liwad is that the people shelter behind one another, this one concealing himself behind that one and that one behind this one, as al-Dahhak said.

* *

His saying: ﴿or a painful punishment strike them﴾

He says: or a painful punishment from Allah strike them in the immediate life of this world, for their conduct and for opposing the command of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

* *

His saying: ﴿So let those who oppose his command beware﴾

"'An" has been inserted, because the meaning of the speech is: Let those who shelter away from his command and turn their backs on him, deflecting, beware.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 24, verse 64:

The explanation of the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Surely to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth. He already knows the state you are in; and the Day they are returned to Him, He will inform them of what they did. And Allah is Knowing of all things.﴾

His saying, may His remembrance be exalted: "Surely to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth" means: Allah possesses the dominion of all the heavens and the earth. He means: a slave should not oppose his master's command and disobey him, thereby deserving His punishment. He means: likewise, O people, it is not fitting for you to oppose your Lord, who is your Master. So obey Him, carry out His command, and do not turn away from His Messenger when you are with him on a matter requiring gathering, except with his permission.

* *

His saying: ﴿He already knows the state you are in﴾

means: [He knows] your obedience to Him in what He has commanded and forbidden you,

as related:

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying: ﴿He already knows the state you are in﴾: "This conduct of yours too," ﴿and the Day they are returned to Him﴾ means: and the Day those who oppose His command return to Allah, ﴿He will inform them﴾ means: He will then inform them, ﴿of what they did﴾ in the world, then He will recompense them for what they committed there of opposing their Lord, ﴿And Allah is Knowing of all things﴾ means: and Allah has knowledge of everything you have done, you and others, and other matters. Nothing is hidden from Him; rather He encompasses all of that, and He will fully repay every worker among you the reward of his deed on the Day you are returned to Him.

End of the tafsir of Surat an-Nur.
